News.title: Female SWAT cop ‘bullied by male officers after she refused to let them hold her down and bite her bum’ in sick ritual
News.content:
VILE 'INITIATION' Female SWAT cop ‘bullied by male officers after she refused to let them hold her down and bite her bum’ in sick ritual







Next

A FEMALE SWAT cop has alleged male colleagues bullied her after she refused to let them hold her down and bite her bum as part of a sick “hazing” ritual.

Officer Perla Dominguez, a 14-year veteran of the San Antonio Police Department (SAPD), has claimed that fellow cops verbally and sexually harassed her for years.



Dominguez was the city’s only SWAT cop, but asked to be reassigned after alleging she was ostracised for reporting sustained “sex-based harassment and hazing” since her 2018 appointment.

A lawsuit, filed against the City of San Antonio, refers to a hazing ritual where new SWAT cops are held down and bitten on the rear by other officers.



Dominguez claims she was tormented by colleagues after refusing to engage in the “sexually degrading” ritual.

New recruits are also allegedly expected to get a lightning bolt tattoo, which she described as “offensive”, according to the lawsuit.

The document also claims that Captain Jamie Trevino said the tattoo was about “loyalty and trust” at a 2022 leadership event.

Dominguez felt that the comment was personally aimed at her.

Soon after, the lawsuit says she requested “a temporary assignment at the SAPD Training Academy” in February 2022, which was granted.

Dominguez is now looking to recoup “lost compensation” associated with the transfer and the alleged discrimination she suffered.



She has also asked the court to be reinstated with the SWAT team, receiving back pay and compensatory damages.

According to the lawsuit, Dominguez was forced to change in the women’s bathroom at the SWAT facility.

She also claimed that, as there had been no female officers before, her male colleagues continued to use the toilet even after she asked them to stop.



The lawsuit alleges that in February 2019, a male officer walked in while Dominguez was partially undressed.

She was later given a key to lock the bathroom, but Officer Greg Cummins threatened: “The moment you leave that door open, I’m going to take a s*** in your sink”, according to the suit.

In 2020, Captain Miles Earwood allegedly asked her to put it somewhere so male colleagues could access it.

A year later, officers Salvador Hernandez and Marshall Davis allegedly repeatedly pressured her to take part in the hazing ritual, with Hernandez claiming her refusal made colleagues question her loyalty.

Later that year, after Dominguez revealed she and her wife were expecting twin boys, she allegedly found a used condom in her locker.



An investigation was launched, but she claims the city never identified or disciplined whoever left it there.

The lawsuit also says that colleagues made derogatory comments about a nonbinary public figure, which Dominguez reported without action being taken.

In 2022, Sergeant Frank Gutierrez allegedly gave her a negative performance review, suggesting she seek psychological services, before changing the assessment after she refused to sign it.

A spokesperson for the City of San Antonio Attorney’s Office told the Daily Mail: “The City and SAPD take claims of harassment seriously.

“Now that suit has been filed, we will be defending against these claims.”

News.title: Dad, 32, dies after being shot in car while trying to break up road rage row – as murder probe launched & man charged
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'MURDER' PROBE Dad, 32, dies after being shot in car while trying to break up road rage row – as murder probe launched & man charged







Next

A DAD-OF-THREE has died after being shot in a car while trying to break up a road rage row as police launch a murder probe.

Police were alerted to reports of gunfire in Woolwich, London, on Thursday, October 22.

Firearms cops and specialist detectives were scrambled to the scene, the Met Police said.

Responding officers found Terry Dearsley, 32, in a car parked near the Royal Artillery Barracks suffering from a gunshot wound.





He was rushed to an East London hospital to receive treatment for life-threatening injuries.

Tragically, Terry was pronounced dead on Wednesday, November 4, despite the best efforts of medics.

His family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

A man was charged with attempted murder and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life in connection with the tragedy.



Paul Rosser-Davies, 48, of Brewhouse Road, Greenwich, was charged on Sunday, November 1.

He appeared at Wimbledon Magistrates’ Court on Monday and was remanded into custody.

Rosser-Davies will next appear at the Old Bailey on Monday, November 30.

The Met Police has now confirmed that a murder investigation into the incident has been opened.



The barracks in Woolwich is home to some 700 soldiers and housed the Royal Artillery from 1776 to 2007.

A Metropolitan Police spokesman previously said: “Police were called at 8.09pm on Thursday, October 22 to reports of a shooting in Frances Street, Woolwich.

“Officers attended and found a man, aged in his 30s, suffering from gunshot wounds.

“They performed first aid until the London Ambulance Service and London’s Air Ambulance arrived.

“The man was taken to an East London hospital with life-threatening injuries.



“Firearms officers and specialist crime detectives attended the scene.”

News.title: Albanian drug dealer to remain in UK after judge rules offending ‘not serious enough to be classed as foreign criminal’
News.content:
MIGRANT ROW Albanian drug dealer to remain in UK after judge rules offending ‘not serious enough to be classed as foreign criminal’







Next

AN ALBANIAN drug dealer will dodge deportation after the judge ruled that his crime was not serious enough to deem him a foreign criminal.

Ndue Paluca was jailed in October 2021 for growing cannabis and supplying it to an organised drug gang.

But Paluca – who entered the UK “without leave” – will now have his case reviewed after the court found his offence did not cause “serious harm”.

Legally speaking, this is what is needed to qualify as a foreign criminal if you are serving less than a year in prison.





The judge found that as a “farmer” cultivating the plants, the Albanian national – who arrived in the UK in 2012 – played a marginal role.

Three years later, he made an asylum claim as he was in a relationship and had two young daughters.

However, he then withdrew the claim because it was made in bad faith, as he was facing threats of deportation at the time.

As a “gardener” growing cannabis for an organised crime group, he was loosely involved in various sketchy schemes, including car deals, opening bank accounts and obtaining leases.

After being jailed in 2021, the Home Office found he could not be automatically deported because his sentence was less than a year.

They sought instead to remove him on the grounds of causing “serious harm” – an argument which has now been dismissed.

Paluca appealed against deportation on human rights grounds which was overridden by a first-tier tribunal judge.

The judge ruled that just because Paluca’s role had been marginal, this did not mean his work hadn’t caused serious harm to others.



The judge said: “Obtaining properties to grow drugs and all of the other illegal activity undertaken to set up the conspiracy on the specific facts of the case and as referenced in the sentencing remarks caused harm. For the above reasons I therefore find that [Paluca] is a foreign criminal.”

However, this initial ruling has now been dismissed by upper tribunal judge, Sarah Grey.

She noted that no drugs had been supplied to the public and there was no evidence Paluca had been involved in other nefarious aspects of the drug dealing.

The case is now being re-considered by the first-tier tribunal.

News.title: Moment supercar smashes into barrier at 280mph during test – as driver miraculously walks away without serious injuries
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a £2.2million electric supercar slams into a barrier at high speed with the driver miraculously walking from the wreckage unharmed.

Dramatic footage captures the near-supersonic motor skidding across the track at 280mph with thick smoke pouring from its rear before it violently careens into a safety barrier.



Video recently surfaced of the horror crash at an undisclosed Chinese track, just days after the supercar became the first to hit 310mph during a test in the UAE.

Chunks of debris flew across the road as the Yangwang U9 Xtreme spun uncontrollably.



Crews desperately rushed to the stricken driver.

Despite the car’s body taking severe damage, the driver remained unharmed and, according to reports, he even managed to get out of the car on his own.

BYD hasn’t said when the incident occurred or what caused its supercar to lose control.

Photos from after the crash show the extent of the damage to both the front and rear bodywork.



The force of the impact tore the rear axle and all four wheels completely off the car, while the entire bonnet was obliterated.

The Yangwang U9 Xtreme is the most extreme version of BYD’s U9 electric supercar.

In September 2025, it reached 308.3 mph, officially making it the world’s fastest car.

BYD is a major Chinese multinational high-tech car manufacturing company headquartered in Shenzhen, China.

Their cars have witnessed significant growth in Britain, reporting a 113 per cent sales increase in the first half of 2026 and currently selling through 144 car dealers.



In June, the brand said it wanted to become the world’s biggest automaker in the next five years, already overtaking Tesla last year.

The dramatic crash comes following another hypercar smash, this time in Spain.

In September a £3.3million Bugatti Tourbillon was smashed into by a £20,000 Volkswagen Polo during a test drive.

The ultra-rare hypercar prototype was being put through its paces in the scorching Sierra Nevada when a normal traffic stop turned into an expensive nightmare.

Footage shared online shows the luxury Bugatti travelling behind a white Kia XCeed while a grey Volkswagen follows closely behind.



The Kia suddenly stops at a red light in front of planned roadworks, forcing the Bugatti driver to also slam on the brakes.

The £3.3million motor’s stopping speed and reaction times are among the best in the world – even on a winding mountain road.

Unfortunately, the Polo had no such luck as it couldn’t come to a screeching halt quick enough.

The hatchback’s tyres can be heard squealing before the car crashes into the sculpted rear of the Bugatti.

The heavy impact appeared to have left the Tourbillon with mostly cosmetic damage, but with such a supercar even the slightest repair job could trigger a staggering bill.

News.title: Critical incident declared after shots fired at car near Asda as armed cops swoop and boy, 16, & man, 41, arrested
News.content:
Next

TWO people have been arrested after a shooting left bullet holes in a car and debris strewn across the roads, as cops declare a critical incident.

The altercation is believed to have taken place shortly after 5pm in Morriston, Wales, near the Asda on Clase Road.



Cops said one of the vehicles had sustained damage “consistent with a firearms discharge”.

A 41-year-old man from Llansamlet has been arrested on suspicion of possessing a firearm with intent to endanger life.



A 16-year-old boy has also been arrested on suspicion of affray.

One image shows cops inspecting an Audi with a smashed driver side window and a rear number plate falling off.





Another photo shows a vehicle stranded on the verge with damage to its bumper and steelwork.

Onlookers reported a police helicopter circling overhead, as well as a large number of officers on patrol in the area.

A cordon is currently in place on the dual carriageway, near Castle Bingo, with roads closed off on Upper Forest Way.

South Wales Police have declared it a critical incident and said a criminal investigation is now underway.

The public are being urged not to approach the area.



A local fireworks display – organised by Morriston Town AFC – was cancelled at the request of the police.

Small fires burning in the vicinity have also been reported, with fire crew confirming they had extinguished a car blaze.

It is unknown whether these are linked to the shooting.

Chief Superintendent Stephen Jones said: “A policing presence will be visible in the area whilst this investigation is ongoing.

“It is important that people avoid the area so we can effectively deal with this incident and return the area to normality.



“We are aware of footage circulating online in relation to this incident.”

They are urging anyone with information to come forward.

News.title: Venezuelan migrant arrested near White House after ‘multiple weapons found in stolen car’ in Trump ‘assassination bid’
News.content:
'ASSASSIN' ARREST Venezuelan migrant arrested near White House after ‘multiple weapons found in stolen car’ in Trump ‘assassination bid’







Next

AN ARMED man has been arrested near the White House after he allegedly said threatened to kill Donald Trump.

Secret Service agents found the Venezuelan migrant in a stolen car packed with firearms, according to the Department of Homeland Security.



Officers said they approached the suspect after spotting him “acting suspicious in his car while parked on Constitution Avenue in Washington.”

He reportedly told police that he heard voices in his head telling him to come to the capital and kill Trump, the DHS said.



Officers seized three firearms, including an AR-15-style rifle and two handguns, along with dozens of rounds of ammunition.

The US president has had to deal with numerous high-profile attempts and threats on his life in the last three years.

Read more US news MILLER TIME Trump's post-midterms purge begins as he axes chief of staff Susie Wiles

An open-air presidential campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania on July 13, 2024, was the closest a would-be assassin has come.

The perpetrator, 20-year-old Thomas Crooks, fired eight rounds at Trump from an AR-15-style rifle, grazing him on the ear and fatally wounding 50-year-old attendee Corey Comperatore.

Crooks was promptly killed by Secret Service counter-snipers, while other agents shielded Trump on the ground.

Three months later, 58-year-old Ryan Routh lay in wait for 12 hours at the Trump International Golf Club in Florida, while the then-presidential candidate was playing a round.



A Secret Service agent spotted the barrel of a rifle sticking out of some bushes and shot at Routh, who fled before being detained within 45 minutes.

In April this year, a heavily-armed Cole Thomas Allen allegedly attempted to storm the White House Correspondents’ Dinner at the Washington Hilton.

The 31-year-old teacher was detained outside the banquet hall after firing shots at officers stationed at the security checkpoint.

A manifesto later revealed Allen’s deep-seated hatred of Trump and his administration, as well as a disturbed psyche – with the suspected gunman referring to himself as the “Friendly Federal Assassin”.

The most recent high-profile attempt attempt came in May, when Nasire Best opened fire at a White House checkpoint before being shot dead by the Secret Service.



The 21-year-old had claimed to be Jesus Christ in a previous White House arrest.

Professor Javed Ali, a former official in the FBI and Department of Homeland Security, previously told The Sun: “I don’t think we’ve seen anything like that, that kind of frequency in US history before.”

News.title: WW2 hero, 105, to be given replica RAF uniform by proud family as they fly to US to ‘take Remembrance Sunday to him’
News.content:
SURPRISE VISIT WW2 hero, 105, to be given replica RAF uniform by proud family as they fly to US to ‘take Remembrance Sunday to him’







Next



A 105-YEAR-OLD World War II hero will be presented with his original RAF uniform at a Remembrance Sunday ceremony dedicated to him in his US care home.

Ronnie Holdsworth served with 158 squadron of Bomber Command as a tailgunner – completing an extraordinary 32 operational missions.



Tailgunners – exposed to enemy fighter planes seated at the back of the aircraft – survived just three missions on average.

But brave Ronnie defied the odds in his Handley Halifax Bomber – and is still alive to tell the tale.



Proud Bradford-born Ronnie is living in a retirement home in California and wanted to return to the UK to pay his respects on Remembrance Sunday.

But unable to fly on doctors’ orders, his family are instead heading out to surprise him – armed with an array of poignant gifts.





“We’re taking Remembrance Sunday to Ronnie,” said his great niece, Angie Burns.

“He’s returned to the UK over the years for reunions with 158 Squadron but he can no longer travel. Ronnie’s retirement home in Bakersfield is organising a special event for him – and we’ve mobilised to make it special.”

To mark the occasion, International Bomber Command has obtained an RAF uniform for Ronnie to wear and produced a replica of his logbook, detailing all of his 32 daredevil ops.

One of eight children, Ronnie volunteered for the RAF in 1940. He was stationed at RAF Lissett with 158 squadron, converting from twin-engined Vickers Wellingtons to the Handley Page Halifax, a four-engined heavy bomber.

His plane was called the “Zed Zombie” with the first six flights over France and Holland. The final 26 were over Germany.



Recalling the 1,000-bomber raid on the German city of Duisburg, he said: “I’ve never seen so much fire in all my life. I remember thinking ‘It must be terrible down there’. But we did what we had to do.”

He said of sitting in the trail turret: “As a rear gunner, I was the only one who flew backwards.

“My job was to safeguard the aircraft from rear attacks. I was in that cramped, freezing turret for six or seven hours. Most of the time I’m looking around and fidgeting – I can’t sit still or I’d fall asleep. That happened to quite a few.

“I couldn’t talk to anyone, if you started chirping on the intercom the pilot would tell you to shut up.”

The crew came close to crashing near Duisberg on Christmas Eve, 1944 and made an emergency landing at RAF Carnaby near Bridlington. “We all piled out and saw the damage – a hole in the side of the plane,” Ronnie recalled.



His last mission was near Berlin on January 16, 1945. He said: “It felt like a load had been taken off, but one crew member we knew well didn’t make it that night.”

A framed photo of the WWII aircraft which Ronnie flew on signed by the Air Chief Marshal Harv Smyth will also be presented to him.

Handing over the precious memento will be 83-year-old Air Commodore Roderick Aeneas Chisholm, who shot down at least five enemy aircraft in WWII and is responsible for nine aerial victories.



Married father of two sons, Ronnie emigrated to America in 1958. He attended 158 Squadron reunions when physically possible and wrote to his WWII crew until they died.

Angie told The Sun: “Ronnie’s war service is incredible. He is one of the world’s last surviving WWII airmen.

“He’s very humble and still has a sense of humour. His crew nicknamed him Chico because he was from a musical family and liked to dance. He still does a dance class every day.

“People say ‘there aren’t any war veterans left now’ – well we want the world to know that Ronnie is still here. A Bradford man who flew backwards, in a cramped, isolating, freezing turret, for hours, on dangerous raids, day and night.

“All his old crew are gone. It’s more important than ever to remember what he did. Remembrance Day really matters to him. He just doesn’t want to be forgotten.



“He’s still bright as a button. And likely to be dancing again after the service.”

She has been accompanied by her hubby and daughter Freya, a stewardess for British Airways, who made the tip possible.

Ronnie’s RAF uniform and framed WWII portrait was poignantly laid out on BA Captain Jon Brown’s seat before a BA flight left Heathrow on Thursday.



The veteran pilot will also be attending Saturday’s ceremony to salute Ronnie.

Sean Doyle, British Airways Chairman and CEO BA also signed a ‘Certificate of Gratitude’ for Ronald Holdsworth.

The framed document stated: “With profound gratitude for your extraordinary service to our country during the Second World War.

“As a Royal Air Force Rear Gunner with No158 Squadron, you completed 32 operational missions aboard Halifax bombers. Your courage, resilience and devotion to duty remain an enduring inspiration to us all.”

Mr Doyle told us: “Ronnie’s story is a remarkable reminder of the generation we owe so much to.



“Everyone at British Airways was proud to play a small part in bringing Ronnie’s family together in California for Remembrance Day, ensuring he could mark this important occasion surrounded by loved ones.

“Ronnie’s extraordinary wartime service continues to inspire us all, and everyone at British Airways joins me in thanking him for his service.”

And proud BA crew member Freya Burns, 25, said: “Uncle Ronnie served in the RAF, and his experiences are something we are all incredibly proud of. I am particularly grateful for the opportunity to spend time with him and celebrate his life.”

BA boss Sean Doyle also signed a ‘Certificate of Gratitude’ for Ronald Holdsworth.

“As a Royal Air Force Rear Gunner with No158 Squadron, you completed 32 operational missions aboard Halifax bombers. Your courage, resilience and devotion to duty remain an enduring inspiration to us all.”

News.title: Vance and Rubio’s battle to succeed Trump is a fight not just for America but the entire West
News.content:
Next

AND they’re off.

In a spectacular display of disloyalty, Donald Trump’s Midterms bin fire was not yet smouldering before JD Vance fired the starting gun on the race to replace President No47.



Breaking cover to blame his own administration’s war in Iran for Tuesday’s nationwide thwacking, the Vice President moved quickly to prop up his position as front-runner.

His long statement, not cleared by the White House, can be summarised thus: “I told you so, so please don’t tar me with the same brush.”



But it landed badly. Not least because Trump plucked Vance from relative obscurity, promoting the junior senator from Ohio to a heartbeat from the Presidency.

And the famously territorial POTUS has allowed JD to spend the past two years openly flirting with the MAGA base that Trump built from scratch.

But the VP is gambling that, following Tuesday’s results, the Don’s endorsement might not be as valuable as it once was.

Instead, he is going directly for that base, who are livid at Trump for abandoning his America First campaign pledge of no new wars.

Fascinatingly, Trump’s own son Don Jr publicly stated he agreed with “every word” of Vance’s backstabbing broadside — it’s long been rumoured he eyes a spot on the Vance ticket.

How well he comes through months of show trials into the family affairs remains to be seen, but Democrats are vowing to use their newfound Congressional powers to haul the son and heir before the court of public opinion.



Meanwhile, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who many on the right are desperate to see run, took a different tack: Quickly shutting down DC rumours that he was on the verge of quitting, instead pledging loyalty.

But one thing changed. Having previously stated he would never run against his “friend” JD, the door crept open to a tilt for the top job.

“I literally will not talk about 2028 any more,” he told the New York Times. “I just won’t.”



He’s being coy but keeping his options open at least . . .

Trump has riffed endlessly that this pair would be unstoppable if they teamed up to replace him, and even hinted there shouldn’t be a race but a backroom stitch-up.

But he was quick to reverse that after Tuesday, telling reporters there would “probably” have to be a primary contest. He’s spot on, as that fight would be about far more than personalities.

A civil war has been raging in the Republican Party and MAGA movement all year.

It’s mostly been hyper-online, with influencers trading blows from mysteriously well-funded platforms. Podcasters have spent months accusing each other of being in the pay of some foreign state or other as they bicker about Israel.



Fringe figures of the Right, such as Gen Z racebaiter Nick Fuentes, have sounded more like the darker, nastier side of the Left as they blame the Middle East’s only democracy for all of America’s woes.

America’s first Muslim senator Abdul El-Sayed, a Democrat, refused to criticise his supporters’ advert that blamed high prices on support for Israel.

In the ad, a couple stand in a supermarket unable to buy eggs saying, “we have to set that $7 aside for killing Palestinians.”

It was straight out of the Goebbels playbook, but the sentiment is no different to what El-Sayed uttered himself on the stump. But it is not very different from big-hitters on the hard-right fringe, a perfect example that the political spectrum is not a straight line but a horseshoe.



Traditional conservatives and friends of Israel have been fighting a losing battle to distance the Republicans from this fringe, and the war in Iran has sent the row thermonuclear.

Last December I watched JD Vance try to ride both sides of this schism, with a carefully crafted speech to 30,000 MAGA activists in Phoenix, Arizona.

Their gathering had been marked by well-known voices on the right like Steve Bannon, Tucker Carlson and Ben Shapiro trading public blows about Israel’s influence in US politics.

Yet the VP arrived declaring: “I didn’t bring a list of conservatives to denounce or to de-platform.”

Foghorn not whistle



Now, as the race to replace Trump ignited the morning after the Midterms, Vance has picked a side.

Five little words in his 600-word mission statement — “change our relationship to Israel” — said it all.

It wasn’t so much a dog whistle but a foghorn. And it puts him on a collision course with his pal Rubio.

In Jerusalem not long ago, the Secretary of State said: “If there were more countries like Israel, the world would be a safer and better place.”

And it speaks to a much broader ideological debate that the Republicans need to have in the open.



In simple terms, Vance is a far more hardline isolationist than Trump ever was, despite the campaign rhetoric.

Rubio, on the other hand, still sees America as a global leader in a dangerous age.

Just take his speech in Athens last month where, standing in the cradle of democracy, he warned we are at an “inflection point”, urging the West to rediscover its ambition, courage and pride through leadership.

This primary is shaping up to be a battle for the heart and soul of not just the Republican Party, or America but the entire Western alliance.

If Rubio truly believes what he says about stemming our decline, it is impossible for him to sit this one out.



DONALD TRUMP says the Republican “bench is deep” when it comes to a 2028 Presidential candidate – but on the Democrat side their own range of picks just got significantly larger.

California Governor Gavin Newsom is looking increasingly like yesterday’s man with the many failures in his home state a growing ball and chain on his candidacy.

Enter Jon Ossoff, the pretty-boy Senator of Georgia, who was re-elected in the swing state with a thumping margin.

At just 39, he would be the youngest President since Theodore Roosevelt in 1901 – but JD Vance is only a couple of years older.

It’s probably too soon for new Texas Senator James Talarico, despite some of the breathier commentary on the left this week.



And after hard-left candidates were able to win in unlikely parts of the US, it’s all but inevitable that lot will weigh in behind the fiery-eyed Queen of Woke Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

AOC, as we must call her, is hardly hosing down the suggestion, telling supporters this week “she will continue to do what she has always done; look for ways to do the most good for the most people”.

What we call in the trade: Not a denial.

News.title: Dad of Learjet co-pilot had final wish before 'soulmate' daughter died in horrific crash
News.content:
Dad of Learjet co-pilot had final wish before 'soulmate' daughter died in horrific crash

"I wanted to be by her side. Inside the plane, to help, to be by her. I had to be next to her," the father of the co-pilot, who was killed in the horrific plane crash, said.

View 5 Images Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras and her father Allan (Image: Allan Filgueiras via AP)

The father of the co-pilot killed in the horrific plane crash in Florida this week has said he wanted to be with her in her last moments. She bravely tried to save the aircraft as it plummeted to the ground and crashed near Donald Trump's Mar-a-Largo estate on Sunday.

‌



‌



Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras was just 20-years-old. Now her father, Allan, has paid tribute to her in an emotional press conference. He shared his final wish to be with his daughter in the final moments of her life.

‌



"I wanted to be by her side. Inside the plane, to help, to be by her. I had to be next to her," he said, according to the New York Post .

‌



View 5 Images Nathalia bravely tried to save the aircraft (Image: Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras)

Allan fought back tears as remembered his daughter. He said she was his "soulmate". The heartbroken father said Nathalia showed him "what it is to be a hero".

Nathalia was among nine people who died when after Learjet 60 nosedived into a street in Palm Beach, Florida during a flight from Texas to the Bahamas. Pilot-in-command Jeff Gregory, who appeared to be praying in his final moments, also passed away.

‌



Multi-millionaire tech founder Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp and their two young children Emma and Charlie, were also on board the doomed flight. They were accompanied by friends Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr as well as nanny Anita Maria Apellido Cetina.

View 5 Images Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp and their two children (Image: Family Handout)

‌



The plane was heading east at 35,000 feet when pilots reported turbulence, icing and precipitation. The pilot declared an emergency as the aircraft began losing altitude at an alarming rate.

The youngster made a desperate mayday call to air traffic control over the radio but was unable to stop the plane from crashing. Her last moments were captured on the gut-wrenching call: "722 Bravo Delta, we're descending 8000. Mayday, Mayday, we're descending 10,000 feet per minute!"

‌



"We are banking 60 degrees, we are going to die," she yelled.

View 5 Images A dashcam captured the moment the private plane crashed next to a busy road in the Greenacres area of Palm Beach County, Florida (Image: Aki Kuusisto via Storyful / AP)

‌



Allan has listened to his daughter's final words on repeat. "I did listen to (her radio transmissions) many times, trying to find a clue in my head how that happened. And wow, she's tough," he said.

He fondly recalled how he would fly with his daughter, who got her pilot licence in high school before she could even drive. "When we were flying together, I used to instruct her. And then, she became my instructor," he said.

‌



View 5 Images Nathalia was first introduced to flying at the age of 12 (Image: itsnatfilg/threads)

Nathalia was first introduced to flying at the age of 12 when her dad would take her on his flights. Five years later, she secured her private pilot's licence through a school program which paid for her to attend an aviation academy.

Article continues below

Despite the devastating loss, Allan said he will "have to find a way to live and make it through".

He said: "It feels like someone is tearing the heart right out of my chest. Nathalia doesn't want to see a father falling apart … I'm going to find a way to make her proud."

News.title: Thomas Markle released on bond hours after arrest for alleged child sex abuse images
News.content:
Thomas Markle released on bond hours after arrest for alleged child sex abuse images

Meghan Markle's dad Thomas Markle Sr has been accused of possessing child abuse images, according to the US Department of Justice (DoJ)

View 3 Images He has previously denied the allegations against him, calling them “sick lies” but he did not enter an official plea during his Friday court appearance (Image: Channel 5)

Thomas Markle Sr has been released under home detention and electronic monitoring just hours after his arrest.

‌



‌



Mr Markle Sr was reported to authorities in the Philippines last month after his son Thomas Markle Jr claimed he found a haul of child sex abuse images. Last week, four boxes of materials allegedly found in Mr Markle Sr’s former home in the Philippines are said to have been handed over to authorities. It is understood the boxes contained computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes.

‌



Mr Markle Sr was seen being taken from the care home in a wheelchair. He has previously denied the allegations against him, calling them “sick lies” but he did not enter an official plea during his Friday court appearance at the federal courthouse in Tampa.

‌



View 3 Images Federal agents seized nearly 80 items from inside storage units rented by Mr Markle Sr

According to PEOPLE he was required to surrender his passport and was released under his own recognizance - a written promise and trust that they will return to court, though a penalty amount is still legally attached if they fail to show up.

It comes as the DoJ said federal agents seized nearly 80 items from inside storage units rented by Mr Markle Sr, including slides, film negatives and books that contained suspected child sex abuse images. He was allegedly in some of the images that were found. It said if convicted, he would face a maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison.

‌



The statement from the DoJ went on: “According to an affidavit filed with the complaint, in October 2026, law enforcement learned that an individual signed an affidavit regarding their discovery of suspected CSAM among Markle’s possessions in the Philippines.

“Law enforcement also interviewed another individual who disclosed that Markle rented a storage unit in the Los Angeles area. Information from the first individual later led agents to a second unit.

‌



View 3 Images Meghan has distanced herself from her dad in recent years

“Pursuant to judicially authorized warrants, FBI special agents searched two storage units registered to Markle. Markle has rented both storage units since 2008, with his most recent payments on both made last month by auto-pay.

‌



“Inside the units, agents seized approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives, and books that contained suspected CSAM. The affidavit describes three of those images. Two images depict an adult man – whom a witness identified as Markle – with a nude prepubescent girl.

“The third image depicts a nude prepubescent girl in a room that appears to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines. The affidavit also describes additional photographs that appear to show Markle with children in various stages of undress.”

Article continues below

When allegations against him surfaced, Meghan Markle revealed she was "deeply distressed" and said she was sent a letter via the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection in 2019 which made “troubling and disturbing allegations” about her father, but that she was given assurances these were being investigated.

The Met has admitted it never shared the details with other law enforcement agencies, with the police watchdog, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), now investigating the force’s conduct.

News.title: Russell Brand  – latest updates: Bear Grylls speaks out over decision to baptise disgraced comedian
News.content:
The disgraced entertainer will be sentenced on Monday – and has been told to expect a lengthy prison sentence

Bear Grylls has insisted Russell Brand's conversion to Christianity "seemed genuine" when he attended his private baptism.

Brand, 51, is facing a significant prison sentence after he was convicted on Thursday of raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others.

TV star Grylls helped to baptise Brand in a ceremony on the River Thames near Henley-on-Thames, Oxfordshire, in early 2024 - after allegations against Brand came to light following an investigation by The Sunday Times and Channel 4.

At the time, Brand shared a photo on Instagram of the adventurer embracing him, writing: "Me, Bear Grylls, The River Thames and of course, The Holy Spirit."

Reacting to the news of Brand’s guilty verdict, Grylls wrote on X: "Brand’s faith seemed genuine to me at the time when I was a guest at his private baptism.

"I have attended a few now. Even visiting in prisons with people who have committed terrible crimes.

"It’s part of our calling as men and women of faith, to love and serve anyone. It is the sick that need healing.

"Judgement is for the courts and God… I wouldn’t want to ever discourage someone’s coming to faith.

"It is right that justice has now been served. I can’t imagine how hard this time has been for the victims, the heroes of the day."

For updates on Russell Brand, follow our live blog below

News.title: Boy, 6, dies weeks after Waterford house fire that killed four family members
News.content:
Boy, 6, dies weeks after Waterford house fire that killed four family members

Six-year-old Elliot English has died following a house fire in Waterford, Ireland, as his brother pays tribute and another child remains critically injured.

View 3 Images Elliot English died in hospital more than three weeks after a house fire in Waterford, Ireland. (Image: Supplied)

A six-year-old boy has died in hospital more than three weeks after a horror house fire in Ireland that killed four members of his family.

Elliot English, who suffered critical injuries in the blaze in Waterford on October 13, had been receiving treatment at Children's Health Ireland in Crumlin, Dublin, before his death on November 6.

The youngster's parents, Kim and Philip English, along with his brothers, Callum and Jayden, all died following the arson attack on their home in the Birchwood estate in Waterford, on October 13.

His heartbroken brother John James English paid tribute to him alongside a smiling photograph, writing: "RIP baby bro Elliot... Your in God's arms and bk with our dad Philip and your mam Kim and lil brothers callum. Jayden" (sic).

It was posted alongside a smiling picture of Elliot.

View 3 Images The house has been boarded up since the fire (Image: PA Wire)

Elliot and another child were rushed to hospital following the attack. The other child remains in a critical condition.

A spokesperson for An Garda Siochana told the Irish Mirror: "An Garda Síochána can confirm that 6-year-old Elliot English who sustained critical injuries during a fire at his home in the Birchwood area of Waterford City on Tuesday, 13th October 2026, has passed away on today’s date, Friday 6th November 2026, at Children’s Health Ireland (CHI) Crumlin, Dublin 12.

"The thoughts of all members of An Garda Síochána are with the extended English family at this sad time."

In total, six people have been arrested by Gardai probing the attack. Four were released without charge, while the other two are before the courts.

Last month, the funerals of Philip, Kim, Jayden and Callum were for the “innocent victims of a web of evil which is the drugs trade”.

View 3 Images Tributes left outside the home following the tragedy (Image: PA Wire)

Bishop Alphonsus Cullinan, who presided over the service at the Sacred Heart Church in Waterford for Philip, Kim, 12-year-old Callum and nine-year-old Jayden, said the tragedy has shocked everybody to their core.

Bishop Cullinan said it was “heart-wrenching” to see four coffins in front of the altar and said those in the drugs trade “need to see the consequences of their dark trade”.

In a powerful message to heartbroken mourners, he said: “This tragedy has shocked us all to the core. How heart-wrenching it is to see four coffins before this sacred altar, and this entire community and the whole country joining in loving solidarity with the family and the many friends of Kim and Phil and Callum and Jayden.

“Four beautiful innocent lives have been taken. Two loving, devoted parents who did their best for their children. Innocent victims of a web of evil which is the drug trade. And as a country, I ask, ‘have we really faced up to this problem?’

Article continues below

“It is a fact that in every city, every town and village and townland, harmful drugs are available. Up and down this dear land of ours, some people are turning to drugs. Young lives and the lives of the not-so-young are being destroyed by drugs. Those who work behind the scenes need to see the consequences of their dark trade.”

News.title: Florida Learjet crash: Co-pilot's dad says her final radio calls showed 'she's tough'
News.content:
Florida Learjet crash: Co-pilot's dad says her final radio calls showed 'she's tough'

Co-pilot Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras declared an emergency as the Learjet descended at 20,000ft per minute. Her dad, a pilot himself, said he listened to the recording repeatedly, hoping to find a clue to what went wrong

View 4 Images The 20-year-old co-pilot declared an emergency moments before the jet crashed (Image: WSVN via AP)

The heartbroken dad of a 20-year-old co-pilot who died in a Learjet crash said her final radio call showed just how tough she was.

‌



Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras was one of nine people killed when the Learjet 60 crashed on a busy road in Palm Beach County on Sunday afternoon. The private jet was flying from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas when it came crashing down. The impact left a deep crater and scattered burning debris just feet from homes and businesses.

For Allan Filgueiras, a pilot himself, the recording was a chance to hear what was happening in the cockpit in his daughter’s own words. He went back to it again and again, listening for anything that might explain the crash.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras had logged more than 1,300 hours of flying (Image: Threads/Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras)

Killer who hid mum-of-seven's body in cellar and dumped bones in bins jailed 28 years later READ MORE :

Fighting back tears at a press conference on Friday, Allan said: “I did listen to that many times trying to find a clue. In my head. How’d that happen? And wow, she’s tough.”

In her final conversation Nathalia could be heard calmly reporting a build-up of ice as the jet flew into a thunderstorm. Turbulence sent the aircraft up and down by 700ft, and it soon began losing altitude rapidly.

As the plane picked up speed, Nathalia told air traffic controllers: “Declare an emergency 722-Bravo-Delta. We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute!”

View 4 Images The Learjet came down on a busy road in Palm Beach County

The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating what caused the crash. The Learjet went beyond its design speed limits as it descended, and parts of its tail were found miles from the crash site.

Relatives confirmed that technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp and their two young children were among those who died. The family’s nanny, Ana Maria Ramirez Cetina, was also killed. The plane’s captain, Jeff Gregory, 55, was at the controls as the jet descended.

Nathalia had logged more than 1,300 hours of flying and completed extensive training to earn her commercial pilot’s licence. Her family used Friday’s press conference to respond to people online who had questioned whether she had enough experience to co-pilot a Learjet.

The family’s lawyer, Stuart Grossman, said the aim was to “preserve not just her memory, but her reputation.” He said there were no immediate plans to file a lawsuit over the crash.

View 4 Images Nathalia earned her commercial pilot's licence before becoming a Learjet co-pilot (Image: itsnatfilg/threads)

Grossman said: “She was at the top of her class in everything that she did, and she was perfectly qualified to be the co-pilot on this flight, despite her tender years.”

John Cox, a retired airline pilot who now leads Safety Operating Systems, started flying professionally at 19. He said securing a co-pilot’s seat on a Learjet at Nathalia’s age was an achievement.

Cox said: “To be in the right seat of a Lear 60, she had to impress somebody, because that’s a good ride. I mean, that’s great. I know she loved it.”

Speaking in Spanish about losing his daughter, Allan said: “For the family - it’s like having the heart torn from my chest,” before adding: “I have to find a way to go on living.”

He added: “She showed me what it is to be a hero because once you see that coming, a lot of the big boys - military or whatever - they can’t handle. And she was the one over there to the last minute fighting.”

News.title: Plane bomb threats: Flights at Heathrow and Birmingham airports hit by hoax
News.content:
Multiple flights across Europe were hit by bomb threats on Friday for the second day in a row and the third time in a week

Bomb threats have been made against several flights across Europe for a second day in a row, causing chaos at airports across the continent.

Flights to and from countries including the UK, Ireland, Denmark, Spain, the Netherlands, Cyprus, Italy and Romania were affected on Friday. Nine of the affected flights were either heading to or departing from Václav Havel Airport in Prague, an airport spokesperson said.

It comes just one day after hoax bomb threats targeted at least 27 flights across Europe. On Thursday, fighter jets were scrambled to escort an Aer Lingus aircraft over France, a Finnair plane over Italy and three Ryanair flights over Bulgaria. The Mirror's map shows all the flights that were disrupted on Thursday.

On Tuesday, seven flights across Europe - two of which had departed from the UK - were subjected to bomb threats.

News.title: Three people arrested after Man Utd fans stage anti-ownership protests at Old Trafford
News.content:
Three people arrested after Man Utd fans stage anti-ownership protests at Old Trafford

Manchester United fans protested against the Glazer family and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch, halting Tuesday's Champions League game against Roma

View 2 Images Manchester United players removed tennis balls from the pitch (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Three people were arrested for throwing objects onto the pitch as part of protests during Manchester United's clash with Roma. In the 20th minute of United's dramatic 3-2 win on Tuesday, fans in the Stretford End threw green tennis balls onto the pitch.

The Champions League tie had to be stopped and United players removed the balls. Play was halted with Roma leading 2-0, as the atmosphere at Old Trafford turned toxic.

Greater Manchester Police have now confirmed that 11 arrests were made relating to Tuesday's match, three of which were for items being thrown onto the pitch. Police arrested four other people for various assault offences - including assault of an emergency worker - while two arrests were made for public order offences, one for fraud and one for a drugs offence.

The protests started before kick-off, as hundreds of green and gold balloons - the colours used to protest the Glazer family's ownership - were bounced around the Stretford End. Chants against the Glazers and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe were also heard.
