In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Olympics gender row boxer Imane Khelif to make professional debut: Algerian announces fight with 21-year-old in December... two-and-a-half years after controversial gold in Paris
Sports.content:
Olympics gender row boxer Imane Khelif to make professional debut: Algerian announces fight with 21-year-old in December... two-and-a-half years after controversial gold in Paris

Olympics gender row boxer Imane Khelif will debut as a professional boxer in December – with the goal of winning a world title.

The Algerian fighter will take on women's boxer Clarida Sarabia, 21, in Paris – more than two years after being dragged into a controversy at the Olympics there.

Khelif has a naturally high level of testosterone – though takes medication to reduce it – and was engulfed in a gender row at the 2024 Games after failing a gender eligibility test with the International Boxing Association in 2023.

'It’s been over two years since I last boxed, and I've really missed being in the ring,' said Khelif.

'The last couple of years have been quite difficult. The time has come to turn professional, and I’m going to give it my all.'

The 27-year-old also said: 'Days became weeks, weeks became months. I waited, doubted. But deep inside, the fire never died. Behind closed doors, I kept fighting.

Olympics gender row boxer Imane Khelif will debut as a professional boxer in December

'Because this fight was never only mine. It was for everyone who dared to be, for everyone who refused to give up.'

Khelif's coach, Kamel Abdesselam, said that Khelif could challenge for a world title within three to five professional fights.

The 27-year-old also hopes to compete in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games, but must take a sex test to compete in the women's category after that was universally mandated by the International Olympic Committee.

Khelif won welterweight gold at the last Olympics.

A fellow gender row boxer, Lin Yu-ting, who claimed the featherweight title in Paris, was cleared earlier this year to return to World Boxing events after a sex test, casting doubt on the fairness of the controversy over her gender.

Khelif has not competed since sex tests were introduced by World Boxing in 2025, taking the fight to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in a bid to compete without being tested, for which a hearing is yet to be held.

But the fighter is happy to take a sex test for the next Olympics, saying to CNN in February: 'Of course, I would accept doing anything I'm required to do to participate in competitions.

'They should protect women, but they need to pay attention that while protecting women, they shouldn't hurt other women.'

Last year, Donald Trump signed an executive order entitled 'Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports'. The United States President referred to Khelif as a 'male boxer' who had 'transitioned' and 'stole the women's gold medal' by competing in Paris.

The President doubled down on calling Khelif a 'male' during a speech to Republican lawmakers in January.

Trump has previously claimed that Khelif is transgender. Our current understanding is that that is incorrect. The boxer was, as far as we know, born female, but is believed to possess the SRY gene, which is associated with male sex chromosomes.

'I respect everyone, and I respect Trump because he's the president of the United States,' Khelif told L'Equipe. 'Trump cannot distort the truth. I'm not trans, I'm a girl.

'I was raised as a girl, I grew up as a girl, people in my village have always known me as a girl.'

Sports.title: Jake Paul will make his boxing comeback on Christmas Eve in Dubai - just a year after suffering a double broken jaw in brutal defeat by Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua.

The YouTuber turned boxer will headline a Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) event on December 24, marking his first professional fight in Dubai.

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem, although Paul is understood to want the Dutchman to lose a significant amount of weight before they could agree to fight.

MVP have yet to confirm who Paul will face as he prepares to return to action following the most damaging defeat of his professional career.

The 29-year-old was stopped by Joshua in the sixth round of their heavyweight showdown in Miami on December 19, 2025, after struggling to cope with the Briton's size, power and experience.

Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua

Paul pictured fighting AJ at the Kaseya Center, Miami, Florida on December 19, 2025

Paul spent much of the early stages attempting to keep his distance from the former two-time unified heavyweight world champion, using his movement to evade Joshua's attacks.

But the contest began to turn decisively in the fifth round as Joshua increased the pressure, flooring Paul twice and leaving him struggling to cope with the relentless assault.

The American survived the round but was dropped again in the sixth before Joshua delivered the decisive blow, landing a powerful right hand that sent Paul to the canvas for a fourth time.

Paul failed to beat the referee's count, with the contest officially stopped at one minute and 31 seconds of the sixth round.

It marked the first knockout defeat of Paul's professional boxing career and his second loss overall, following his split-decision defeat by Tommy Fury in February 2023.

The damage extended well beyond the result. Paul confirmed immediately after the fight that he had suffered a double broken jaw, later sharing an X-ray on social media showing fractures in two places.

He subsequently had surgery to repair the injuries, with two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed. Recovery did not go according to plan, with Paul having to go back under the knife for a second time.

The severity of the injury raised questions over how long Paul would be sidelined and whether he would return to the ring.

The YouTuber-turned-boxer pictured alongside his fiancee Jutta Leerdam (Olympic champion)

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till

But the American has now confirmed his comeback, with Dubai set to host another major event as he looks to rebuild his boxing career.

'I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face,' Paul said.

'Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward.

'I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey.

'Dubai is a city that thinks big, breaks boundaries, and doesn't believe in limits. That's exactly the kind of place I want to make my comeback.

'We've got plenty of names on the list; let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out.'

Paul, who boasts a professional record of 12 wins and two defeats, has become one of boxing's biggest commercial attractions since making his debut in 2020.

His November 2024 bout against Mike Tyson attracted a reported 125million global viewers, while his showdown with Joshua a year later drew 33m.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem (above)

The announcement comes as MVP continues to expand its international presence, with the Dubai event being organised in cooperation with the Dubai Sports Council and the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism.

MVP co-founder and chief executive Nakisa Bidarian said Paul's return demonstrated his determination to continue competing after his injury against Joshua.

'Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport,' Bidarian said.

'This is more than a fight. It's a global event in one of the world's great destination cities, on one of the most special nights of the year, when families everywhere are together and watching.

'We're finalising an opponent worthy of Jake's return and look forward to sharing more in the coming weeks.'

Till, who previously challenged for the UFC welterweight title, has increasingly explored opportunities outside mixed martial arts since leaving the UFC.

Overeem, meanwhile, enjoyed a lengthy career at the highest level of MMA and kickboxing, competing in promotions including the UFC, Strikeforce and K-1.

The 45-year-old Dutchman has not competed in professional MMA since 2021, when he was released by the UFC following his defeat by Alexander Volkov but has stated he's interested in pursing a boxing career.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and wife Paris both break down in tears as they recount how he 'didn't want to live' in deep depression amid his alcohol and drug addiction in new Netflix documentary trailer
Sports.content:
A tearful Paris Fury has revealed how she was left 'scared' over husband Tyson's alarming health decline, with the heavyweight superstar opening up on his paralysing drink and drug addiction in a new documentary.

Tyson, 38, saw his life spiral out of control after reaching the pinnacle of boxing following his heavyweight title triumph over arch rival Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

The Gypsy King, speaking in Netflix's new documentary Tyson Fury, confessed how he had lost his 'whole point of existence' after his win in Dusseldorf, leading to a crippling addiction to alcohol and cocaine.

In the documentary trailer, Tyson says: 'All I wanted to was beat Klitschko. It was an obsession for me.

'I'd achieved all my childhood dreams, but my whole point of existence had been taken away. I didn't want to live.'

Tyson and Paris Fury both broke down in tears as they recounted his troubling addiction past

Fury revealed how he had lost his whole point of existence after winning the heavyweight title

Fury fulfilled a career-long obsession after beating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015

Tyson's wife and childhood sweetheart Paris, could only watch on as her husband's life unravelled, and was emotional as she recounted the traumatising episode.

'Straight after [the Klitschko fight], Tyson said to me "this is as good as it is ever going to get". I didn't understand at the time what he meant,' she says.

'The Tyson I knew was gone and I was so scared.'

The documentary, which charts Tyson's incredible rise to heavyweight champion of the world, tells how he grew up surrounded by strong male figures - where discussing emotions was off limits.

'Growing up in my family, there was no emotion shown. They were all hard nuts. Like 50cent said: "Show no love, love will get you killed."'

Fury fought back from his addiction problems to make his boxing comeback in 2018, before triumphing over Deontay Wilder in a sensational heavyweight trilogy against the big-hitting American - where he won the WBC title.

The Gypsy King sought to unify the heavyweight division against the all-conquering Oleksandr Usyk, but twice fell short in a pair of thrilling contests against the Ukrainian.

Netflix cameras have documented the lives of the Fury family since 2023. The latest series centred on Fury's decision to come out of retirement, plus the family's move from Morecambe to the Isle of Wight.

The streaming giant will broadcast Fury's mega-fight against Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11.

Sports.title: Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga arrested after striking baby mama on the head with a pistol in heated dispute
Sports.content:
Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery following a heated physical bust-up with the mother of his child.

Berlanga, who is signed to Dana White's Zuffa Boxing, was arrested and booked in Polk County, Florida, on one charge of battery and one charge of aggravated battery on Monday.

The fighter is alleged to have repeatedly slapped a woman before hitting her on the head with a gun, according to court documents obtained by the Daily Mail.

The alleged victim, the mother of Berlanga's son, told police that the pair became embroiled in a heated argument while the boxer was driving after leaving a gun range on October 18.

She claimed that the dispute turned physical when Berlanga began slapping her before reaching into the vehicle's cupholder and retrieving a pistol, according to police documents.

The boxer is then alleged to have struck the woman on the forehead with the magazine well of the gun.

Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery

The boxer is accused of hitting the mother of his child on the forehead with a pistol

He lost to Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in 2024

The woman claimed she attempted to escape from the vehicle and flee only for Berlanga to grab her arm and pull her back into the car. She eventually managed to exit the vehicle and sought safety at a nearby 7-Eleven.

Police said they observed swelling and bruising on her face which corroborated her allegations. They also said that they noticed a rip in her shirt and bruising on her inner arm consistent with her claims that Berlanga grabbed her.

When asked by officers if the gun Berlanga struck her with was real, the woman confirmed that it was and that she had witnessed the boxer fire the gun multiple times at the range around 20 minutes earlier.

The police report stated that she was unsure if she wanted to press charges, however, Berlanga was still ultimately arrested as officers declared it a domestic violence case.

Berlanga was booked on felony aggravated battery and misdemeanor battery touch/strike. He made his first court appearance on Tuesday and bond was set at $16,000, per court records.

Berlanga is a top rising boxer with a 24-2 record with 19 KOs. He went up against Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in September 2024 but lost by unanimous decision.

Earlier this year, he headlined an event at Madison Square Garden in New York City, where he delivered a KO loss to Steven Butler in the seventh round.

Sports.title: Teen fighting for life identified after Brisbane boxing night mass shooting - as event official speaks out
Sports.content:
Teen fighting for life identified after Brisbane boxing night mass shooting - as event official speaks out

Jimboomba woman Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau, 19, has been identified as the innocent bystander fighting for life after being shot in the head and neck outside a Queensland pub.

She remained in a critical and unstable condition at Princess Alexandra Hospital on Monday afternoon. Metro South Health confirmed the teenager is still fighting for life in the intensive care unit.

The teenager was active on social media just hours before the shooting. She and her partner were seen lip syncing to Justin Bieber's Daises in a video posted on Saturday afternoon.

Four people were wounded outside Fitzy's Loganholme, south of Brisbane, on Saturday night, while more than 100 spectators, including families with young children, attended the Logan City Titles boxing event.

Phil Austin, from the Australian National Boxing Federation Queensland, categorically rejected suggestions it was a bikie or organised crime attack targeting the boxing.

Austin was in the venue's foyer when the shots erupted.

'The wider community is questioning how can this happen in Logan?' Queensland Police Chief Superintendent Mel Adams said on Monday.

Jimboomba woman Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau remains critically injured after suffering gunshot wounds to her head and neck

Vision of bullet marks on a mirror after four people were shot outside Fitzy's Loganholme during a boxing event on Saturday night

Boxing official Phil Austin was in the foyer when shots erupted, with flying glass striking his arm

'That's a popular local pub, a well-respected institution. That location had children, teenagers, mums and dads at that sporting event.'

Taskforce Maxima is a specialist Queensland Police squad that investigates outlaw motorcycle gangs and serious organised crime.

It is assisting Logan CIB and State Crime Command, which are jointly leading the investigation into the Fitzy's Loganholme shooting.

But Austin told Daily Mail that speculation linking the boxing event to bikies and organised crime was 'people putting two and two together and getting five'.

'I haven't seen any reputed organised crime figures at a fight show in this country in years,' he said.

'Bikies used to go to events, but since the government changed their laws, you just don't see them.'

Austin said he did not recognise any of the victims and could not say whether they had been attending the boxing.

'I don't even know if they were there to watch the boxing,' he said.

Ms Schuster-Togiatau (above) remained in the intensive care unit on Monday afternoon

Austin rejected speculation linking the boxing event to bikies and organised crime

'There's more than just boxing happening at that pub.'

He said no fighters or trainers appeared to have been involved and challenged assumptions that the boxing event itself had been targeted.

'We just happened to be there,' he said.

'It could have been the flower arranging show. It's just the fact that we were there.

'We have no idea why what happened happened. The only thing that we know for sure is it's a tragedy.'

Austin said he had just finished seeing a fighter and left the room being used as the dressing rooms near the venue's front doors when the shooting began.

'I'm in the foyer. I've got maybe a couple of metres, and then there's just a series of shots very, very quickly,' he said.

'We're talking about five or six shots in that or less seconds.'

Police say shots were fired from a Mitsubishi's front passenger window near the venue's drop-off area

Two men wearing balaclavas and gloves were seen inside the vehicle, according to police

Ms Schuster-Togiatau (above) had shared a video lip syncing to a Justin Bieber song just hours before the shooting

Flying glass struck the back of his arm.

'I was wearing a long shirt. Nothing hurt, but it just sort of reinforced me like, okay … this is happening,' he said.

'Before I could sort of basically say to myself, 'Oh crap,' it's over.'

Austin saw a car with its lights on but did not see anyone get out.

'It was my impression that they were actually still in the car,' he said.

Police said a Mitsubishi approached the passenger drop-off area during an intermission and shots were fired from its front passenger window.

Two men wearing balaclavas and gloves were seen inside.

Austin went to alert his crew in the boxing hall at the rear of the venue, away from where the shots had been fired.

Three men aged 27, 37 and 38 remain in hospital with serious injuries but are improving, police said

The Mitsubishi was found burnt out at Waterford West shortly after the shooting

'Then people's reactions start to kick in, and there's a bit of pandemonium, really, a lot of very, very angry people,' he said.

'They used the boxing room, basically, like a safe haven for everybody.'

Patrons began leaving through the back as hotel staff and security marshalled the crowd.

Chief Superintendent Mel Adams said everyone who witnessed the violence would carry some trauma from the night.

'This could have been your family member,' she said.

'This was a random group of people at the front of a popular hotel that became victims.'

The three other victims, men aged 27, 37 and 38, all suffered gunshot wounds to their abdomens. The 38-year-old was also shot in the arm.

All three remained in serious conditions on Monday but were improving, Adams said.

Police have not confirmed whether the men knew one another.

Police believe the attack involved pre-planning but say it remains premature to speculate about gang or organised crime involvement.

The Mitsubishi was found burnt out at Waterford West shortly after the shooting.

CCTV from nearby homes showed its occupants being collected by another vehicle after the car was torched. Police believe one of those involved may have suffered burns or another injury.

A ute was also found burnt later that night, with investigators still examining whether it was connected.

Adams urged anyone who knew or suspected who was responsible to come forward.

'There will be people out there who know who did this or suspect who did this,' she said.

For Austin, who has a son the same age as the critically injured teenager, the shooting has hit particularly hard.

'I've got a son her age, so it's really, really hit home hard,' he said.

He offered the federation's support to the victims, their families and friends.

'This is an awful, awful time for everyone,' he said.

'Let's just hope this girl recovers. It's just awful.'

Sports.title: Conor Benn calls out Conor McGregor for lucrative crossover fight - as he looks to bounce back from brutal second-round knockdown by Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Conor Benn has called out Conor McGregor for a potential crossover fight, just weeks after suffering a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia.

Benn was stopped in the second round of his world title challenge against Garcia in Las Vegas, with a brutal right hand sending the Briton crashing to the canvas before the American finished the job.

It was the first knockout defeat of Benn's professional career and left serious questions over what comes next for the 30-year-old.

But he appears to have an unexpected opponent in mind.

Benn took to social media to share a fight poster featuring himself and McGregor, accompanied by the caption: 'Benn vs McGregor coming soon, 2027'.

He added to the speculation by responding: 'Any day of the week.'

Conor Benn (pictured above) has called out Conor McGregor for a potential crossover fight, just weeks after suffering a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia

Benn is understood to be interested in making the fight happen and is expected to explore potential terms with the Irishman.

Benn has previously been tipped to face McGregor in a lucrative crossover bout, with boxing legend Roy Jones Jr suggesting that the fight would make sense.

He said the crossover bout would be one of two major paydays for the Brit before he considers bringing his career to a close.

Jones also suggested such a contest could help Zuffa Boxing recoup its investment in Benn.

The prospect would offer Benn the chance to headline another major event without the pressure of a world title being on the line, while a fight against McGregor would attract an audience well beyond traditional boxing fans.

McGregor is one of the biggest names in combat sports, having become a global superstar during his time in the UFC before stepping into the boxing ring to face Floyd Mayweather in 2017.

The Irishman is also coming off a difficult period of his own, having suffered a fresh setback on his return to the Octagon against Max Holloway.

A fight with Benn would undoubtedly attract huge attention, although there is no indication yet that the pair are close to agreeing a deal.

Roy Jones Jr has said such a contest could help Zuffa Boxing recoup its investment in Benn

Benn's call-out comes after a brutal night in Las Vegas, where his hopes of becoming a world champion were ended in devastating fashion.

The British fighter had talked up his chances of upsetting Garcia, but the American's speed and power proved too much.

Garcia caught Benn with a vicious right hand in the second round, dropping him heavily to the canvas. Benn managed to get back to his feet, but Garcia immediately went on the attack again, forcing referee Thomas Taylor to step in after just one minute and 25 seconds of the round.

It was a crushing result for Benn, who had worked his way back into contention following his two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Benn lost their first encounter by decision in April 2025 before getting his revenge with a points victory in November.

He subsequently returned to welterweight to challenge Garcia for the WBC title, but the American proved a step too far on the night.

The defeat also raised fresh questions about Benn's future at 147lbs, with making the weight having been a talking point in the build-up.

After the fight, Benn admitted he was unsure what came next and spoke about the sacrifices his boxing career had demanded of his family.

Benn was beaten inside two rounds by Ryan Garcia in their welterweight championship fight

It was the first knockout defeat of Benn's professional career and left serious questions over what comes next for the 30-year-old

He made it clear that spending time with his children was his immediate priority, leaving his next move uncertain.

A lucrative showdown with McGregor would offer a very different route back into the spotlight from another world title challenge.

McGregor, meanwhile, has endured his own difficult return to competition.

The former two-weight UFC champion had been out of action since breaking his leg during his trilogy fight with Dustin Poirier in July 2021.

His long-awaited comeback against Holloway was supposed to mark the start of a new chapter, but things quickly went wrong.

McGregor injured his knee after attempting a jumping kick in the opening seconds of the fight. Unable to continue, he was forced to withdraw after just 69 seconds, handing Holloway the victory.

The result was a frustrating setback for the Irishman, whose return had generated enormous interest among UFC fans.

McGregor subsequently announced plans to undergo surgery, leaving his immediate and long-term future uncertain once again.

McGregor's long-awaited comeback ended in disaster at UFC 329 in Las Vegas (above)

The Irishman blew his knee out after throwing a kick within the first seconds of the bout

At 38, he remains one of the most recognisable figures in combat sports, but another comeback will depend on his recovery and whether he can return to full fitness.

A boxing match with Benn would be a different proposition from another UFC appearance, though it would still require McGregor to make a significant commitment to training and preparation.

McGregor is no stranger to a crossover fight.

His most famous venture outside MMA came in August 2017, when he faced Floyd Mayweather in one of the most heavily promoted boxing matches of all time.

McGregor had never competed in a professional boxing bout before, but that did little to dampen interest in the contest.

The pair embarked on an extraordinary promotional tour, trading insults in front of huge crowds as the fight became a global spectacle.

McGregor made a competitive start, but Mayweather quickly took control before stopping him in the 10th round.

Mayweather improved his professional boxing record to 50-0, while McGregor returned to the UFC having secured a huge payday and further cemented his status as one of sport's biggest commercial attractions.

Sports.title: Boxing world champion Adrien Broner back in hot water as video shows him being handcuffed and hauled into police car in Beverly Hills
Sports.content:
Adrien Broner, the troubled former boxing champion once seen as the future of the sport, had another run-in with police over the weekend in Beverly Hills.

Now more than two years removed from his last fight, the 37-year-old Broner was among a group of men recording content on the streets of Beverly Hills for the social media platform, Kick, when local police arrived.

Viral footage from the incident shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner and his fellow content creator, Deen The Great.

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs. Broner is seen trying to poke fun at the situation by doing a funny walk for the officers' benefit, but they did not seem amused.

'Broner was detained during a traffic stop as part of an investigation into a large street gathering in a residential area,' Beverly Hills police told TMZ in a statement. 'He was released from the scene and a citation was not issued.'

The Daily Mail has sought further information from Beverly Hills police.

Adrien Broner dancing while getting put in handcuffs by the police 💀 pic.twitter.com/h9SZlIYfdM — Happy Punch (@HappyPunch) October 26, 2026

Viral footage shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner (center, open gray sweatshirt) and his fellow content creator, DeenTheGreat

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs on the streets of Beverly Hills

Adrien Broner and Deen The Great attend the Internet Ball on August 19, 2026

Broner is currently among several defendants being sued in Los Angeles County over allegations of sexual battery, battery and assault.

'Plaintiff alleges that Broner repeatedly pressured Plaintiff for sexual activity after repeated refusals, attempted to isolate Plaintiff, repeatedly pressured Plaintiff while intoxicated, attempted unwanted physical contact, publicly humiliated Plaintiff, and made false sexual statements about Plaintiff to a livestream audience,' read the complaint, obtained by The Daily Mail.

Broner has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

Previously, in September of 2025, Broner was kicked off rapper Cam'ron's popular podcast after ignoring the host's warnings to stop flirting with his on-air co-host.

Sporting a greying beard and speaking in an increasingly raspy voice, Broner repeatedly interrupted the interview to make passes at Treasure 'Stat Baby' Wilson, who co-hosts It Is What It Is with Cam'ron and Ma$e.

Adrien Broner and Deen The great attend Sold Out Saturdays on August 15, 2026 in Atlanta

Adrien Broner punches Gavin Rees during their WBC Lightweight Title fight at Atlantic City Boardwalk Hall in 2013. Broner won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011

At one point, Broner responded to a question about boxing's welterweight division by telling Wilson: 'Stat, I love you.'

Things ultimately boiled over during a discussion about Sunday's NFL action when Broner appeared to stop himself from making another comment about Wilson: 'I can't talk… You told me to stop.'

Cam'ron took the moment to end his interview with Broner.

'Hey, we going to have to ask you to go, my n*****,' Cam'ron said before pulling a stack of cash out of a small bag to give to his guest.

'I don't have no problems with you, but I'm gonna pay you for your time,' the rapper said, adding: 'You can't violate, bro.' Cam'ron went on to explain that Wilson's boyfriend was on set.

A native of Cincinnati who won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011, Broner enjoyed a meteoric rise in the boxing world before his career was derailed by a series of arrests, upset defeats and mental health issues.

Sports.title: Aussie boxing legend Jeff Fenech hospitalised as he faces fresh new health battle: 'He's always a fighter'
Sports.content:
Aussie boxing legend Jeff Fenech hospitalised as he faces fresh new health battle: 'He's always a fighter'

Australian boxing legend Jeff Fenech has been hospitalised with heart problems, with his NRL star son-in-law Bradman Best revealing the family’s concern ahead of his Kangaroos debut.

The four-weight world champion, 62, was admitted to Strathfield Private Hospital around 10 days ago after suffering severe fatigue, breathing difficulties and feeling unwell.

Fenech has since had a blood clot removed from his wrist and undergone tests to investigate whether a potentially life-threatening staph infection has returned.

A recurrence has not been confirmed.

Best, who has a baby daughter with Fenech’s daughter Kayla, disclosed the hospital stay while discussing the boxing great’s influence on his career.

The Newcastle centre is preparing to make his Australian Test debut against Fiji on Sunday, but took time to acknowledge Fenech’s health battle.

Jeff Fenech, 62, has been hospitalised after suffering heart problems, fatigue and breathing difficulties

Bradman Best paid tribute to his father-in-law ahead of his Australian Test debut

Fenech has reportedly had a blood clot removed from his wrist and undergone tests for a possible recurrence of a serious infection

‘Jeff has been massive for me, I just want to give a quick shout-out to him,’ Best said.

‘He’s actually in hospital at the moment.

‘I’m thinking of him. He’s tough, he’s always a fighter.’

Best said Fenech had become an invaluable source of advice as he worked towards representing Australia.

‘Jeff has done a lot for me in my career,’ he said.

‘I was visiting him last week and he’s always giving me tips on what to do and how to be better.

‘It’s special having a father-in-law like that who’s a four-time world champion.

‘He’s an icon in Australia and it’s special having a bond like that with him.’

Tim Tszyu’s preparations for his world-title clash with Erislandy Lara have been disrupted by his trainer’s hospitalisation

Fenech became one of Australia’s greatest boxers, winning world titles across four weight divisions during a career that earned him the nickname ‘The Marrickville Mauler’

Asked whether Fenech’s condition was serious, Best remained hopeful.

‘Yeah, he will be right. He’s always a fighter. He’s been in there with a few heart problems and stuff, but he’ll be good.’

The hospitalisation has also interrupted Tim Tszyu’s preparations for his planned WBA middleweight world-title clash with Erislandy Lara.

Fenech became Tszyu’s head trainer in July, helping guide him to a unanimous decision victory over American star Errol Spence Jr.

Tszyu credited the veteran trainer with helping inspire that result, which set up his pursuit of a world championship in a second weight division.

With Fenech sidelined, fellow trainer Basil Nassis has taken charge of Tszyu’s work in the gym.

The Lara bout is expected to take place in Australia in November or December, according to the reports.

Fenech hopes to recover in time to be involved, although the Telegraph reported he is unlikely to perform padwork during the build-up.

The latest scare follows two major heart operations.

In October 2019, Fenech underwent emergency open-heart surgery in Thailand while preparing Jack Brubaker for a fight against Tszyu.

He needed another six-hour open-heart operation in 2024 during a serious infection.

Sports.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Antonelli quickest in tricky FP2
Sports.content:
Newly-minted world champion Kimi Antonelli topped Friday's second practice session at the Brazilian GP, heading Lando Norris and Max Verstappen in Sao Paulo.

At the classic 4.3km Interlagos circuit, Antonelli set his quickest time just before the halfway mark of FP2 as drivers moved towards soft-tyre running, the Italian going faster than Lando Norris and Max Verstappen.

Despite fans intermittently reaching for their ponchos, light drops of rain never really persisted on what was predicted to be the clearest day of a rain-affected weekend. But the cooler, overcast conditions did affect the running in different ways, as Lewis Hamilton reported he "can't get the tyre temperatures up". Hamilton was one of several drivers to lock up the front-left wheel on approach to the heavily cambered Turn 1.

Antonelli, who became F1's youngest ever world champion last weekend in Mexico, suffered from heavy bottoming on the bumpy layout, but still managed to lead the early running on hard tyres with a 1m11.8 lap.

Following a quieter spell, the paddock collectively unwrapped Pirelli's soft tyre compound. Russell, who has a five-place grid penalty overhanging his weekend for taking a new engine, came to the fore with a 1m11.016s lap, before being demoted by Norris and Verstappen.

Russell's Mercedes partner Antonelli went quicker still, dipping below the 1m11 barrier with a 1m10.763s effort. That was a quarter of a second quicker than three drivers from three different teams, such is the convergence of performance towards the end of the 2026 season.

In the upgraded McLaren MCL40, which boasts a new front wing, Norris took second with a 1m11.016s lap, which was 0.006s ahead of third-placed Verstappen, who caused some hilarity with his radio complaints about his Red Bull's clutch.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: James Sutton / Formula 1 / Formula Motorsport Ltd via Getty Images

Russell and Oscar Piastri all followed within a tenth of Norris to complete the top five. Ferrari, often strong out of the gates on Friday, had an unusually muted start in Brazil. After going quickest in the first sector, Hamilton settled for sixth with team-mate Charles Leclerc in seventh, Leclerc rueing being impeded on the straight by Haas debutant Rafael Camara.

Aboard a dark green Audi, Gabriel Bortoleto was eighth on home soil, with Isack Hadjar and Haas driver Oliver Bearman rounding out the top 10.

Camara eventually took 16th, half a second off his team-mate, as Haas' 2027 signing completed his first full day as a grand prix driver replacing the ousted Esteban Ocon.

Audi's Nico Hulkenberg remained stuck in the garage after undisclosed issues plaguing FP1 stand-in Freddie Slater earlier on Friday.

Sports.title: Vasseur issues reminder to Hamilton and Leclerc in post-Mexico Ferrari talks
Sports.content:
Ferrari F1 chief Fred Vasseur insists he has cleared the air with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton after their highly publicised Mexican Grand Prix clash last week.

At the Mexico City event, Hamilton and Leclerc both went off track on lap one as they fought for the lead, with Hamilton losing a position to Max Verstappen instead, while Leclerc was penalised and eventually also ceded the lead to the Red Bull driver.

Verstappen went on to win the race with Hamilton second and Leclerc off the podium in fourth, with the sabre-rattling on lap one robbing the team of a possible third win of the campaign. Hamilton was particularly furious about how Leclerc had raced him at the start, lobbying for the stewards to hand his team-mate a bigger penalty for cutting the track.

The seven-time world champion demanded serious talks with Leclerc and Vasseur over how hard his team-mate was racing him, while Vasseur was frustrated with what he felt was a lack of respect towards Maranello's 2,000-strong staff trying to provide both drivers with a winning car.

Those talks have since happened on Thursday night in Sao Paulo, and speaking to the media for the first time since last weekend, Vasseur was adamant the message to both of his drivers was loud and clear. Ferrari must always come first.

"The guidelines are always the same. They are two competitors with a fighting spirit for sure, but they need to have respect for each other," Vasseur said. "But mainly and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working on track. I think we are putting a lot of effort on this and the message was clear and will stay clear."

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: James Sutton / Formula 1 / Formula Motorsport Ltd via Getty Images

On Thursday Hamilton said he agreed with suggestions that Leclerc was racing him harder than he raced other drivers, his team boss pointed towards Leclerc's aggressive overtake on Verstappen in Austin to downplay those claims.

"He said that he was fighting probably a bit harder with him than with some others, but if you have a look at what Charles did in Austin in the first sector, everybody said that it was magic," Vasseur said. "The line is fine between the two. But he didn't crash into the other car."

The Frenchman added: "For sure, in this situation, we failed collectively because we were one and two and we didn't win the race at the end. That means that it's clear that we failed and we have to react.

"But the conclusion of the meeting yesterday evening was clear that it was a clear reminder that the Ferrari is coming first, is coming first for the brand, for the employees, for the Tifosi, and this we have to keep it in mind."

Sports.title: Herta qualifies for F1 superlicence as Bottas remains bullish on 2027 seat
Sports.content:
Cadillac Formula 1 test driver Colton Herta has finally obtained the last remaining superlicence point required to drive in the series, but incumbent Valtteri Bottas remains bullish on his future with the squad.

Herta conducted his sixth Friday practice session of the 2026 season at Interlagos, reaching the required threshold of 100km to earn his 40th superlicence point needed to race in F1.

Cadillac believed the former IndyCar ace had reached that threshold last week in Mexico, but it soon emerged the Californian was still one point shy amid confusion over his previous IndyCar results. The US-owned squad rectified that error by handing Herta another Friday FP1 session in Sergio Perez's car.

That allows the team to keep its options open as it considers retaining incumbent Bottas for a second year alongside Perez or handing Herta his F1 debut in 2027.

The amount of time, energy and money spent by Cadillac to prepare Herta and ensure he kept churning out FP1 sessions suggests that the team is set on promoting the 26-year-old American as early as next year.

But Bottas was bullish on retaining his seat for 2027 and said he was bemused by the extent of the rumours around his seat after a difficult year with the troubled Cadillac MAC-26. Alongside Herta, several other drivers have either held private talks with Cadillac or publicly applied for Bottas' seat, like Mercedes reserve driver Frederik Vesti.

Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT images via Getty Images

"I've been quite surprised about the amount of noise on that," Bottas said on Thursday. "Because I know what my situation is. And all I've heard, the team has been happy with what I'm doing.

"But at the same time, we know how this sport works. Everyone wants to be in F1 and if somebody sees an opportunity somewhere, they're going to try and go for it one way or the other.

"But the way our team is structured and the way decisions are made for the future, everything needs to be approved by the board. And I believe that meeting is still yet to happen. I've been convinced nothing has changed."

Read Also: Formula 1 Liverpool FC owners emerge as potential buyers of Cadillac F1 shares amid TWG uncertainty

Bottas has underperformed compared to team-mate Perez, but has also dealt with numerous issues with Cadillac's debut car, the latest coming in the shape of a high-speed accident in Mexico due to a suspension failure. That has made the Finnish veteran's performances tougher to judge, but the 10-time race winner insists the right people know how to appraise him.

"I think the people who know, they know. That's what I feel like. And I've got good support on that side," the 37-year-old said. "We have bigger problems to solve than the drivers at the moment and I think Mexico was a good example.

"The team knows what they can get out of me if everything works well. But so far, they haven't really delivered with a car that I can do much. But honestly, that was always what I kind of expected for the first year. I came here to try and improve things for the future, definitely not with a mindset to fight for my seat."

Sports.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Norris fastest in opening practice from new champion Antonelli
Sports.content:
Lando Norris was fastest in first practice at Formula 1’s Brazilian Grand Prix, leading Kimi Antonelli, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.

This classification meant the four top teams were again very close to one another. Norris outpaced Antonelli by 0.082s on the soft rubber with a time of 1m11.717s, while Verstappen and Hamilton were two and three tenths adrift respectively.

Not all of them were happy, however, with Verstappen complaining about a longtime problem of the RB22. “Unacceptable, man. Unacceptable, these downshifts. What the ****?” he ranted on the radio. Later on, he mentioned yet another issue: “There’s something wrong with my steering. It’s getting harder and harder to turn the wheel.”

There were hefty lock-ups galore in Turn 1, for veterans and rookies alike – and there were many of the latter in action now. The most prominent of them undoubtedly was Rafael Camara, with Haas’ 2027 driver making an early F1 debut at home this weekend following Esteban Ocon’s fallout with the team.

Formula 2’s championship leader was 18th-fastest in this session, nearly nine tenths slower than team-mate Oliver Bearman.

One rookie who did outpace the sister car was Alpine’s Gabriele Mini, who took seventh place with a 1m12.569s, 0.085s quicker than Franco Colapinto. No other test driver made it into the top 10; McLaren’s Leonardo Fornaroli was 11th (+1.116s vs Norris), Williams’ Luke Browning 17th (+0.080s vs Alex Albon, who had a mechanical problem) and Cadillac’s Colton Herta 20th (+0.904s vs Valtteri Bottas).

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

Herta’s trouble-free session – other than a mammoth lock-up into Turn 1 – should theoretically mean he will collect the final required point for an FIA superlicence, making him eligible to a 2027 F1 seat should Cadillac elect to promote him next year.

Ferrari’s Dino Beganovic and Audi’s Freddie Slater propped up the classification after encountering technical issue which prevented them from setting soft-tyre times and restricted their mileage. “The car has just switched off,” Slater said, causing a red flag just 12 minutes into the session. The pair completed 11 and seven laps respectively.

Sports.title: "Exhausted" Russell set for Brazilian F1 grid penalty
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver George Russell will lose five places on Sunday's Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix grid as he takes his sixth internal combustion engine of the season.

Following a brace of power unit related issues earlier this year, the latest arriving after a failure at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia, Russell was always going to require a sixth ICE before the end of the year.

With Lewis Hamilton's spectacular sprint recovery from 20th to fifth in mind, which he pulled off at the 2021 edition with Mercedes, the team felt Interlagos was as good a place as any to take it.

As Russell had already exceeded his initial allowance of four units for the season in Singapore, his additional engine only costs a five-place grid penalty.

"We always had to take a grid penalty at some point between Singapore and the end of the year and we felt like a good place to take it," Russell said on Mercedes' social media channels.

"Obviously, Lewis took a very big penalty here a number of years ago and did pretty well. Five places isn't that bad."

George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Planned or not, it's Russell's latest setback after a nightmarish 2026 campaign in which he was never able to build up momentum and ended up being outperformed by newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli.

Speaking on Thursday, Russell admitted that the number of times he has had to bounce back after a disappointing weekend, of which there were many, had been wearing on him.

"I probably just feel a bit exhausted this season of constantly picking myself back up. When you get kicked to the ground you pick yourself back up, then you get kicked down again, you pick yourself back up. I was hoping to do that maybe twice in the season, not every other weekend," he said with a wry smile.

Russell, who has dropped to fourth in the standings behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, always insisted the 2026 power unit regulations punished his natural driving style, having chased his tail across the season to try and adapt. But with the rules reducing the share of electric power next year, amid other tweaks, Russell backed himself to overcome his down year.

"The power unit changes next year. The tyres are changing slightly for next year," he said. "I've had a lot more good years than bad years. I don't think there's a single athlete or just individual in the world that [only] goes through great years every single year.

"It's the way you bounce back from those years to continue having the belief and courage to return to those positive ways, and that mental resilience. What this year has taught me is that I still believe in myself and next year we fight again."

Sports.title: Ferrari set for crunch meeting as Hamilton and Leclerc tension reaches Brazil
Sports.content:
Ferrari arrived at Interlagos facing a problem that, until just a few weeks ago, would have been difficult to imagine in quite this form. After a long season spent chasing competitiveness, the team finally appears to have found many of the answers that had been missing with its SF-26 Formula 1 car.

The results from the last few grands prix confirm that progress, but just as the Scuderia has regained the ability to fight for victories, a delicate issue has emerged: the relationship between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc on track.

What happened in the opening corners of the Mexico GP continues to dominate the conversation. The flashpoint between the two Ferrari drivers compromised a Sunday that could have delivered a very different result for the team and, more importantly, exposed a tension that does not appear to have dissipated after the race.

Speaking to the media at Interlagos yesterday, Hamilton reaffirmed the position he had expressed on Sunday evening in Mexico City. There was no backtracking and no attempt to play down what happened. It is a sign that the issue remains unresolved.

Read Also: Formula 1 Hamilton backs claims Leclerc races him harder than F1 rivals

There has been no opportunity for the two drivers and team boss Fred Vasseur to sit down together since Mexico. Vasseur returned to Maranello, while Leclerc went to be with his family ahead of the birth of his child with his wife, Alexandra. The discussion has therefore been postponed until today, when the Monegasque arrives in the Interlagos paddock.

It will be an important meeting. Not so much to establish who was right or wrong in Mexico, but to define a principle that both drivers must respect: when a Ferrari is in a position to win, the team's interests cannot be put at risk by an internal battle.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

But why have two drivers who are no longer in contention for the world championship reached such a high level of tension? The answer is not straightforward and inevitably involves a degree of speculation. Hamilton has spent much of his career in a very particular position. Following Nico Rosberg's retirement at the end of 2016, the British driver enjoyed many years at Mercedes with a team built around him. It was a situation in which his position was never genuinely in question.

His move to Ferrari brought him into a very different environment. Hamilton found himself alongside a team-mate who not only knows the organisation inside out, but has also built a very strong relationship with the Scuderia over the years. For a driver accustomed to being the reference point within his team, sharing that role can be an unfamiliar experience.

On the other side is Leclerc, who has worn Ferrari colours since 2019. The Monegasque has endured difficult seasons, accepted the technical limitations of cars that have often fallen short of expectations and continued to be one of the team's cornerstones. It is understandable that he now feels he has earned a position he has no intention of surrendering, even in the face of a seven-time world champion.

These are two different journeys, two strong personalities and two drivers with more than enough motivation to not give ground. A world championship does not necessarily have to be at stake to fuel a rivalry. Sometimes, it is precisely the absence of an immediate shared objective that makes finding a balance more difficult.

The paradox is that this situation has emerged just as Ferrari appears to have overcome many of the problems that have hampered its season. Over the last three races, the Scuderia has scored more points than any other team in the constructors' championship, marking a significant turnaround compared with the first part of the campaign.

The SF-26 has once again become a car with which Hamilton and Leclerc can target pole positions and wins. Yet, at precisely this moment, the team must contend with the risk that an internal battle could compromise the collective result. What happened in Mexico showed just how fine the line can be between a rivalry that helps drive performance and one capable of turning a potential victory, or even a 1-2 finish, into a missed opportunity and what ended up being second and fourth.

Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT images via Getty Images

Vasseur's role

The French team principal faces one of the most delicate challenges of his tenure. Until now, he has consistently defended his drivers' freedom to race each other on track, believing that two champions should be allowed to compete without excessive restrictions. It is a philosophy that makes sense, but it requires one fundamental condition: both drivers must understand and respect the point beyond which individual rivalry becomes detrimental to the team.

That is precisely what today's meeting at Interlagos must address. Hamilton has already made it clear that he has no intention of changing his interpretation of events. Leclerc's position remains to be heard, as he was absent from yesterday's media commitments. Vasseur's task will be to listen to both drivers and, above all, establish rules that leave no room for interpretation.

To achieve that, however, the team principal must have the full backing of Ferrari's leadership. This is not simply about giving him the support he needs to make decisions, even unpopular ones, but ensuring that there is a single voice when dealing with the drivers – one that everyone recognises as the ultimate authority.

This is a fundamental principle in running a team, particularly one with drivers of Hamilton and Leclerc's calibre. If instructions come from different people, or if there is even the possibility of seeking confirmation and support elsewhere, the authority of the person responsible for leading the team inevitably risks being undermined. Ferrari's leadership must support Vasseur, but, more importantly, it must allow him – and him alone – to represent the team's position to its drivers. That is the only way to give decisions full authority and ensure they are respected.

Managing two drivers of this calibre cannot be influenced by the weight of their respective reputations or by the potential external repercussions of a decision. If the objective is to return Ferrari to a position where it can consistently fight for world championships, the team's needs must take precedence over any individual ambition. That does not necessarily mean introducing predetermined driver hierarchies. Rather, it means ensuring that decisions taken in the Scuderia's best interests are recognised and respected by both drivers, without exception.

There is one final aspect that makes the Interlagos meeting even more important. The 2026 season is now entering its closing stages, but Ferrari is already working towards next year's championship, with the ambition of arriving at the season opener in a position to fight for the biggest prizes.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Manuel Eletto / Getty Images

That prospect requires not only a competitive car, but also a harmonious environment and an organisation in which everyone understands their role. A potential battle for the world championship would inevitably make managing a rivalry even more difficult – one that has already shown signs of tension despite there being no title at stake this season.

For that reason, the meeting between Vasseur, Hamilton and Leclerc will be about more than simply clearing the air over what happened in Mexico. It could mark the moment when Ferrari establishes the ground rules for how its drivers will work together in the future.

The SF-26 finally appears to have rediscovered the path to competitiveness. Now it is up to the team to ensure that, when the opportunity to win comes, its own drivers do not turn it into another missed opportunity.

Sports.title: Permane signs new Racing Bulls F1 deal
Sports.content:
Red Bull has given Alan Permane a new contract as the Racing Bulls Formula 1 squad’s team principal.

Permane will retain the reins of the Faenza-based outfit until the end of the 2031 season.

A stalwart of the current Alpine squad, where he worked from 1989 to 2023 in various capacities including race engineer and sporting director, Permane joined Racing Bulls (then known as RB) ahead of the 2024 campaign as its racing director, before being promoted to the team principal role when incumbent Laurent Mekies replaced Christian Horner at Red Bull.

Oliver Mintzlaff, CEO Corporate Projects and Investments Red Bull, said: “Alan is doing a tremendous job, and the progress the team has made is a direct reflection of his experience, commitment and competitive mindset. He brings clarity, composure, and a deep understanding of what it takes to perform in Formula 1, while creating an environment where people can consistently deliver at their best.

“The results Visa Cash App Racing Bulls has achieved in recent seasons underline the strength of the team and the work being done throughout the organisation. Alan has played a key role in that progress, and we are very pleased that he will continue to lead the team as we look to build on this momentum in the years ahead.

“Together with Peter Bayer as Co-CEO Commercial, Alan forms a strong and experienced leadership team. They complement each other exceptionally well, bringing different strengths and perspectives to the organisation. I am delighted that we have this stability and continuity in place, providing a clear platform for the team’s future development and long-term ambitions.”

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Alan Permane, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls, Peter Bayer, Racing Bulls Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

Permane added: “I am immensely proud to be continuing this journey with VCARB, and I would like to thank everyone at Red Bull for the trust and support they have given me. What makes this team special is the shared spirit of everyone; trackside, in Faenza and in Milton Keynes, and it is a privilege to lead such a talented and committed group every day.

“Fighting for fifth in the championship is something we should all be very proud of, but it is the result of years of hard work from a lot of people, and we are not done yet. We have the right people, the right culture and a clear sense of where we want to go, and I am excited to keep pushing together.”

The Italian team has made steady progress under Permane, having scored 46 points in 2024, 92 last year and already 108 so far this season, with the outfit all but certain to clinch fifth place in the constructors’ championship – its highest finish ever since it was founded as Minardi in 1985.

Asked about Racing Bulls’ progress back in Baku, Permane told Sky Sports F1: “What we've done through the year is we've just put load on the car. We've just put downforce on, and every time we've brought an upgrade, it's worked.”

Sports.title: Hamilton backs claims Leclerc races him harder than F1 rivals
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton maintains Ferrari needs further talks to iron out its rules of engagement, backing claims Charles Leclerc races him harder than drivers from rival teams.

Hamilton and Leclerc came to blows on lap one of last weekend's race in Mexico with both drivers going off the track at Turn 4, which eventually handed Max Verstappen a golden opportunity to snatch away the win and costing Ferrari a possible 1-2 victory, instead the duo finishing second and fourth.

Hamilton was incensed by how hard Leclerc raced on the opening lap, only for the Monegasque to permanently stay ahead as he cut the track at Turn 4. Leclerc only received a five-second penalty for gaining a lasting advantage, with mitigation bringing that punishment down from 10 seconds.

Their Mexico fight further fed suggestions that Leclerc appears to race his teammate harder than anyone else, having come after a Singapore Grand Prix in which Leclerc backed off at the start despite being fully on the inside of polesitter Max Verstappen. Leclerc did race the Dutchman hard at the subsequent US Grand Prix in Austin, however, overtaking the Red Bull man around the outside of COTA's Esses.

When asked if the idea of Leclerc racing him harder than other drivers is something Hamilton has also noticed, the seven-time world champion replied: "Yes. I see what you see. In Singapore, he was fully on the inside into Turn 1, he had won the lead, and he backed off. It was definitely different.

"But I mean, if you look at the team-mates, it was the same with Sebastian [Vettel]. It was the same with Carlos [Sainz].

Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

As emotions ran high, Hamilton demanded talks to clarify the team's rules of engagement and warned of "big problems" for the squad. Autosport understands team principal Fred Vasseur has spoken briefly to both drivers, albeit separately, after feeling the events of Mexico showed a lack of respect towards the team's 2000 people staff.

But with Vasseur having travelled back to Europe in between races and Leclerc spending time with his family following the birth of his daughter, Hamilton welcomes further talks with Leclerc and their boss in Sao Paulo on Friday. "Naturally I was frustrated, and I'm still frustrated," he said when asked by Autosport if he views the events of Mexico in a different light now they have had time to cool off. "So, conversations need to be had. We will have those when the time permits.

"We had an opportunity to win for the team. The team has done such an amazing job in bringing upgrades this year and I think they've done an incredible job. We've scored more points than any other team in the last three or four races. We could have easily had a one-two, so we definitely have to work towards making sure that doesn't happen again."

Hamilton drew criticism, too, for openly lobbying for his team-mate to get a bigger penalty than the five seconds he was held at his pitstop, as cutting the track handed Leclerc a much bigger advantage than that on a circuit where overtaking proved extremely difficult. But the 41-year-old said he "will not be silenced". "I don't really care how everyone feels about what I've said. I wear my heart on my sleeve, and I say how I feel in the moment," he said.

"I did see something that someone was saying that the things that I'm saying are calculated, and I just want to combat that with the fact that when you're in the race, your heart rate is like 170. You're driving 200 miles an hour. You don't have time to be calculated in what you're saying and thinking about what the media are going to write about, you don't think about that.

"Of course, there's some times you say things and maybe you might regret it afterwards, but I don't, and I'm never going to apologise for being authentic and real. I'm not gonna be silenced. I've never ever been silenced. I have not been asked to not say anything [by the team], and that's just the way it is."

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Keeping Lawson is the smart choice for Racing Bulls | Brief
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls are heading for the best-ever championship finish but the driver who scored the majority of their points does not know whether they will keep him for next season.

He has 83 points so far this season (Lindblad (a rookie, and also excellent) has 38; Hadjar (driving the car that Lawson gained 8 of his points in) has 107 (only 24 more). Further, Racing Bulls have 108 points (39 more than Alpine) and lie (solidly) in fifth place in the constructors’, which as the article says would be the team’s best finishing position in its history (including 2008, when Vettel won at Monza).

His brief time at Red Bull this season was not brilliant (rather like his previous (even briefer) time with Red Bull. But then nor has anyone been brilliant in the second Red Bull seat (since Ricciardo), and in any event he has shown what he can do in the (easier to drive) Racing Bulls car.

It is November. Unless he wanted to race for Cadillac (even if the seat was his for the taking) he has no other race seat option for next year.

Given the stage of the season, and given the performance of both of their drivers this year, Racing Bulls owe it to both Lawson and Lindblad to keep them on for 2027. Ultimately, I am confident that will be happen. If it doesn’t, however, they will have ripe cause for complaint.

Wellbalanced

Sports.title: Ferrari’s racing guidelines “still the same” after Mexican GP talks – Vasseur | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur has not changed the racing rules between his drivers following their defeat in the Mexican Grand Prix.

Vasseur made his dissatisfaction clear after seeing his drivers lead the field away at the start of last week’s race, only to be beaten to victory by Max Verstappen . The Red Bull driver gained the upper hand when the two Ferrari drivers went off fighting for the lead on the first lap.

Lewis Hamilton accused Charles Leclerc of costing the team a one-two finish by challenging him too robustly at the start. Vasseur said he reminded the pair to put the team’s performance first.

“For sure, in this situation, we failed collectively because we were one-two and we didn’t win the race at the end,” he said. “That means it’s clear that we failed, and we have to react.

“But, yes, the conclusion of the meeting yesterday evening was clear. It was a clear reminder that Ferrari is coming first. It’s coming first for the brand, for the employees, for the Tifosi, and this, we have to keep it in mind.”

However he has not issued new instructions on how the pair engage with each other on the track. “The guidelines are still the same,” said Vasseur.

“I think they accumulated a bit of frustration because they are starting each weekend side by side and you have a kind of accumulation of facts. But at the end of the day, the guidelines are always the same, they need to respect each other.

“They are two competitors with fighting spirit for sure, but they need respect for the other one. But mainly and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working on track.

“I think we are putting a lot of effort on this and the message was clear and will stay clear.”

Sports.title: Camara reprimanded over “clearly dangerous” incident with Leclerc in practice | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 newcomer Rafael Camara has received an official reprimand over an incident during his first day in an official track session.

Haas’s new driver impeded Charles Leclerc during the second practice session at the Interlagos circuit. The stewards ruled Camara caused a dangerous situation.

After speaking to Camara and his team, the stewards ruled the driver was given sufficient warning about the Ferrari approaching him at one of the quickest points on the circuit.

“Car 51 [Camara] was warned multiple times that car 16 [Leclerc] was arriving on a fast lap. Yet, Car 51 was weaving and moving well into the racing line.

“Car 16 had to take evasive action to avoid a collision by moving to the right, with a significant amount of the car off the track. The situation that was created was clearly dangerous and car 51 should have taken more care to avoid impeding car 16.

“While the typical penalty for impeding in a free practice session is a warning, in this instance, we are of the view that a reprimand is warranted.”

Sports.title: Wolff criticises Moto GP riders over Qatar race: ‘They know nothing about what’s going on’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has strongly criticised Moto GP riders who have expressed concerns about racing in Qatar this weekend.

The majority of riders have urged the motorcycle series to provide guarantees for their safety at this weekend’s round in the Middle East.

The Moto GP race was originally due to take place in April but was postponed following the outbreak of war between the US and Iran. Fears over a possible resumption in hostilities have grown following the results of this week’s midterm elections in the US.

Four bikes are missing from this weekend’s event after Yamaha announced on Sunday it would not participate due to concerns over safety in the region. F1 is due to race at the track in three weeks’ time.

Wolff said he trusts FOM CEO Stefano Domenicali and FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem to judge whether it is safe for F1’s race to go ahead and claimed Moto GP riders are ignorant about the situation.

“Stefano and Mohammed have been pretty clear about the situation, that Formula 1 follows what the international guidelines are, whether there’s travel restrictions, airlines not flying, any warnings in the region,” said Wolff. “The kind of feedback that local governments are making, so not only the promoters, but what the local governance are making.

“This is what you need to rely on in my opinion. And I’m fully with that. I think that if riders stand up, that, geopolitically, know nothing about what’s going on, but have the audience that listens, I think that is something that creates media value.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But I would have done the same that Moto GP management has done. You want to ride or drive, go, if you don’t want to, don’t go, as simple as that. And everybody can take their personal decisions on that and I respect that.”

However Wolff admitted the situation could change. “Of course you’ve got to be wary of what’s happening in the next few days, a few weeks and Stefano has the finger on the pulse to monitor that. If things were to get more dangerous then he’s going to be the first one, together with Mohammed, to protect the people that were meant to travel. And so that’s why I’m following their guidance for what I’m hearing.”

He said no one within Mercedes has raised any concerns about travelling to Qatar. “Internally, it hasn’t been raised, it hasn’t been a topic.

“But also there, if someone feels he or she doesn’t feel comfortable in travelling, then it’s something that I would always respect and maybe that’s an opportunity to give somebody else a chance. It wouldn’t change anything for the relationship, I’ve always respected that some people didn’t want to go to certain grands prix and that’s how I see it at the moment.”

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur echoed Wolff’s views on whether it is safe to race in Qatar. “I think that our organisation is quite robust, that I have full trust in the FIA and FOM and Stefano, and let’s see what we will do,” he said.

“Concerning the point that if we had questions internally: honestly, we are in the middle of nine races in eleven weeks, everybody is focused on the triple one. Perhaps the topic will come on the table a bit later, but it’s not the case today.

“In any case, we will respect the decision of the team member. If someone feels something and doesn’t want to come, then we will accept the decision.”

Sports.title: Antonelli comfortably on top in second practice | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli and Lando Norris swapped places at the top of the times in the second practice session.

The Mercedes driver, who narrowly missed out on the top time in the first hour of running, was a quarter of a second quicker than anyone at the end of second practice.

Max Verstappen was third-quickest again, followed by George Russell. With Oscar Piastri’s McLaren in fifth place, the four drivers closest to Antonelli were covered by less than a tenth of a second after their qualifying simulations on soft tyres.

Thick cloud settled over the Interlagos session ahead of the second session. Slight drizzle fell before the hour of running ended but not enough to prevent drivers completing the session on slick tyres.

Neither Ferrari driver figured in the top five. Lewis Hamilton was almost half a second behind in sixth place while Charles Leclerc, back in his car after Dino Beganovic’s run in first practice, was seven-tenths adrift.

Another strong run for Gabriel Bortoleto saw him end Friday’s running in eighth place, displacing Isack Hadjar. But Nico Hulkenberg did not run at all after the problem which brought his car to a stop while Freddie Slater drove it earlier in the day.

Sports.title: Williams has not upgraded 2026 car to “save the cost cap dollars for next year” – Vowles | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Williams team principal James Vowles says the decision not to bring further upgrades for its car was “painful”.

The team which finished fifth in the world championship last year has sunk to ninth in the standings. It introduced a new chassis for both drivers at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix but has not developed it in order to maximise its potential under Formula 1’s budget cap.

“We’ve had a tough year, simple as that,” Vowles told Sky. “This is not where we wanted to be.

“Our development kicked in to ’27 early on. The chassis we brought to Baku were ’27 chassis, perfectly brought forward, but spent the money in this year to allow us to get to where we need to.

“We’ve purposely not spent money on – we have more aero locked away in the wind tunnel that we have not brought to the track, really saving the cost cap dollars for next year.

“It’s horribly painful. I can’t tell you how painful it was to sit in the meeting and make those decisions, because it’s just not the way you think. You want every millisecond on track.”

He said the team has focused its efforts on developments for next year, when the chassis will be largely unchanged from this season.

“The work we’ve been doing in Austin, the work we have done less so today, but more in Mexico, was preparation work for ’27 as well. Understanding the package, the aero development mechanisms we’ve gone through, it helps us get ahead of the curve.

“We’re aware that with this car at the moment, points are only going to be there if fortune falls our way, and the reality behind it is we’re better off investing in the future.”

However the team also limited its running in practice today in order to reduce wear on its diminishing stock of parts.

“We are getting towards the end of the season so we want to basically reduce down the mileage just a little bit for both cars and just make sure that we’re clean all the way through for the remainder,” said Vowles.

Sports.title: Norris narrowly leads Antonelli in first practice at Interlagos | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Outgoing world champion Lando Norris put McLaren on top in the first practice session for the Brazilian Grand Prix.

Max Verstappen and Andrea Kimi Antonelli took turns at the top of the times after setting quick laps on soft tyres. But last year’s Brazilian Grand Prix winner displaced them both with a quickest lap of 1’11.717.

Norris and his successor as world champion were separated by less than a tenth of a second at the top of the times. Verstappen, who began his soft tyre run early in the session, was two tenths of a second behind in third place.

Lewis Hamilton ensured four different constructors filled the top four places. The Ferrari driver was one of several to lock up heavily at the first corner and run wide during the session.

Six junior drivers took the opportunity to participate in the session. Gabriele Mini was the quickest of them, putting his Alpine in an impressive seventh place behind George Russell and Isack Hadjar. His team complimented him on a “decent” effort which left him just under a tenth of a second faster than regular driver Franco Colapinto.

Gabriel Bortoleto set the eighth-fastest time for Audi in front of his home crowd. But their junior driver Freddie Slater suffered another disrupted session, coming to a stop on his seventh lap after barely 10 minutes of running, triggering a red flag.

Sports.title: Spotlight: Who won F1 and F2 in the same year? Colapinto knows his history | Brief
Sports.content:
Sebastian Vettel was renowned for his knowledge of Formula 1 history, but does any driver on the grid today measure up to that standard?

Alpine driver Franco Colapinto showed he know his stuff in yesterday’s press conference when the discussion turned to Formula 2 points-leader Rafael Camara making his grand prix debut this weekend.

Camara gave no insight into whether he’ll return to F2 after making his debut for Haas this weekend. Colapinto wondered if he might do both.

“It would be really fun to do F2 and F1 at the same time,” the Alpine driver suggested. “You can do the same weekend, both? Do F2 quali, you jump in F1.”

“Jim Clark won both in the same year. But it’s the same, a little bit?”

Clark did indeed clinch F1 and F2 championships in the same year, 1965. In fact, he and F1 rival Graham Hill finished first and second in both series.

But there’s no chance of Camara being able to race for both Haas and Invicta. F2’s regulations state: “Any driver nominated to race by a competitor participating in the FIA Formula One World Championship will not be permitted to participate in the FIA Formula 2 Championship in the same competition.”
