Sports.title: Canelo Fought Kovalev, So Why Rule Out Beterbiev?
Sports.content:
Sergio Mora argues that Canelo Alvarez is simply too small for Dmitry Bivol or Artur Beterbiev, but that claim collides with Canelo’s track record. Moving up to light heavyweight did not stop Canelo from taking on Sergey Kovalev, so physical scale alone should not close the book on either matchup.

When Chris Mannix asked what should happen if Bivol gets past Callum Smith, Mora chose a third meeting between Bivol and Beterbiev over a Canelo rematch. He dismissed Canelo’s prospects, pointing to edges that reach beyond the 175-pound limit.

“Bivol’s bigger, he has faster feet, and he has one of the best jabs in boxing that gives Canelo issues. And Beterbiev is just way too big, way too strong, and he has smart footwork as well. Not in and out like Bivol, but it’s smart fundamentally. No, both of those guys are too big for him,” Mora told DAZN Boxing.

The technical points Mora raises hold far more substance than simple scale. Canelo climbed to 175 in November 2019, stopping the 36-year-old Kovalev in the eleventh round to capture the WBO belt. That victory remains a cornerstone of his four-division resume, keeping any future venture at light heavyweight open to legitimate discussion.

If Canelo truly cleaned out 168 and sits on a throne where nobody at super middleweight is worthy, then stepping up to fight Artur Beterbiev is the exact test he should take.

The critics who instantly rule out a Beterbiev clash point to size, power, and danger. Yet those same excuses vanish whenever people praise Canelo for jumping straight to light heavyweight in 2019 to take out Sergey Kovalev. If handling the physical jump to 175 was good enough to claim a belt back then, using size as a shield today doesn’t work. Canelo already established that he will willingly step into the ring against a light heavyweight champion when an opportunity presents itself.

The timing makes the matchup entirely fair game. Beterbiev is past 40, carrying the heavy mileage, wear, and physical toll of a brutal, extended career. When Canelo moved up to dethrone Kovalev, he targeted a 36-year-old champion with clear vulnerabilities. Facing a 41-year-old Beterbiev fits the identical blueprint. If Canelo’s supporters argue that Beterbiev’s age is catching up to him, then Canelo has zero excuses to avoid testing those waters.

Ruling the fight out gives Canelo a convenient pass to linger in safe territory. Instead of entertaining another slow, uneventful outing against Terence Crawford or settling for predictable matchups at super middleweight, Canelo ought to prove his greatness where the stakes are genuine. If he were brave enough to hunt Kovalev at 175, ruling out an aging Beterbiev looks less like caution and more like dodging a fight that would truly test his limits.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Calls Haney’s Knockout Talk A Bluff
Sports.content:
Liam Paro expects Devin Haney to abandon his knockout talk once they fight, leaving the Australian needing to create punching opportunities against an opponent he believes will avoid sustained trading.

Paro would welcome Haney standing with him. His preparations, however, must account for the cautious approach he expects rather than the aggressive one Haney has promised.

“I believe Haney is one of the hardest tasks, just his style. He’s not going to be there to engage. But look, he said that he’s looking for a knockout. I guarantee I’ll beat him in a firefight, but I know he’s not going to do that. He’s a good boxer,” said Paro to the Punch Podcast.

The first problem is getting past Haney’s jab without spending rounds following him. As a southpaw, Paro can contest that punch with his lead right hand, tapping or occupying Haney’s left to disrupt his ability to judge distance. That could help Paro bring his rear left into range without having to rush through a clean jab.

There is a cost to reaching for that control. If Paro becomes preoccupied with Haney’s lead hand, he can leave an opening for the straight right. His hand fighting needs to accompany his footwork, giving him a route to attack rather than becoming an exercise Haney can read.

Paro also needs to distinguish pressure from pursuit. Following Haney around the perimeter would allow the American to choose when to stop, punch, and move again. Short diagonal steps across his route would make Haney change direction or surrender space toward the ropes.

The straight left to the body could help there. Paro does not have to reach Haney’s head with every attack to make his movement less comfortable. Targeting the torso gives him a chance to score beneath the jab and draw a defensive reaction that creates his next opening. Overreaching would leave him vulnerable to a counter or a clinch.

What happens after Haney punches could be just as valuable. Paro needs to position himself to answer before Haney has completed his retreat. A short right hook or a straight left may catch an exit, but only if Paro remains balanced enough to throw immediately. Loading up would let the opportunity disappear.

Paro estimates they have shared close to 100 rounds of sparring. That experience could help him recognize when Haney intends to move, hold, or counter. It also means Haney has substantial knowledge of Paro’s approach. Familiarity becomes an advantage only if Paro can disguise what he does next.

His first-round knockout of Brock Jarvis demonstrates the danger when he lands cleanly. It does less to explain how he will manufacture that opening against Haney.

Paro’s clearest route is to make brief encounters productive: interfere with the jab, close space without reaching, and score before Haney gets clear. If he can do that consistently, he can win rounds without needing Haney to accept the firefight he expects him to refuse.

Sports.title: Melikuziev Crushes Sharipov To Keep Munguia Fight On Track
Sports.content:
Bektemir Melikuziev cleared his final obstacle before an expected world-title shot, knocking out Karomatullo Sharipov in the second round Friday night at Nikki Beach Resort in Dubai. The WBA mandatory challenger finished his overmatched opponent quickly, keeping his pursuit of super middleweight champion Jaime Munguia on course.

Uzbekistan’s Melikuziev (18-1, 12 KOs) needed less than two rounds to finish Tajikistan’s Sharipov (4-4-1, 3 KOs) in the main event of MUKA Boxing’s “Fury by the Sea” card. The scheduled four-round bout marked Melikuziev’s return after more than eight months out of the ring.

The decisive moment came late in the second round. Melikuziev landed a heavy shot that sent Sharipov flat onto his back, bringing the fight to an end. There was no recovery from the knockdown, and the 30-year-old southpaw had completed the immediate task in front of him.

Melikuziev pressed forward in the available second-round footage, finding opportunities to land clean power punches despite brief clinches and return fire. Sharipov could not keep the more experienced contender from getting into punching range, and the difference in their power became decisive before the round ended.

It was the result Melikuziev needed from a fight with limited competitive upside. Sharipov entered with only four professional victories, making this a substantial drop from the opposition the Uzbek contender must beat to become a world champion. A quick knockout met expectations, although it offered little evidence about how Melikuziev will handle a sustained fight against Munguia.

The practical benefit was ending his inactivity. Melikuziev had not fought since stopping Sena Agbeko in seven rounds in February. With his championship opportunity still awaiting a date, Friday’s appearance gave him another training camp and a short spell under fight conditions without committing him to a lengthy contest.

His title claim was already established. The WBA ranks Melikuziev No. 1 at super middleweight and previously ordered Munguia to defend against him. The organization subsequently permitted Munguia to face Nikita Zon on October 31, with the requirement that the winner face Melikuziev next.

Munguia retained his belt by unanimous decision, but his difficult sixth round against Zon gives the mandatory challenger reason for encouragement. Zon hurt the champion badly before Munguia recovered and took control over the second half. Melikuziev’s power makes those defensive openings a concern for Munguia, even allowing for the considerable difference between Friday’s opponent and a reigning champion.

The Ring reported earlier this week that a deal is in place for Munguia to face Melikuziev, although a date and venue have yet to be determined. Friday’s knockout leaves the challenger available to move toward that fight.

For Melikuziev, the title opportunity would represent the biggest step in a rebuilding run that began after Gabriel Rosado knocked him out in 2021. The 2016 Olympic silver medalist later avenged that defeat on points and has now won 11 consecutive fights.

Sharipov was never likely to provide the examination Munguia will. Melikuziev nevertheless did what a leading contender should against this level of opponent: he ended the fight early. The next question is whether he can produce the same damaging offense against a champion capable of surviving trouble and fighting back.

Sports.title: Johnny Fisher’s Kristian Prenga Target Could Backfire Horribly
Sports.content:
Johnny Fisher is flirting with disaster by targeting Kristian Prenga for his planned late-February return. Two confidence-building wins against Ivan Balaz and Michael Pirotton may have steadied the ship after his May 2025 stoppage loss to Dave Allen, but stepping straight into the pocket with the man who put Anthony Joshua on the canvas twice is a massive leap in lethality.

Fisher openly favors Prenga over former IBF titleholder Charles Martin, drawn primarily to the marquee value of the Albanian’s recent high-profile outing.

“I think Prenga would be a good one because he’s fought recently against Joshua,” Fisher told EverythingBoxing.

While that Joshua link offers undeniable promotional appeal, it also provides every reason for his corner to slam the brakes on. Prenga proved in July that he possesses sudden, fight-altering power by flooring Joshua twice in the opening round before being halted in the second. If Joshua struggled to stay upright under that initial barrage, Fisher’s punch resistance will face immediate trial.

The issue stems directly from how Fisher operates inside the ropes. His trademark front-foot assault demands constant forward momentum, letting his hands go in high-volume bursts. That aggressive approach requires meticulous defensive exits. Every exchange demands a snapped-back high guard, a sharp change of angle, or a clean exit out of range. Fisher cannot afford to linger in the pocket to hunt for an extra punch. Lingering against Prenga is an invitation for disaster.

Prenga’s failure to finish Joshua in the second round exposed his own tactical flaws, notably an apparent reluctance to press his advantage when his opponent needed time to clear the fog. Some attributed that hesitation to early fatigue from emptying the tank, while others saw it as costly indecision. Fisher cannot build an entire game plan on the hope that Prenga lets another hurt man off the hook. Slipping shots, disrupting Prenga’s rhythm, and forcing misses remain far safer than trading bombs in the pocket.

Martin offers an entirely different, perhaps more educational test. Dealing with Martin’s southpaw stance, deceptive reach, and straight left hand would force Fisher to sharpen his footwork and spatial awareness. While Martin still carries punch power, his style tests tactical discipline rather than delivering the raw, explosive trauma Prenga brings to the opening bell.

Fisher deserves praise for targeting a live wire, but Zuffa must weigh whether his defensive adjustments are genuinely ready for this level of fire. Another devastating stoppage loss would undo his rebuilding progress, leaving the promotion with a badly damaged asset whose flaws were exposed by the very first puncher capable of exploiting them.

Sports.title: Mora Warns Joshua Buatsi: Stop Brawling with Hutchinson
Sports.content:
Sergio Mora argues Joshua Buatsi can simplify his rematch with Willy Hutchinson by sticking to a disciplined jab and compelling the counterpuncher to initiate the action. The difficulty lies in implementing that strategy without muting the devastating rib attack that defines Buatsi, or getting dragged into brawling the moment Hutchinson scores.

Two knockdowns secured the verdict for Buatsi in their first encounter, yet Mora insists the Londoner gave away unnecessary openings by working inside the telephone booth. The former world champion urges Buatsi to command distance, bag rounds on the scorecards, and make the Scotsman gamble.

“Buatsi can make it so easy for himself. I know he’s a great body puncher, and he makes fights entertaining. But he can make this fight so easy if he uses more boxing than fighting, and he fights a little bit longer. If he pops behind the jab. Let Hutchinson make the mistakes because Hutchinson, he’s a good fighter, he’s a good counter-puncher, but he’s a reactive fighter. He’s not a go-get-you fighter,” said Mora to DAZN Boxing.

Strategic compromises exist within that blueprint. Hooking to the body requires closing the gap through the danger zone where Hutchinson’s hand speed can intercept incoming fire. Boxing at range shields Buatsi from check hooks, yet it inevitably caps the number of flush shots he can sink downstairs.

Stabbing jabs into Hutchinson’s chest and solar plexus provides an answer. Buatsi can disrupt breathing without smothering his own reach, keeping the target moving while assessing whether heavier artillery should follow. The body work shifts from an all-out physical press into an earned sequence.

Sharper feints also disrupt a reactive opponent. Buatsi has no obligation to commit fully with every twitch. Subtle level changes and shoulder feints will pull Hutchinson out of his stance, leaving him off balance when he reaches for air.

None of this functions without banking early points. Hutchinson will gladly sit back if he is allowed to dictate the pace from the outside. Mora’s scenario of a stoppage depends on Hutchinson feeling desperate enough on the scorecards to march forward into incoming traffic.

“So if Buatsi can win some early rounds and get Hutchinson to come at him, I could see Buatsi running him into a right hand and hurting him, and dropping him and maybe stopping him,” said Mora.

Securing ring center anchors this entire setup. Forcing Hutchinson to circle eats away at the Scotsman’s legs while preserving Buatsi’s stamina for the late rounds. An active lead hand must continually penalize every reset.

Temperament presents the true obstacle. The moment Hutchinson lands an eye-catching flurry, Buatsi must fight his natural urge to fire back instantly in the pocket. Stepping back behind the jab after tasting leather will reveal whether Buatsi values tactical efficiency over raw violence.

Buatsi faces Hutchinson in a rematch for the vacant WBC light heavyweight title this Saturday, November 7, at Manchester’s AO Arena, live on DAZN.

Sports.title: Outbox or Get Cracked: Shane Mosley’s Bentley Gamble
Sports.content:
Shane Mosley Jr. needed two trips to the scale on Friday, sweating off a stubborn final pound to reach the 160-pound limit after coming in at 161. That extra hour in the sauna creates immediate questions about his legs, particularly against a puncher like London’s Denzel Bentley over 10 rounds at the Copper Box Arena. Bentley checked in right on the mark at 160 on his first try.

Mosley’s stated strategy depends on superior activity and sustained output. With a five-inch reach advantage, his cleanest route to a points win is operating behind a busy, disciplining jab to trap Bentley on the perimeter. But if Friday’s late weight cut robs Mosley of fluid lateral movement, Bentley will not have to work hard to close the distance.

Middleweight madness incoming 👀 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 @2Sharp_D – 160lbs

🇺🇸 @IamShaneMosley – 160lbs 📺 @SkySports + @ParamountPlus | #ZuffaBoxing12 https://t.co/E1Rvtw2vJI — Zuffa_Boxing (@Zuffa_Boxing) November 6, 2026

Mosley made his intentions clear this week, saying that a points victory in hostile territory holds more value for him than an early finish:

“The reason why I feel like it’s even better to beat you on points than to knock you out is because if I can show everybody in here, everybody in the arena that I’m better than you, that’s better to me than knocking you out,” Mosley said to Sky Sports Boxing sit down. “What’s better is if I went to your hometown and in front of your fans and beat you convincingly, where everybody said, ‘Yeah, he won.’ That to me shows greatness.”

Aiming to win a clear decision on British cards requires a dominant volume gap, especially against a hometown fighter. Scraping by on split margins fails the standard of mastery Mosley outlined.

Bentley was initially unfazed by the prediction before recognizing the tactical insult behind it.

“At first I thought, ‘All right.’ I went back and I thought, ‘Wait, I’d rather he say he’d knock me out,’” Bentley admitted. “He’s basically saying he can outpoint me.” His response was blunt: “That’s not happening.”

For Bentley, winning does not require round-by-round territorial dominance. He carries an 82% knockout rate and thrives when opponents throw in prolonged combinations, creating counter-punching lanes for his right hand. If Mosley’s punch output dips in the middle rounds from dehydration, Bentley’s heavy single shots will stand out sharply on the scorecards.

“I want to crack that chin. I want to see if it’s real. Watch,” Bentley said.

Bentley has acknowledged Mosley’s chin and ring experience, so a wild blitz out of the gate is unlikely. Even with the WBO belt absent after Bentley opted for this bout over a mandatory assignment, the terms of the fight are clear: Mosley must execute a disciplined, 10-round boxing clinic at range, while Bentley needs only one sustained opening to punish him on the inside.

Sports.title: Groves Expects Fury vs Joshua Despite Fury Injury Rumor
Sports.content:
George Groves fully expects Tyson Fury to step into the ring against Anthony Joshua, brushing off chatter that an injury could derail the December 11 date. His view is simple. Both men are battle-worn veterans, so expecting either to show up at one hundred percent is unrealistic.

The conversation kicked off after Frank Bruno claimed an insider from Fury’s gym told him an injury could stop the clash from happening. Groves did not have insider details on Fury’s body, yet he cast heavy doubt on the idea that the event is actually in jeopardy.

“I don’t know about any rumors, but there might be a lot of kidology, a lot of rumors floating about. Could have been leaked by anyone,” Groves told talkSPORT Boxing. “I genuinely don’t know, but I’ll be very shocked if that fight don’t happen. I think both guys will fight no matter what.”

Groves offered an unfiltered take on where both boxers stand right now. He views them as past their physical primes, meaning a completely smooth camp is out of the question for either side.

“I don’t think at this stage either one of these two guys who are veterans, way past their best, are going to be in perfect condition going into this fight. That doesn’t matter. They’re going to fight,” Groves said.

It is a harsh reality check for an all-British heavyweight meeting years in the making. Fans are getting the spectacle, but Groves points out that the clock has been ticking the whole time.

Looking back on his own ring days, Groves pointed out that modern training camps are never completely clean. Wear and tear, missed sessions, or personal distractions always creep in, no matter how sharp someone looks at the podium.

Whether Fury carries a genuine knock remains unconfirmed. Bruno’s story is secondhand talk, and Groves made it clear he has no direct intel. Still, Groves remains convinced that both heavyweights will walk through fire to make the bell.

When a guaranteed nine-figure bag is sitting on the table, standard training camp knocks take a back seat.

Walking away from a projected 100 million dollars each over an elbow tweak, sore shoulder, or bruised rib would be professional madness. At this stage of their careers, neither Tyson Fury nor Anthony Joshua has another payday of this magnitude waiting in reserve.

If one pulls out now with a minor complaint, there is zero guarantee the momentum, public appetite, or financial backing survives to reschedule it cleanly.

Both fighters have operated under fire while compromised before. Fury fought through severe cuts and facial trauma, while Joshua has spent years managing the mileage on his body. Every veteran north of thirty-five carries something into the ring; reaching fight night at one hundred percent physical perfection is a myth in modern heavyweight boxing.

Unless one of them suffers a catastrophic structural tear or a medical commission flat-out denies a license, they are walking to the ring on December 11 in Cardiff. At 100 million dollars apiece, you fight through the aches, take your shot, and settle whatever needs healing after the final bell.

Sports.title: Fury: Ryan Garcia Has The Star Power Haney And Shakur Lack
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury believes Ryan Garcia is primed to take over as the premier attraction in American boxing once Canelo Alvarez steps away. Fury points directly to Garcia’s charisma and gift for commanding headlines, putting pure drawing power ahead of pure technical mastery.

While Fury listed talents like Devin Haney, Shakur Stevenson, Abdullah Mason, and Richardson Hitchins, Garcia earned his clear vote. The challenge facing everyone else is something victories in the ring cannot automatically fix: reaching beyond the hardcore boxing bubble.

“Other than Canelo, which Canelo’s obviously on his way out too, then it’s Ryan Garcia in America,” Fury said on Behind the Mic. “He’s got a personality. He talks. He’s entertaining. He’s charismatic.”

Asked if he sees reflections of himself in Garcia, Fury agreed completely, admitting others might possess sharper fundamentals but insisting they cannot generate the same revenue.

It is a crucial division when assessing Canelo’s commercial heir. Observers can debate Garcia’s ring craft against elite competition, yet Fury focuses strictly on ticket sales and viewer attention. Boxing culture often conflates technical brilliance with stardom, even though they demand completely different skill sets.

Garcia keeps the public talking during long layoffs. His unpredictable persona draws viewers who would never bother watching sparring footage or checking divisional rankings. People tune in hoping to see him win or desperate to watch him get knocked out, but either motivation sells pay-per-views.

Fury sounded far more skeptical about the mainstream presence of other top contenders.

“Inside of boxing people know who they are,” Fury said. “Outside of boxing, you go and ask 50 people … they don’t know who they are.”

Haney, Stevenson, Mason, and Hitchins have built formidable resumes. Yet Fury argues that respect from devoted boxing circles will only carry an athlete to a certain ceiling. Becoming the marquee figure who causes general sports fans to clear their weekend calendars demands a bigger presence.

Fury also took aim at modern streaming setups, questioning whether current platforms actually build true mainstream excitement. He recalled previous eras where extensive profile features introduced contenders long before fight night, whereas modern streaming formats often show the event without making casual viewers care in advance.

Because of that shift, self-promotion falls squarely on the fighter. Fury stressed that young talent must chase interviews, drop consistent content, and hustle for their own spotlight instead of waiting for a promoter to do the heavy lifting.

Garcia naturally excels at that playbook. Pure spectacle does not guarantee long-term dominance, since keeping the public invested still requires memorable bouts and dependable results. Even so, Fury’s view holds firm: Garcia knows how to hook an audience before the first bell sounds, while his peers face a much steeper climb proving they can match that commercial reach.

Ghana News.title: Fire destroys Agbogba restaurant near Yellow Container
Ghana News.content:
Firefighters on Friday, November 6, 2026, battled a fiercely spreading inferno that completely destroyed a restaurant near the popular Yellow Container landmark at Agbogba in Accra.

The destructive blaze, which broke out during the day, sent thick plumes of smoke into the sky, drawing crowds of anxious onlookers and threatening nearby properties.

Responding to distress calls, operational teams from the Madina Fire Station, reinforced by crews from the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) Headquarters, were quickly deployed to the scene to bring the situation under control.

Through a coordinated effort, the firefighters managed to contain the flames and prevent the blaze from spreading to adjoining commercial structures in the densely populated neighborhood.

The GNFS has commenced preliminary investigations to ascertain the exact cause of the outbreak.

Ghana News.title: Zenith SME Business Empowerment Lab: SMEs urged to identify business risks and adopt mitigation strategies to ensure sustainability
Ghana News.content:
Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have been encouraged to adopt proactive risk management practices as a critical step toward building resilient, sustainable businesses capable of withstanding unforeseen challenges.

According to the experts, business resilience goes beyond responding to crises. It requires a deliberate and strategic approach to identifying potential vulnerabilities, safeguarding critical operations and implementing contingency measures that enable businesses to adapt, recover and thrive in the face of disruptions.

The call was made by industry experts during the third edition of Zenith Bank Ghana's SME Business Empowerment Lab, held virtually on Thursday, October 29, 2026, under the theme, "Building a Resilient and Disaster-Proof Business."

Warning signs

Speaking at the webinar, the Chief Operating Officer of the Ghana Incentive-Based Risk-Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (GIRSAL), Samuel Yeboah identified six major business red flags, categorised into internal and external risks. “While internal risks include poor cash flow, rising debt, inadequate record-keeping and weak governance structures, external risks comprise excessive dependence on a single buyer or supplier, unmanaged climate-related threats and declining product quality”.

Drawing attention to agricultural SMEs, Mr. Yeboah explained that climate shocks, fluctuations in production costs, delayed payments from buyers and biological hazards could significantly disrupt business operations. He particularly cautioned against overdependence on a single customer or supplier, stressing the importance of diversifying business relationships to minimise potential losses.

To address these vulnerabilities, he outlined a five-step business resilience plan, encouraging SMEs to identify their most significant risks, assess their financial implications, develop appropriate response measures, assign clear responsibilities and regularly review their contingency plans.

He further emphasised the importance of maintaining accurate financial records and establishing alternative suppliers and buyers to strengthen business continuity.

Economic stability

Also addressing participants, the Chief Operating Officer of the Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GNCCI), Frederick Adu-Amoako urged SMEs to take advantage of periods of economic stability to strengthen their preparedness against potential business disruptions.

Citing Ghana's improving economic indicators, including declining inflation and Treasury bill rates, he emphasised that favourable economic conditions should provide an opportunity for businesses to build resilience ahead of future uncertainties.

He identified natural disasters, cyber threats, supply chain disruptions, reputational damage and regulatory challenges among the risks businesses must anticipate and prepare to manage.

To mitigate these risks, Mr. Adu-Amoako encouraged entrepreneurs to develop a simple, one-page crisis management plan outlining potential threats, critical business operations, emergency contacts and staff responsibilities.

He further stressed the importance of maintaining backup records, protecting financial resources and ensuring employees are adequately prepared to respond to emergencies.

He also highlighted the GNCCI's role in strengthening business resilience through advocacy, capacity building, business networking and access to market opportunities.

He added that the Chamber engages government and regulatory institutions on issues affecting businesses while facilitating partnerships and market expansion opportunities for entrepreneurs.

Insurance

Speaking on the role of insurance in business resilience, the Head of Alternative Distribution and Customer Experience at Hollard Insurance Ghana, Yvonne Dowuona underscored the importance of insurance as a critical risk mitigation tool for SMEs, urging business owners to adequately protect their operations against unforeseen losses.

She emphasised the need for entrepreneurs to accurately assess the value of their business assets and select appropriate insurance policies that provide sufficient coverage for their specific risks.

She further encouraged SMEs to consider insurance protection for their properties, business operations, liabilities and lives to minimise their financial exposure in the event of unexpected disruptions.

Ms. Dowuona also advised business owners to regularly review the scope of their insurance coverage and renew their policies annually to ensure they remain adequately protected as their businesses evolve.

She stressed the importance of aligning insurance coverage with the changing needs and risks of businesses to support long-term sustainability.

About the Zenith SME Business Empowerment Lab

This edition marks the third webinar in the Zenith SME Business Empowerment Lab series for the year, further extending the Bank’s efforts to provide SMEs with relevant knowledge and practical insights to support different aspects of their business operations.

The first and second editions explored the themes “Building Stronger Businesses: Unlocking Zenith Bank’s SME Ecosystem” and “Building a Sustainable Business in a Changing Economy – Legal and Regulatory Essentials for Small Businesses”, respectively, addressing key areas critical to business growth, sustainability and compliance.

Through these engagements, the Zenith SME Business Empowerment Lab continues to serve as a platform for knowledge exchange, capacity development and practical business education. Ultimately, the initiative seeks to contribute to a stronger SME sector, with better-equipped enterprises that are positioned to innovate, compete, create employment and play a greater role in Ghana’s economic development.

Ghana News.title: Policy rate of 14% between May and September 2026 was meant to preserve economic stability – BoG Governor
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Asiama

The Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr. Johnson Asiama, has strongly defended the decision by the Monetary Policy Committee to hold the policy rate at 14% between May and September 2026.

According to him, the Committee’s action is to preserve economic stability despite unfavourable external conditions, including rising global oil prices and domestic price pressures.

The Governor disclosed this when he appeared before the Parliamentary Committee on Economy and Development to update Parliament on the Monetary Policy and Macro-Economic Developments in the first half of 2026.

The clarification by the Governor is coming at a time when some market analysts had pushed for a rate cut because inflation during the period declined, whilst other macroeconomic conditions improved.

At the last Monetary Policy Committee Meeting in September 2026, the majority of the MPC members cited external risks to the economy and concerns about rising inflation as one of the major reasons for the steady policy rate.

Fiscal and Economic development

Dr. Johnson Asiama also took the opportunity to explain to the Committee the workings of the Bank of Ghana, and how the fiscal authorities had played a major role in helping Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth to hit 6.4% in the first quarter of this year, while inflation fell to 3.2% in March 2026 and remained below the 6-10% target band.

The Governor also mentioned the developments in the external sector, saying it has been good, with “Ghana recording a trade surplus of US$8.81 billion and a current account surplus of US$5.1 billion”.

He also intimated that “The country’s international reserves reached US$12.94 billion, equivalent to 5.0 months of import cover".

On the banking front, Dr. Asiama highlighted how interest rates and credit conditions have improved, with the average lending rate dropping from 27% to 15.6% while private sector credit grew by 41.2 %.

Total Assets in the banking sector, the Governor stated, rose by 30.7% to reach GH¢502.4 billion, while the Capital Adequacy Ratio also stood at 20.4%, with Non-Performing Loans declining to16.1% from 23.1%.

The Bank of Ghana Governor also talked about some key reforms that have taken place, including a uniform cash ratio of 20%, a transparent and rules-based foreign exchange intervention framework and the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Programme (GANRAP), which actually targets 15 months of import cover by 2028.

Dr. Asiama concluded, expressing his outfit's commitment to price stability, transparency and accountability to Parliament and the people of Ghana

Ghana News.title: ‘Days of diverting cocoa inputs are over’ – COCOBOD CEO
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) has issued a stern warning to individuals and officials involved in the diversion, hoarding or illegal sale of free fertiliser and other farm inputs, saying a new digital monitoring system will make it easier to identify and prosecute offenders.

Chief Executive Officer of COCOBOD, Dr Randy Abbey, said the days when inputs intended for cocoa farmers could be diverted without detection were over, following the introduction of a digital tracking mechanism under the relaunched Free Fertiliser Distribution Programme.

Addressing farmers and stakeholders at the relaunch in Sefwi Wiawso in the Western North Region, he said the system would track every consignment from the point it left a warehouse until it reached the farmer for whom it was intended.

“Let me send a clear and unequivocal warning to smugglers and saboteurs. The days of diverting inputs meant for our farmers are over. Any officer, buyer, or individual found diverting, hoarding, reselling, or smuggling these inputs will be dealt with according to the law,” he said.

Dr Abbey said the digital system was being deployed to close loopholes that had allowed subsidised and free agricultural inputs to find their way onto the open market, or be smuggled across borders instead of reaching cocoa-growing communities.

Under the new arrangement, eligibility will be restricted to registered cocoa farmers whose farms have been mapped and recorded on COCOBOD’s digital Cocoa Management System (CMS).

At distribution centres, farmers will be required to establish their identities with their farmer identification cards, Ghana Cards or biometric details. The measures, he explained, were intended to prevent impersonation and eliminate fictitious names from beneficiary records.

The quantities allocated to each farmer will be determined automatically by the system, taking into account the size and condition of the farm. Distribution officers will therefore have no authority to alter individual allocations.

Every bag to be accounted for

Dr Abbey said the digital monitoring process would create a record of every consignment as it moved from warehouses to district and community distribution points.

Each bag issued would be linked to the identity of its recipient, enabling officials at the district, regional and national levels to monitor the process and identify irregularities as they occurred.

“Every bag issued is tagged against the name of the farmer who received it. At any moment, we can reconcile what was dispatched against what was received and what was issued. A bag that goes missing now leaves a trail,” he said.

He said the arrangement was expected to reduce the influence of personal connections and favouritism in the distribution of inputs, while ensuring that smallholder farmers, women, young farmers and elderly producers received their allocations without having to pay unofficial fees.

Farmers whose farms had not been captured on the CMS were urged to contact their agricultural extension officers to complete the registration and mapping process.

Dr Abbey also tasked extension officers to ensure that all cocoa farmers and their farms in their respective districts were registered and properly mapped to prevent eligible producers from being left out.

Free fertiliser policy

The COCOBOD chief executive described the shift from a 50 per cent fertiliser subsidy to the provision of free fertiliser as a significant change in the support available to cocoa farmers.

He said the policy was intended to remove the cost of fertiliser as a barrier to farm productivity and improve the capacity of farmers to maintain their farms and increase output.

The programme was relaunched under the theme, “Cocoa Sector Reset: Free Fertiliser for Increased Productivity and Improved Farmer Income”.

For his part, COCOBOD Board Chairman, Dr Samuel Ofosu Ampofo, reaffirmed the government's commitment to interventions aimed at raising cocoa production and improving the incomes of farmers.

The relaunch forms part of efforts to reset the cocoa sector, with the new tracking system expected to strengthen accountability in the distribution of inputs and ensure that the benefits reach the farmers for whom they are intended.

Ghana News.title: Sons of the sound: How Mfanstsipim incubated and nurtured Ghana’s contemporary gospel
Ghana News.content:
A School, a sound and a new movement

Contemporary gospel music emerged in Ghana in the early 1970s, marking a major development in the country’s Christian music. Churches had long used hymns, anthems, cantatas, indigenous songs and some western instruments, yet many conservative evangelicals still regarded rock, soul, disco and electric guitars as worldly.

Through Noise of Joy, Joyful Way Singers and its link with Calvary Road Singers, Mfantsipim incubated and nurtured a challenge to these attitudes, proving the value of contemporary Christian music for evangelism, fellowship and spiritual formation.

Noise of joy: The beginning of a new sound



In July 1970, guitarist Emmanuel Lartey, now the Rt Rev Prof Emmanuel Y Lartey of Emory University, formed Noise of Joy with fellow students Joseph Quist, Kwame Kyeretwie Ofori, Henry Badoo, TVO Lamptey and James Walton, joined by girls from Wesley Girls’ High School. That September, a visit by Youth For Christ’s Teen Team affirmed what the group had begun. Rather than suppress the movement, the School embraced it: because ‘Methodism was born in song,’ tutors such as W Paul Grimble and E John Watson encouraged the group to perform at services and gatherings across Cape Coast, as did Clarice Garnett of Wesley Girls’, who also guided them.

From noise of joy to Joyful Way

Parallel groups followed, notably the Evangels, led by Adisadel keyboardist Emmanuel Kweku Frimpong (‘Odas’). On 15 January 1972, Noise of Joy and the Evangels merged, combining a Beatles-style guitar sound with piano-led music reminiscent of the Edwin Hawkins Singers, a mix Professor Joe-Nat Clegg-Lamptey called ‘like dynamite!’ As Rev Joseph Gyebi observes, Joyful Way’s use of popular forms challenged prevailing evangelical attitudes and reached young people.

Taking the gospel beyond the school gates

Joyful Way toured nationally in the 1972 Nationwide Love Mission and was heard on GBC radio. In 1974 it appeared on Break For Music and launched Explosion of Joy, its Boxing Day concert, which still draws about 4,000 patrons a year and may be Africa’s longest-running annual contemporary gospel concert.

Joyful Way inspired Calvary Road Singers, founded around December 1976 with Rev Spencer Duncan as founding President. Duncan had become ‘born again’ at a Joyful Way programme at Adisadel in 1972. As Rev Ebenezer Markwei, a founding member, recalls, ‘right from the start, we wanted to be like Joyful Way.’ Later groups shared this aspiration, including New Creation, Come Back, Abundant Life, the Commissioned Family and, more recently, Team Eternity, whose founder calls Joyful Way ‘a template.’

Joyful Way and Calvary Road: Completing each other

Calvary Road combined music with drama, prayer and preaching. Dr Kwame Owusu Dapaah-Afriyie introduced it to Mfantsipim around 1980, and it grew into a network of campus ministries.

At Mfantsipim, a friendly, sometimes competitive rivalry fostered musical talent and leadership, producing a strong line of vocalists, keyboardists, guitarists and drummers. As Kojo Folson (Borax) – former Deputy Headboy, Calvary Road member and possibly Mfantsipim’s finest guitarist – puts it, ‘we did not necessarily compete with each other; we completed each other.’

Changing scenes and shifting tides

From the mid-1980s, the groups’ fortunes in Cape Coast declined. Joyful Way decided to close its branches in 1985, and the Cape Coast branch’s attempt to survive was dealt a fatal blow in 1986, when it was banned from Wesley Girls’ after a disputed service. The Adisadel branch gradually faded, but the Mfantsipim branch carried on as Joyful Noise, forming affiliations with groups at Ghana National and Wesley Girls’, and resumed its original name when Joyful Way reversed its decision around 1996.

Calvary Road, by contrast, was swept up in the charismatic church wave of the late 1980s and 1990s. More than a dozen churches emerged from it or were founded by its members, including Lighthouse Chapel, Living Streams, Harvest Chapel and New Creation Chapel, though its influence as an independent music ministry has since dwindled.

From school groups to national artistes

As noted, the groups produced notable musicians. From Joyful Way came TVO Lamptey, a leading gospel tenor; Patrick Osei-Hwere, arguably Ghana’s first recorded gospel rapper who also helped found Intellecto Choirofest, the inter-university mass choir festival; vocalists such as Luigi Maclean, Calvis Hammond, Seth Acquah, Elvis Bentil and Nana Yaw Ofori-Atta; and songwriters such as TVO Lamptey (Wonjie Oyi), Sackey Bennin (Osabarima), Justice Akushie (I’ve Found It) and the present writer (Wahenni). The Calvary Road tradition produced award-winners Nii Okai and the late Kofi Dua-Anto (KODA). Other old boys emerged outside the two traditions, notably Perez Music, a 2023 Vodafone Ghana Music Awards winner, trumpeter Frank Guildford and Rev Joseph Gyebi.

Joyful Way’s honours include the 1988 ECRAG and 1990 PAFAM awards and recognition at the 2003 Ghana Music Awards for its ministry and the packaging of Barima Yesu, written by the present writer. Its tours have reached West Africa, the United Kingdom, Germany, the United States and Rwanda, and its 1979 visit to The Gambia led to the founding of Youth For Christ, Gambia.

A living legacy at 150

Mfantsipim’s musical traditions, including Joyful Way and Calvary Road, have shaped alumni in ministry and secular careers alike, building discipline, teamwork, leadership and Christian service.

On Saturdays, young men still rehearse in Mfantsipim’s Assembly Hall as Joyful Way, the Mfantsipim group, probably unaware of the history behind each session. Calvary Road’s legacy lives on through its churches and leaders. Ironically, churches that once resisted Joyful Way’s style now routinely use contemporary gospel music in worship. As Mfantsipim turns 150, its story honours the sons of the School who transformed not only the sound of Ghana’s gospel music, but also how faith is expressed and lived.

[A fuller version of this article will be published in the Mfantsipim Speechday brochure]

The author is Ace Anan Ankomah, Esq, FGA (MOBA’84), Lawyer and Music Hobbyist

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian singer Efya marries Nigerian star Tomi Thomas
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian singer Efya Nokturnal and Nigerian musician Tomi Thomas have formalised their union in a colourful traditional marriage ceremony in Accra, bringing together music, fashion and cultural traditions from both countries.

The ceremony, held on Friday, November 6, 2026, attracted a host of personalities from the entertainment industry, politics and traditional leadership, as the couple celebrated their marriage ahead of their scheduled white wedding.

Efya, known for her powerful vocals and hit songs, made a striking appearance in a specially designed Kente gown that paid homage to her Ghanaian heritage.

Her husband also embraced the occasion’s cultural theme, choosing a richly woven Ghanaian Kente cloth complemented by gold accessories. His arrival, accompanied by an entourage and traditional musicians, added to the excitement surrounding the celebration.

The ceremony offered a blend of Ghanaian and Nigerian influences, with the couple’s backgrounds reflected in the attire, music and festivities.

Among the prominent guests were Minister of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Dzifa Abla Gomashie, and the Paramount Chief of Akuapem, Oseadeeyo Kwasi Akuffo III.

The entertainment fraternity was also strongly represented, with Efia Odo, Sister Derby, Salma Mumin, Fantana and Becca among the celebrities who attended.

Music formed a major part of the celebration, as guests danced to a mix of highlife classics and contemporary Afrobeats.

The traditional marriage marks a significant milestone in the couple’s relationship, with preparations now turning to their white wedding, scheduled for Saturday, November 7, 2026, in Accra.

Ghana News.title: Ghana loses $6.5bn in potential mining revenue – IFS
Ghana News.content:
The country loses an estimated $6.56 billion in potential revenue from the mining sector every year due to the government’s limited participation in mineral extraction, the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) has revealed.

The institute explained that the country could have generated that additional money from mining in 2025 if its revenue generation from the sector had matched Botswana’s performance due to its active involvement in the sector.

The Executive Director of the IFS, Dr Said Boakye, who made this known at a policy briefing on low government revenue mobilisation in Accra yesterday, said the situation reflected the country’s inability to maximise returns from its considerable mineral resources, and, therefore, asked the authorities to use the upcoming 2027 Budget to correct the leakage.

Dr Boakye further identified revenue leakages, including tax evasion, underreporting, tax avoidance and collusion involving revenue administrators, as major factors undermining domestic revenue mobilisation.

He cited revelations by the Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority, Anthony Sarpong, in April 2026 that the country had lost more than GH¢11 billion in revenue at its ports through incorrect declarations involving the country of origin, classification and valuation of imported goods.

He said the low government revenue mobilisation had constrained the country’s ability to finance development.

Dr Boakye added that the country’s total revenue and grants-to-GDP ratio stood at 15.7 per cent in 2022, against the average of 20.1 per cent for 25 sub-Saharan African countries examined in the IFS report.

The institute estimated that Ghana would have collected GH¢288.26 billion in total revenue and grants in 2025 if its revenue-to-GDP ratio had matched the sub-Saharan African average, compared with the actual collection of GH¢224.88 billion.

Poor performance

The figure, he said, placed Ghana 18th among the 25 countries, highlighting the country’s relatively poor performance compared with its regional peers.

Comparing the systems in Ghana to Botswana’s, for instance, he said the southern African country generated $13.4 billion in value added from mining in 2025, while Ghana’s revenue from the sector amounted to only $1.6 billion, representing 11.9 per cent of the sector’s value.

He said if it had generated mining revenue at Botswana’s average rate of 60.9 per cent, the government would have earned $8.16 billion instead of the $1.6 billion collected.

Dr Boakye attributed Botswana’s stronger performance to the government’s active involvement in the mining sector through partnerships with private companies.

He explained that such arrangements enabled Botswana to benefit from corporate income taxes, dividends and royalties, while gaining better insight into the operations and profitability of mining companies.

“The government of Botswana does not only earn large corporate income tax revenue from mining because it has an insider knowledge of mining operations and profitability, it earns even larger revenue from dividend payments and royalties,” he said.

He contrasted the arrangement with Ghana’s concession-based system, under which private companies largely undertake mineral extraction, leaving the government with limited access to information about their operations and profitability.

Dr Boakye said the revenue shortfall had serious implications for public investment and the country’s debt situation.

“The low government revenue mobilisation usually leads to shortage of money to fund the government’s developmental projects, making it resort to borrowing. This has led to frequent large debt build-ups, high debt service costs, and fiscal or debt crisis,” he stated.

Tax exemptions

Dr Boakye further identified excessive tax exemptions granted to businesses as another factor contributing to the country’s weak revenue performance.

The report cited incentives under the Free Zones regime and the automotive industry development policy, which offered businesses tax holidays, import duty exemptions and other fiscal concessions.

Dr Boakye said the Ghana Investment Promotion Centre’s incentives inventory lists 31 income tax, customs and financial incentive packages available to businesses across various sectors.

Recommendation

To address the challenges, Dr Boakye recommended greater government participation in the extractive sector through direct investment and partnerships with private companies.

He also proposed production-sharing agreements as an alternative to the existing concession arrangements, saying such agreements would provide the government with better returns from the exploitation of the country’s natural resources.

He further called for an intensified fight against corruption within tax and non-tax revenue collection agencies, alongside a review of existing tax incentive packages.

Dr Boakye urged the government to discontinue exemptions which did not make economic sense in relation to the revenue being forfeited, and to rely more on improvements in the macroeconomic and political environment to attract investment.

Ghana News.title: Man allegedly spends 3 days in cemetery coffin in suspected money ritual at Foase
Ghana News.content:
A bizarre discovery at a cemetery in Foase in the Atwima Kwanwoma District of the Ashanti Region has left residents unsettled after a hunter reportedly found a 28-year-old drug store operator inside a coffin.

The man, identified only as Foster, was discovered on Thursday, November 5, 2026, in a coffin placed in an open area of the community's cemetery.

Residents suspect that he may have been engaged in a money ritual, although the circumstances surrounding his presence at the cemetery remain unclear.

According to information gathered, the hunter was passing through the cemetery when he noticed the coffin and became suspicious because it had been left exposed.

His dogs reportedly approached the coffin, prompting him to draw his gun and threaten to shoot whoever might be inside.

A resident who recounted the incident said the threat forced the occupant to emerge.

“After seeing the coffin, his dogs ran to the coffin, so the hunter pointed his gun at the coffin and threatened to shoot whoever is in it, only for the man to come out of it,” the resident said.

A herbalist who was also in the vicinity, reportedly on his way to gather herbs, joined the hunter in bringing the man into the community.

Their arrival attracted a crowd of residents, many of whom gathered to establish what had happened. Some called for police intervention.

The discovery has fuelled speculation among residents, with claims that Foster had allegedly spent three days inside the coffin as part of a suspected money-making ritual.

The man was subsequently handed over to the police to assist with investigations into the incident.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: ‘Alien-cortical’ mice: Can human brain cells grow inside animals?
World.content:
Modified mice with human brain cells ignite debates over neurohybrids and the future of cross-species medical research.

In a laboratory in California, in the United States, mice are scurrying around their cages, as mice do. But inside their brains are millions of working human neurons.

Researchers at Stanford University have implanted lab-grown human cells into mice genetically engineered to lack parts of their brains, including the cerebral cortex, the outer region that plays a major role in perception, movement, decision-making and attention.

According to a study published in Nature, these so-called “alien-cortical mice” may offer a new way to study neural circuits and brain disorders such as schizophrenia, cerebral palsy and dementia.

Putting human brain tissue inside an animal sounds like something out of Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein, but how “human” are these mice, really? And what have the researchers found?

Here is what we know.

How did the experiment work?

Researchers genetically modified the mice so they were born and grew without most of the cerebral cortex and the neighbouring hippocampus, which are needed for movement, learning and memory.

When the animals were two days old, researchers injected human “organoids” into the empty spaces. Organoids are miniature masses of cells grown in a laboratory from stem cells or tumour tissue which mimic real human organs. Each was grown from healthy donors’ stem cells and holds about 100,000 human cells.

Overall, researchers removed about 14 million mouse neurons and added about 4 million human ones.

This is not the same thing as a brain transplant, and the animals are not “mice that think like humans”, the researchers emphasised.



They tried the transplants on 29 mice, and it worked on 25 of them.

What happened to the mice?

Within three months, the human tissue had grown about five times larger inside the mice’s brains, connected to their blood supply and filled more than 90 percent of the cavities.

The “alien cortex” mice walked and vocalised mostly normally, even though human tissue made up about half their brain volume.

In a maze test, mice without the implanted human tissue kept getting lost, however, while those with human cells did better, suggesting the human tissue contributed to cognition.

Unexpectedly, some of the tissue developed into von Economo neurons, which are long, rare cells normally absent in mice and almost impossible to make in a lab. They are found in highly social animals such as humans, apes, whales and elephants.

The experiment might also help explain cerebral palsy.

While human infants can suffer from oxygen deprivation as a result of more frequent complications during much longer and trickier childbirth, mice infants rarely do, which has made the condition hard to study in rodents.

When the modified mice in this case were exposed to low oxygen, they showed brain damage, an altered gait and poor limb coordination.

Why put human neurons in a mouse?

Human brain diseases are among the hardest conditions to study. The brain contains about 86 billion nerve cells linked by trillions of connections. Ethical and safety barriers, along with the brain’s high biological complexity, limit access to living human brain tissue.

Scientists have spent years growing “organoids” instead: Small clusters of human nerve cells grown in a lab. But they are not brains in a dish. They lack the connections, inputs and environment of a living brain.

Sergiu Pasca, senior author of the research paper and a professor of psychiatry and behavioural sciences at Stanford University, said this has the potential to give researchers unprecedented insight into the human brain.

“For the past two decades, there’s been a quest to try to build models of the human brain outside of the human body,” he said.

“This is not going to replace all the models we had before, but it’s going to provide us access to other aspects of human brain function that would be very difficult to study otherwise.”

What are the ethical concerns?

As research into brain organoids advances, so too do calls for clear regulations and oversight, given the sensitive ethical questions raised by these technologies.

These questions centre on the possibility that cell clusters and brains grown outside the bodies of their owners possess the capacity for sensation or consciousness, and whether this can be scientifically verified.



The researchers stopped the experiments when the human nerve cells implanted in the brains of mice were six months old, before they could form more neural connections with the animals’ brains, and before any signs of consciousness appeared.

John Evans, a sociology professor at the University of California, San Diego, who was not involved in the study, said this experiment does not in itself raise major ethical issues, but it provides evidence that other animals could be created that might raise more serious ethical concerns.

Setting clear boundaries for this research remains a challenge.

According to Evans, the problem lies in the lack of clear stopping points on the gradual path that research could take from mice to non-human primates.

Accordingly, he suggested that researchers should not go beyond rodents for the time being, in order to avoid creating neurohybrid organisms that combine human and animal characteristics and could provoke an ethical controversy.
