Equally, the National Executive Committee Chairmen Forum of the ADC loyal to Gombe, threatened to embark on a nationwide protest against INEC if it fails to comply with Thursday’s court judgment on the party’s leadership crisis.

In a statement posted on his verified X account, Atiku said: “Let no one mistake the latest court ruling for the will of the Nigerian people. No manipulation, conjecture or concoction can erase our place in this contest, silence our campaign or deny Nigerians the right to choose their future. We are on the ballot, and the people must be allowed to decide.



“Those who boast of having thirty-two governors and claim to have bought, pressured or coerced leaders from other parties into their fold should have no reason to fear a free and fair contest. Yet, instead of presenting their record to Nigerians, they continue to deploy every tactic available to weaken the opposition: political pressure, manufactured narratives, courtroom manoeuvres and attempts to compromise the voters’ register with AI-generated photographs, false names and fictitious identities. These are not the actions of people confident in their record. They are calculated attempts to make genuine competition impossible and push Nigeria towards a one-party state.



“And what record do they have to defend? This government removed the fuel subsidy overnight without a plan to protect Nigerians. It presided over the steep decline of the naira and allowed food prices to rise beyond the reach of ordinary families. Factories and small businesses have shut their doors. Our young people are leaving in search of hope, while bandits and kidnappers continue to hold communities hostage.

“Look around you. Market stalls stand empty. Feeding your family has become a daily struggle. Fuel prices keep rising, and silent pain fills homes across the country. Those in power may want you to believe that your suffering does not matter. They may want you to surrender your future before you even reach the ballot box. Do not lose heart. Do not retreat. Your vote is your power, and together, we will take our country back.



“Let me be clear to every Nigerian who has stood with us: I am in this race. I am not going anywhere. We will be on the ballot. No threat, blackmail or court manoeuvre will make me abandon you or the cause we share.

“We will resist with all our strength every attempt to turn Nigeria into a one-party state. Nigeria belongs to all its people. Our democracy must remain open to more than one party and more than one voice. If those in power believe in their numbers and their record, let us meet at the polls in a free, fair and credible contest.



“Our campaign will continue. Our message on the cost of living will not be silenced or derailed. Stay calm, united and resolute. Together, we will fight for a Nigeria where life is affordable and every citizen’s vote counts.

“Let me say this plainly: Bola cannot use the courts to escape the judgment of Nigerians at the ballot box,” Atiku stated.

ADC Appeals Judgment, Seeks Stay, Writes INEC

The Mark-led ADC has appealed the judgment of the Federal High Court, Abuja, which sacked the party’s National Executive Committee led by Senator David Mark.

The group also applied for a stay of execution of the judgment delivered by Justice Lifu.

Barely 24 hours after the judgment, the ADC approached the Court of Appeal to challenge the decision and applied for an order halting its implementation pending the hearing and determination of the appeal.



The notice of appeal and motion for stay, dated November 6, were filed on behalf of the ADC by its team of lawyers led by Shaibu Enejoh Aruwa, SAN. The party also notified INEC of the appeal and its application for a stay of execution.

In a letter to the commission, the lawyers said: “We are counsel to the ADC, the 1st Defendant in the above-mentioned suit.

“Recall that the Federal High Court, Abuja Judicial Division, delivered its judgment in the aforementioned suit in favour of the plaintiff thereof on November 5, 2026.

“The 1st Defendant, being dissatisfied with the said judgment of the Federal High Court, has filed a Notice of Appeal against the judgment at the Court of Appeal. A copy of the Notice of Appeal dated November 6, 2026 is annexed for your confirmation and same is marked as Annexure ‘A’.



“The 1st Defendant has also filed Motion on Notice at the Federal High Court for the Stay of Execution of the judgment of the Federal High Court delivered on November 5, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the appeal at the Court of Appeal. A copy of the Motion on Notice for Stay of Execution dated November 6, 2026 is annexed for your confirmation and same is marked as Annexure ‘B’.

“We therefore write to bring to your attention that the plaintiff, Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe, is aware of the appeal filed by the 1st Defendant, African Democratic Congress (ADC), as well as the Motion on Notice for Stay of Execution. The Motion on Notice for the Stay of Execution is yet to be taken by the Honourable Court.



“In view of the foregoing, we enjoin the Commission to stay further action on the subject matter of the suit pending the hearing and determination of the appeal now pending at the Court of Appeal,” the letter read.

Justice Lifu had held that the emergence of Senator Mark as ADC chairman, as well as the other members of his executive, violated the party’s constitution and guidelines.

Gombe had approached the Federal High Court, Abuja, to challenge the emergence of the Mark-led executive. In the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, he claimed that following the resignation of the former National Chairman of the ADC, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he was qualified to assume the party’s leadership.



He had asked the court to restrain the defendants from parading themselves as leaders of the party, arguing that the process that produced them violated constitutional provisions and the ADC’s guidelines.

Those sued included the ADC, Mark, Aregbesola, INEC and the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu.

The defendants had urged the court to dismiss the suit for being incompetent and lacking in merit, arguing that the matter concerned the internal affairs of a political party and was therefore outside the court’s jurisdiction.



However, Justice Lifu granted the reliefs sought by the plaintiff and declared unconstitutional, unlawful, null and void, all actions and decisions taken by the Mark-led executive on behalf of the party.

The congresses and convention that produced Atiku and other candidates seeking elective offices at the state and federal levels were conducted by the Mark-led National Executive.

The ADC Director of Strategic Communications, Phrank Shaibu, said the party had also formally notified INEC of the appeal and urged the commission to refrain from taking further action on the matter.



He said: “The application for a stay has not yet been determined. INEC must therefore exercise restraint. It must not act as though the appeal and stay application do not exist, or take any step that could pre-empt the Court of Appeal and undermine the proper resolution of this matter. The Commission must respect the judicial process and allow the appellate court to hear the case.

“The ADC is exercising its lawful right to appeal. The judgment is now under challenge before a higher court, and the legal process must be allowed to run its course. We expect INEC to uphold the law and take full account of the pending proceedings before making any consequential decision.



“To our members, supporters and Nigerians who believe in democracy: remain calm, steadfast and confident. This is not the end of the road. The ADC is taking every lawful step to defend its rights, and we will not be intimidated or distracted from that responsibility. Our commitment to Nigerians and to their right to choose remains firm.

“Our campaigns continue without interruption. There is no stopping the affordability train or our mission to make life better for Nigerians. We will keep taking our message to the people as we pursue every lawful avenue to defend our rights.

“We are confident that the facts and the law will receive a full hearing. The ADC will continue to pursue this matter through the courts and stand for a democratic process in which every party and every voter is treated fairly,” Shaibu stated.

Keyamo: Heaven Will Not Fall if Atiku Is Not on 2027 Ballot

Keyamo has said heaven will not fall if former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar does not appear on the ballot in the 2027 general election.

In a post on X, Keyamo said political actors must respect judicial decisions rather than abuse judges or blackmail the judiciary whenever judgments do not favour them.

He cited the Supreme Court’s 2020 decision nullifying the victory of the APC governorship candidate in Bayelsa State, David Lyon, a day before his scheduled swearing-in.

He recalled that Lyon was inspecting the stadium prepared for his inauguration when the judgment was delivered, adding that the APC accepted the decision with equanimity.



Keyamo also referenced the Supreme Court’s 2019 judgment that removed APC candidates who had won elections in Zamfara State, from the governorship to the House of Assembly, and replaced them with candidates of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

He said Atiku had defended the judiciary following the Zamfara judgment, which went against the ruling party at the time.

Quoting the former vice-president, he said: “That judgment was against the ruling party. We took it on our chins.”

Keyamo added: “You cannot abuse judges and blackmail the judiciary when it doesn’t go your way.”

He concluded: “Heavens WILL NOT FALL IF A CERTAIN ATIKU ABUBAKAR IS NOT ON THE BALLOT IN 2027.”

APC to ADC: Go and Sort Out Your Internal Mess

The APC, however, denied involvement in the ADC’s crisis, accusing the opposition party of blaming it whenever it suffered a legal setback instead of resolving its internal problems.

Its National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, said Thursday’s judgment by Justice Lifu, which sacked the Mark-led leadership of the ADC, was self-inflicted.

He said the nullification of all official acts of the party’s leadership, including its primary election processes and outcomes, resulted from its lawlessness and demonstrated the vibrancy of the rule of law and independence of the judiciary.

Morka added that if the ADC was dissatisfied with the decision, it should exercise its constitutional right of appeal rather than engage in partisan mudslinging against the APC and issue threats capable of inciting anarchy.

He said the ADC hailed the rule of law and extolled the judiciary whenever court decisions favoured it.

Morka said: “In their warped reckoning, only courts and judges that side with them are worthy while those that rule differently are a menace to society. That is senselessness in the extreme.

“The court judgment that has sent the ADC in a tailspin had to do with a notorious case initiated by leaders of ADC against pirate leaders of ADC.

“To be clear, APC is neither a party nor an interlocutor in the matter. Nothing about the case has anything to do with the APC. And the APC has absolutely no role in the party’s judicial quagmire.

“The case resulted from a legal challenge brought by ADC national officers victimised by the bare-faced heist of the party’s leadership by David Mark and his co-pirates to satisfy Atiku Abubakar’s quixotic presidential ambition.

“It didn’t matter to them that their hostile takeover of that party was in flagrant violation of the rule of law and ADC’s internal democracy, as a court of competent jurisdiction has now declared.

“Now they lash out in a fit of rage at the court and innocent spectators for the judicial outcome that was the inevitable consequence of their reckless political misadventure.”

Morka said the ADC had peddled conspiracy theories without taking responsibility for what he described as a self-inflicted injury that the court had judicially certified.

He described the ADC as a decrepit party, adding that it was unfit to be taken seriously by Nigerians.

He said the APC and President Bola Tinubu’s administration remained committed to preserving democracy, upholding the rule of law and delivering good governance.

ADC Chairmen Threaten Protest, demand Mark’s removal

The National Executive Committee Chairmen Forum of the ADC loyal to Gombe has threatened to embark on a nationwide protest against INEC if it fails to comply with the court judgment on the party’s leadership crisis.

The forum also called on INEC to immediately replace the names of Senator David Mark and members of his dissolved Interim National Working Committee on its portal with those of Nafiu Bala Gombe and other party officials it described as legally recognised.

It also urged the Commission to reopen its portal to enable it conduct fresh primaries, where necessary, and upload its candidates for the 2027 general elections.

The Secretary of the forum, Kennedy Odion, made the demands while addressing journalists in Abuja yesterday.

Odion described the ruling as a vindication of the forum’s position that the Mark-led leadership was not constitutionally recognised.

“We, the only legally recognised NEC members, accept in its entirety the judgment declaring our own Alhaji Nafiu Bala Gombe the authentic national chairman of the ADC.

“Failure to comply with this latest judgment will leave us no option but to proceed with our planned nationwide protest against the electoral umpire. Nigeria is for all of us. No individual, however highly placed, is above the law,” Odion said.

Ologbondiyan: ADC Will Be on Ballot Despite Court Ruling

The Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan, has assured that the party will participate in the 2027 general election despite the Federal High Court judgment invalidating the process through which its leadership emerged.

Speaking in an interview with ARISE NEWS yesterday, he said the party would pursue all available legal options to challenge the judgment, dismissing suggestions that the ADC would resort to actions capable of destabilising the country if prevented from participating in the election.

Ologbondiyan criticised the judgment delivered by Justice Lifu, arguing that it contradicted an earlier ruling by Justice Musa Liman on the party’s leadership dispute.

He described the development as a threat to the country’s judicial system and questioned the implications of conflicting judgments on the same matter.

He said: “This topic is not just because I am a member of the ADC or because it is the ADC that is involved, but I always look prophetically towards our tomorrow as a country. I mean, is this the legacy we are going to leave behind for those who are coming after us?

“That we will have a situation back to the days of old? A situation that the late General Sani Abacha pointed to in removing the Shonekan government from office, because judges and justices were busy producing conflicting judgments. Is that where we are going back to?”

Ologbondiyan alleged that the ruling was intended to frustrate the party’s growing political activities, particularly following its campaign outing in Sokoto State.

He said: “Those who said that the ADC and the presidency are rattled are speaking to the fact. They are rattled. They have done everything possible to halt our campaign in Sokoto, including the unimaginable, and we have bypassed all that.

“We had a rally that was mammoth, which Nigerians are commending at this moment.

“And not just that, Dr Abati, it will interest you to know that the dimension which Atiku Abubakar and the ADC introduced to campaigning yesterday has not been seen since 2003, which is a street-to-street campaign. Moving through communities, stopping at every community, talking to the people and addressing them.

“So, I believe, like many Nigerians have said, that they are scared of this dimension of campaigning, of reaching out and being everywhere you go.

“Because of that, they believe that the only thing they can do is to remove the ADC from the electoral process. But that in itself will go nowhere, Dr Abati. It will not go anywhere. The ADC will be in this election.”

On the legal dispute surrounding the party’s leadership, Ologbondiyan questioned why the earlier judgment by Justice Liman was allegedly disregarded in the subsequent proceedings before Justice Lifu.

He said: “How do you forego a judgment because it doesn’t favour you? You go and hire another judge to produce for you another judgment. And that is the case that we have on our hands now.

“Justice Musa Liman, arising from the matter brought by my brother to the court, dismissed the matter. He didn’t even bother to appeal the judgment because if he went on appeal, he would have been caught out. So, he abandoned the matter.

“So, Justice Liman, when you came, we pointed out to your legal representatives that your brother, judge, your brother on the same bench, had delivered a judgment in this matter. And this is the position of the judgment.

“You threw it through the window and said it doesn’t matter. Nobody can stop me.”

The ADC spokesperson said he was reluctant to make sweeping comments about members of the judiciary, despite his reservations about the handling of the case.

He also addressed the party’s unsuccessful attempt to have Justice Lifu recuse himself from the proceedings, saying the ADC had petitioned the Chief Judge over its concerns about the judge’s handling of the matter.

He said: “We did petition the Chief Judge of the court.

“We said we no longer have confidence. We pointed out that this matter that you are taking on has been decided by your brother. He said no, he must hear you.

“Even after his engagement with the higher court, because of ADC, he said he was going to hear it. He cannot be stopped.

“We said, okay, it is not the case of all of you. We no longer have confidence in the court.”

Ologbondiyan also questioned the circumstances surrounding the emergence of the party’s leadership, alleging inconsistencies in the position taken by some individuals involved in the process.

He referred to the resignation of a party official ahead of the coalition process and his subsequent attendance at the inauguration of the new leadership.

He said: “Dr Ubala resigned his appointment to allow the decision of their head there for the party to come, for the coalition to come to the party. He did.

“Now, he even attended the inauguration. He was physically there. I saw him.

“He came back and said, ‘Oh, my signature was poor.’ No proof. Nothing.

“This was proof for Justice Lifu. Every heavy evidence I took for Justice Lifu, they were thrown out. He had just one purpose, and that is the purpose that he delivered yesterday.”

Despite his criticism of the judgment, Ologbondiyan reiterated that the party would follow the legal process and would not support any action aimed at destabilising Nigeria.

He said the ruling had generated concern among party supporters and Nigerians who had invested their time and resources in the ADC’s political activities.

He said: “I believe, like many Nigerians, that in the last 12 hours, I have got more than 100 calls from Nigerians asking, ‘What’s the direction? What are we doing at this time?’

“We will definitely follow a legal process. But a number of Nigerians who are putting in their resources, who are putting in their time, who are campaigning across the length and breadth of Nigeria, one character, with a stroke of the pen, says that he has displaced them.

“I mean, where is the country going to?”

Coalition: FHC Judgment Dangerous Escalation

The Coalition for Democracy, an umbrella body of opposition political parties, has described the judgment of Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, which dissolved the Mark-led leadership of the ADC and invalidated its presidential candidacy, as a dangerous escalation and a systematic campaign to eliminate credible political opposition ahead of the 2027 general election.

The coalition emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on August 31. Its members include the ADC, Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA), National Rescue Movement (NRM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Social Democratic Party (SDP) and Youth Progressives Party (YPP).

It was established to give practical expression to the resolutions of the summit and is committed to defending Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, protecting political pluralism and ensuring free, fair, credible and competitive elections.

In a statement, the coalition warned that what was happening to the ADC could happen to every opposition party.

Its National Coordinator, Salihu Moh. Lukman, raised concerns over what he described as Nigeria’s shrinking democratic space, citing attacks on opposition supporters, obstruction of political activities and the increasing weaponisation of state institutions against political competitors.

Lukman said: “When opposition parties are attacked on the streets, frustrated by state institutions, and threatened with elimination through judicial pronouncements, Nigerians must ask whether the ruling party still intends to face any meaningful opposition at the ballot box.

“While the Coalition respects the independence of the judiciary and the right of aggrieved parties to seek legal redress, the courts must never become instruments through which political competition is extinguished.

“Those who seek to destroy the opposition in order to guarantee their own victory must understand that they are not merely threatening political parties; they are threatening the very foundations of the Republic. A government that cannot tolerate opposition has lost the moral authority to call itself democratic.”

He added: “When a government becomes more afraid of the opposition than it is accountable to the people, democracy itself is in danger. This is why the Coalition warns that the continued narrowing of the democratic space in Nigeria carries grave consequences for national stability. No democracy can remain peaceful when citizens are denied meaningful political alternatives.

“The ballot must remain the battlefield of democracy. No political party should be allowed to achieve through institutional manipulation what it fears it cannot achieve through the votes of Nigerians.

“We therefore stand in solidarity with the ADC in its decision to challenge this judgment through the appropriate judicial processes. We call on all opposition parties, civil society organisations, the Nigerian Bar Association, organised labour, the media and patriotic Nigerians to unite in peaceful, lawful resistance against every attempt to undermine political pluralism.

“Let it be known: the Coalition for Democracy will not stand by while Nigeria is reduced to a democracy without opposition, elections without alternatives, and ballots without genuine choices.

“An attack on one is an attack on all. We will resist it together,” Lukman said

World.title: Afreximbank Targets $1bn Pan African Film Fund to Transform Continent’s Creative Industry
World.content:
*Elombi: Africa must capture more value from its $60bn creative economy

*Oramah proposes dedicated facility, cooperatives to unlock funding, reduce risks

Sunday Ehigiator

The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) yesterday disclosed plan to mobilise up to $1 billion for a Pan-African film fund, as part of efforts to expand financing, strengthen distribution networks and position Africa as a global production hub for creative content.

The Executive Vice President, Intra-African Trade and Export Development at Afreximbank, Mrs. Kanayo Awani, who disclosed this while delivering the opening statement at the 2026 Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) Summit in Lagos, pointed out that the proposed fund being developed through the bank’s impact investment subsidiary, the Fund for Export Development in Africa (FEDA), in partnership with One Street Studios, was expected to finance African content, strengthen distribution networks, develop enabling technologies and build infrastructure for the continent’s film industry.



This comes the President and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Afreximbank, Dr George Elombi, called for stronger African ownership and value capture across the creative-industry supply chain, warning that increased production financing alone will not deliver optimal economic benefits to the continent. Elombi said Africa must move beyond financing music and movie productions to building a comprehensive creative ecosystem that enables the continent to retain more value from its creative output.



Citing estimates from the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), he said Africa’s creative economy was valued at approximately $60 billion, representing about two per cent of the global creative industry.

Equally, former President of Afreximbank, Prof. Benedict Oramah, stressed that unlocking finance for the creative industry would require a fundamental restructuring of how financial institutions assess and support creative businesses. He argued that the challenge was not necessarily a shortage of capital but the inability of smaller creative entrepreneurs to access available funding because they often lacked the business structures and market evidence required by lenders.



Speaking further, Awani said the bank’s investment strategy was designed to address structural challenges confronting Africa’s creative industries, particularly inadequate financing, weak distribution networks, fragmented markets and poor intellectual property protection.

She stressed that Africa’s challenge was no longer a shortage of creative talent but the absence of the financial and institutional infrastructure required to convert that talent into sustainable businesses and economic prosperity.



According to her, much of the value generated by African music, films, fashion, literature, gastronomy and other creative products continue to be financed, distributed, owned and monetised outside the continent.

“The creative economy is no longer peripheral. It is part of Africa’s development story. It is a trade sector, an investment opportunity, and a strategic asset capable of generating jobs, foreign exchange and global influence at scale,” she said.

Awani disclosed that Afreximbank, through its subsidiary, Creative Africa Investments, had approved six investments in new projects spanning film, television, music and digital content.



On skills development, she disclosed that Afreximbank had trained more than 7,000 aspiring jewellers and craftspeople across Africa and the diaspora through its partnership with Egyptian jeweller, Azza Fahmy, and Trace Academia.

In gastronomy and culinary arts, Awani said the bank had connected more than 30 African and Caribbean food brands to buyers, facilitating approximately $20 million in trade deals and opening new markets across Africa, the United States, Europe and the Middle East.



She also disclosed that the CANEX Book Factory had brought together emerging writers from 16 African and Caribbean countries, culminating in the publication of an anthology titled Instances of Exceptional Moments of Hunger, featuring 19 writers.

Similarly, the CANEX Music Factory had brought together more than 150 musicians in collaborative recording sessions, producing 32 original songs released on global streaming platforms.

Beyond music production, she said Afreximbank was working with the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry to establish regional music charts in four African countries, including Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Senegal, to provide credible, data-driven evidence of artists’ performance and strengthen their ability to attract investment and commercial partnerships.

Awani further disclosed that the bank’s CANEX Skills Development Programme, delivered through CANEX.Africa and the Afreximbank Academy, had attracted 12,000 users, offering online training in music, fashion, film and gastronomy.

In his opening remarks, Elombi said Africa must move beyond financing music and movie productions to building a comprehensive creative ecosystem that enables the continent to retain more value from its creative output.

“We can put these financing schemes into music and movie productions. Yet the value we derive will still be low. We must therefore focus on building the creative ecosystem,” he said.

The Afreximbank president identified distribution, branding, marketing platforms and intellectual property ownership as critical areas requiring greater investment and African participation.

He stressed that strengthening these segments would enable the continent to capture more economic value from its creative products rather than concentrating support solely on production financing.

His position underscores the need for a more integrated approach to developing Africa’s creative economy, with greater attention to the structures that connect creative production to markets, commercial opportunities and long-term returns.

Meanwhile, speaking during a panel session at the summit, Oramah recalled that Afreximbank had committed about $2 billion to financing initiatives during his tenure, adding that smaller filmmakers and music producers had not benefited adequately from such facilities.

He said unlocking financing for the creative industry would require a fundamental restructuring of how financial institutions assess and support creative businesses.

He argued that the challenge was not necessarily the absence of capital but the inability of smaller creative entrepreneurs to access available financing because they often lacked the business structures and market evidence required by lenders.

“I don’t think the issue of access to capital is because there is no capital. It’s all about availability of capital.

“When I was at Afreximbank, we put about $2 billion. And we were willing to put more money. But how many people were able to access it? If we go and look at the distribution of those who have been able to access it, most of the beneficiaries will be those who are doing the infrastructure, the big people,” he said.

Oramah identified the absence of clearly established markets for creative products as one of the major factors discouraging banks from financing the sector.

According to him, financial institutions need assurances that creative products would attract buyers and generate sufficient revenue to repay investments, but many producers concentrate on creating content without adequately developing market strategies.

“The first thing anybody does depends on the market. So, if there is no market, then the supply chain cannot be built to make the banks comfortable to finance it.

“So people come and produce something, but the first thing the banker asks is, who will buy this? They haven’t thought about it. They are creative people, they just want to produce, they want to create,” he said.

To address the challenge, he proposed the establishment of a dedicated Creative Industry Project Preparation Facility to help filmmakers, musicians and other creative entrepreneurs develop bankable projects.

He explained that existing project preparation facilities were available to manufacturers and infrastructure developers but largely excluded creative businesses, whose practitioners often lacked the resources and technical expertise to prepare business plans, conduct market studies and structure financing proposals.

“So there has to be what I call a creative industry project preparation facility. It’s unique.

“Because once you think that way, things will begin to change. Because you create a new group of expertise that will help people prepare for things that will come to the market, and it will help them to lend money, because it makes things easier,” he added.

The former Afreximbank chief also advocated grouping smaller creative businesses into cooperatives to reduce lending risks and make them more attractive to financial institutions.

He explained that pooling creative entrepreneurs would enable lenders and credit insurers to spread risks across a larger group rather than assess each individual business in isolation.

“Why don’t we find a way of grouping the creatives, those small creatives, into cooperatives?

“When you group them into cooperatives, then you are able to diversify the risks. You are able to insure the group, because credit insurance takes the risk of large numbers, whereas bankers take the single risk,” he said.

On distribution, Oramah said Africa must move beyond dependence on foreign platforms and gatekeepers by developing and owning its distribution infrastructure.

He said the objective should be to establish an African-owned distribution network and box-office system that would enable local producers to distribute their films across the continent before pursuing international sales.

He disclosed that about 34 private distribution platforms across Africa had been identified as potentially ready to participate in the process, adding that the intention was to work with existing systems while gradually building an African-owned alternative.

Oramah also stressed the importance of retaining ownership of African intellectual property, warning that the continent must avoid losing valuable creative assets to foreign investors and buyers.

The issue of intellectual property ownership also featured prominently during the discussions, with Hollywood actress, director and producer, Megan Good Majors, urging African creatives to move beyond seeking representation in international productions to securing positions that allow them to control and benefit financially from their work.

She said African and diaspora creatives must become more involved in producing, directing, financing and owning the intellectual property generated from their talents.

“It’s really about coming not just in front of the camera but also behind the camera and being really intentional about producing, about directing, about ownership, about every single way that we can be involved that’s not just the talent that we have that’s facing forward but the talent that’s behind the scenes.

“And so I think that really what’s important is that we begin to take up those positions where you do see more people from across the diaspora directing, producing, putting up funding, making sure that we keep our IP once it moves forward,” she said.

Managing Director of OneStreet Studios and JBL Media, Lavelle LeVette, also called for the development of African-owned distribution systems that would enable filmmakers to reach audiences across the continent without depending entirely on foreign gatekeepers.

She said Africa needed a distribution network that would allow local producers to showcase their films through an indigenous box-office system before pursuing international sales.

“The bottom line is, for the continent, how can we own our own distribution system? So that when someone makes a movie on the continent, we’re not waiting and saying, oh, please pick me and bring my movie to the world. We’ll have our own system, our own box office.

“So we’ll say that we have our own box office. We can show our movies here, and then we do our foreign sales, and we distribute them,” she said.

Earlier, veteran actress, Joke Silva, called for stronger protection of African creative works and greater collaboration among stakeholders to ensure practitioners could earn sustainable livelihoods from their labour.

Using the example of Ghanaian visual artist, El Anatsui, whose works have attracted international exhibitions and significant commercial value, Silva said African creators needed stronger mechanisms to protect their intellectual property and secure the economic benefits of their work.

She also recounted how the National Theatre in Lagos was rescued from deterioration through collaboration among Nigerian banks, arguing that the experience demonstrated what could be achieved when institutions pooled resources to preserve important cultural assets.

“The protection of our work lies with our continent. We cannot blame other countries for using or other continents for using our works anyhow they please. They will protect their own, we must protect our own,” she said.

In a separate address, the Commissioner for Health, Humanitarian Affairs and Social Development of the African Union Commission, Ambassador Amma Twum-Amoah, called on African governments to translate existing cultural policies and continental frameworks into practical investments, institutions and measurable outcomes.

World.title: CBN Tightens Stablecoin Rules, Sets N15bn Capital Floor for Dollar Tokens
World.content:
*Says foreign issuers must establish Nigerian entities, secure local licences

*P2P naira-dollar conversions subject to FX approval

Nume Ekeghe

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has introduced new regulations requiring foreign-currency stablecoin issuers to obtain local licences and establish Nigerian-incorporated entities, as it moves to tighten oversight of dollar-backed digital tokens and other virtual asset activities.



The regulations, which took effect on November 5, 2026, establish a formal framework for stablecoins, virtual asset service providers and related payment activities, including peer-to-peer (P2P) transactions, custody, transfers and settlement.

In a circular dated November 5, 2026, addressed to virtual asset service providers and stakeholders in the financial services industry, the apex bank said the framework was designed to promote responsible innovation while protecting the integrity of the financial system.

Signed by the Director, Payments System Policy Department, Musa Jimoh, the regulations establish a risk-based framework covering licensing, authorisation, capital requirements, consumer protection, technology risks, cybersecurity, anti-money laundering controls and regulatory reporting.



The rules apply to persons conducting regulated activities in or from Nigeria, targeting Nigerian users or undertaking activities that could materially affect the country’s payments system, financial system, foreign exchange market or financial stability. They may apply even where an operator has no physical presence in Nigeria.

A major provision requires foreign-currency stablecoin issuers to operate through Nigerian-incorporated entities and obtain CBN approval before making their tokens available to Nigerians.

Under Section 11.1, foreign issuers can no longer rely solely on licences or regulatory approvals obtained in other jurisdictions to access the Nigerian market. They must obtain a Class 2 Foreign Currency Issuer Licence and issue their tokens through a locally incorporated entity.

The regulations further require Nigerian entities to remain fully responsible for compliance, even where they operate through international group arrangements. The CBN will have unrestricted supervisory access to their books, records, systems, reserve arrangements and relevant group information.

The framework also introduces capital requirements based on the currency to which a stablecoin is linked. Issuers of naira-referenced stablecoins, classified as Class 1, must maintain minimum paid-up capital of N10 billion, while foreign-currency stablecoin issuers under Class 2 must maintain at least N15 billion.

Other non-security virtual asset service providers face a minimum capital requirement of ₦1 billion.

The CBN is also introducing a systemic stablecoin category, enabling it to impose enhanced supervisory requirements on tokens whose scale or adoption could have wider implications for the Nigerian financial system.

Under Section 3.6, a stablecoin may qualify for systemic designation if its naira-equivalent circulating supply exceeds N500 billion every day for 30 consecutive days, or if it is held or used by more than five million people in Nigeria.

The apex bank may also consider transaction volumes and values, the number and concentration of Nigerian users or wallet addresses, and the proportion of a stablecoin’s activity attributable to the Nigerian market.

The regulations also bring P2P transactions involving dollar-backed stablecoins under the formal foreign exchange framework, requiring providers to obtain express CBN approval before facilitating conversions between the naira and foreign-currency value.

The bank made clear that approval to provide P2P services does not confer permission to conduct foreign exchange business or create an alternative foreign exchange market.

Providers must secure separate approval before facilitating P2P transactions involving conversions between the naira and a Class 2 stablecoin or other foreign-currency value. Such approval will require the naira leg of the transaction to be settled through, or reported to, an authorised dealer designated by the CBN. Transactions must also comply with prescribed foreign exchange monitoring, limits and documentation requirements.

The rules further prohibit operators from structuring, splitting or routing transactions through multiple channels to evade regulatory oversight, foreign exchange or capital-flow requirements, transaction limits, anti-money laundering controls and reporting obligations.

On reserve requirements, Class 1 stablecoin issuers must maintain at least 20 per cent of their total reserve pool as a cash deposit with the CBN in a dedicated Reserve Deposit Account.

The funds cannot be withdrawn without the bank’s prior written consent. The CBN will have real-time visibility over the account, which will not attract interest. The requirement does not apply to Class 2 issuers, whose operational liquidity is governed by separate provisions.

The regulations also prohibit stablecoin issuers from paying interest, yields, dividends or other financial benefits to holders simply for retaining their tokens. They clarify that stablecoins are not bank deposits and are not covered by deposit insurance from the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation.

The CBN has backed the framework with financial penalties for non-compliance. Unlicensed virtual asset activities attract a minimum fine of N100 million, with an additional N1 million for every day the violation continues.

Breaches involving capital, reserve and liquidity requirements may attract penalties ranging from N50 million to N250 million, while violations relating to reserve leverage or encumbrance carry fines of between N250 million and N500 million.

Non-compliance with anti-money laundering, counter-terrorism financing and Travel Rule requirements attracts a minimum penalty of N50 million. Fraudulent conduct or deliberate misrepresentation carries a minimum fine of N500 million, alongside possible referral for criminal prosecution.

The CBN, however, clarified that the regulations do not displace the statutory mandate of the Securities and Exchange Commission. Activities involving security virtual assets, securities, investment contracts and other capital-market products will remain subject to the applicable capital-market regulatory framework.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu Committed to Free, Fair, Credible Elections, Says Information Minister
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has assured Nigerians and the international community that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration is committed to conducting free, fair and credible general elections in 2027.

Idris gave the assurance during an interview with TRT World, Türkiye’s international broadcaster, on the sidelines of the TRT World Forum 2026 in Istanbul, Türkiye.

The forum, which opened yesterday, is being held under the theme, ‘A World Without a Centre: Who Leads When the Rules Run Out?’

The minister said the federal government would continue to support Nigeria’s democratic institutions, particularly the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), while respecting its constitutional independence.

He stressed that the administration was committed to creating an enabling environment for the electoral umpire to discharge its responsibilities effectively and ensure that the wishes of Nigerians prevailed at the polls.

“Let me assure Nigerians and the international community that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration is fully committed to free, fair and credible elections in 2027. We will continue to support the democratic process and ensure that the will of the Nigerian people prevails,” he said.

On concerns about insecurity and its potential impact on the 2027 general elections, Idris said the federal government was intensifying efforts to tackle security challenges across the country.

He cited the recruitment of additional military personnel and the procurement of equipment by the Tinubu administration as measures aimed at strengthening the operational capacity of the Armed Forces to combat insecurity.

The minister also reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to political and media freedoms, describing freedom of expression and political participation as fundamental pillars of democracy.

However, he cautioned against the growing spread of fake news, misinformation and unverified reports, particularly as the country approaches another election cycle.

He urged Nigerians, political actors and media practitioners to exercise responsibility by verifying information before sharing it, warning that the circulation of false information could heighten political tensions and erode public confidence in the electoral process.

On the growing influence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in journalism and governance, Idris acknowledged its potential to improve public communication, service delivery and access to information.

He, however, warned against the misuse of the technology to create deepfakes, manipulate content and spread disinformation, stressing the need for responsible application of AI.

Addressing concerns surrounding the federal government’s borrowing, the minister defended strategic borrowing as a legitimate instrument for financing critical infrastructure, stimulating economic growth and creating opportunities for future development.

According to him, borrowing is a common economic practice among developed and developing countries, adding that the critical consideration should be the purpose of the loans and the value they generate for citizens.

“Borrowing is not a crime. Countries across the world, whether developed or developing, borrow to invest in their future. What matters is the purpose of such borrowing and the value it creates,” Idris said.

He explained that the administration viewed borrowing as an investment in Nigeria’s future, particularly in the development of critical infrastructure, expansion of economic opportunities and stimulation of sustainable economic growth.

The minister maintained that the government’s economic policies were designed to strengthen the economy, expand infrastructure and improve the living conditions of Nigerians.

Idris, who is attending the TRT World Forum at the invitation of the Turkish government, commended the authorities in Türkiye and the organisers of the event for providing a platform for discussions on pressing global challenges.

He described the forum as an important avenue for world leaders, policymakers, scholars and other stakeholders to exchange ideas and develop practical solutions to shared challenges amid growing global uncertainty.

World.title: Customs Releases 98 of 300 Stranded Containers to Power Minister after FG’s Intervention
World.content:
Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja

The Federal Ministry of Power has secured the release of 98 containers of transmission equipment stranded at the nation’s ports for over a decade, raising hope of a stronger and more dependable national electricity grid.

Minister of Power, Mr. Joseph Tegbe, announced the development in Lagos, a statement in Abuja by his spokesman, Adeola Adelabu, said yesterday. The government did not say why the equipment was detained by the Customs in the first place.

Tegbe said 44 containers were released from the ENL Terminal while 54 were released from the APMT and Sun & Moon Terminals, bringing the total released so far to 98 out of over 300 containers held at the ports.

According to him, the equipment, comprising high-capacity transformers, cables and switchgear, was procured to expand the transmission network and relieve overloaded substations.

He explained that the prolonged detention of the cargoes stalled critical transmission projects, kept existing substations under heavy strain, exposed valuable national assets to deterioration and led to accumulation of demurrage and other charges.

The minister noted that the cost of the delay was being borne daily by Nigerians, including businesses forced to spend more on alternative power, households enduring incessant interruptions and public institutions struggling to maintain essential services.

Tegbe said the release was in response to a directive by President Bola Tinubu for immediate clearance of the cargoes.

He disclosed that following the presidential directive, he and the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Mr. Bashir Adeniyi, swung into action and worked tirelessly to secure the release.

The minister credited Tinubu for the breakthrough and expressed appreciation to the Ministers of Finance and Marine and Blue Economy, Taiwo Oyedele and Adegboyega Oyetola, as well as the Comptroller General of Customs and officials of the Ministry of Power and its agencies for their roles in actualising the release.

Speaking at the event, the Comptroller General of Customs, Adeniyi, said the release was sequel to the President’s directive for immediate clearance and for relevant agencies to resolve all outstanding charges and administrative bottlenecks without delay.

Adeniyi said the Service had commenced steps to clear the containers in collaboration with the Ministry of Power, the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) and terminal operators.

He pledged to work hand in hand with the Minister of Power until all the outstanding containers were cleared, and appealed to terminal operators to support the national effort.

According to the statement, upon inspection, most of the equipment was found to be useful and viable.

The ministry stressed that when fully evacuated, the equipment would be verified, tested and refurbished where necessary, and subsequently deployed to project sites to complete stalled installations, relieve overloaded substations and strengthen constrained transmission corridors.

According to the statement, as the projects enter service, Nigerians should expect fewer interruptions arising from overloading, improved voltage profile and a stronger transmission network to wheel power to homes, businesses and essential services.

The power ministry assured that it would follow the recovery process through to installation and inauguration and provide regular updates on the remaining containers, expressing confidence that they would be released without further delay.

By recovering equipment that had been idle for years, the federal government said it is converting policy into power and promise into progress that citizens can feel in their homes, shops and workplaces.

World.title: Presidential CNG Initiative Launches New Abuja Facility as Private Funding Hits $2.6bn
World.content:
.Total refuelling stations reach 106, 170 more in pipeline, says Ahmed

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja

The Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV) yesterday launched a new daughter station in Abuja, revealing that Nigeria now has 106 such operational refuelling facilities nationwide, with another 170 in the pipeline.

The Executive Chairman of the Pi-CNG & EV secretariat, Ismaeel Ahmed, who disclosed this during the inauguration of the CNG Integrated Refuelling Unit (IRU) in collaboration with Rolling Energy, stressed that total funding mobilised by the private for the sub-sector has reached $2.6 billion.

Ahmed said the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu administration had also directed the deployment of additional 2,000 refuelling infrastructure units in two phases to accelerate the nationwide expansion of CNG facilities.

He said the President ordered the provision of 1,500 units in February and another 500 in August, adding that the facilities were expected to come on stream between this year and early next year.

According to him, the CNG initiative has moved beyond the proof-of-concept stage, with billions in private sector investments already committed to the sector.

“This is almost our 106th station across the country in less than two years. This is not beginning any longer. The market has been proven, and investors are trooping in,” he said.

According to Ahmed, about 170 additional stations were undergoing development or awaiting various licences from the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).

He said the government was working to expand the facilities to commercial transport routes and high-traffic corridors across the country to ensure more Nigerians benefit from cheaper transportation.

The Pi-CNG & EV office chairman said the adoption of CNG-powered buses had reduced transportation costs by between 30 and 40 per cent on routes where the vehicles were operating.

He cited the Kano-Katsina route, where commuters who previously paid between N3,000 and N4,000 could now travel for about N1,500 using CNG-powered buses.

Ahmed, however, acknowledged that the number of available buses remained inadequate, assuring that efforts were ongoing to increase their deployment.

According to the executive director, the expansion of the refuelling network is expected to improve access to CNG, strengthen public confidence in the transition and make cleaner and more affordable transportation fuel available to more Nigerians.

Earlier, the Permanent Secretary, State House, Temitope Fashedemi, said the inauguration of the facility demonstrated the commitment of the State House to the federal government’s alternative energy policy introduced following the removal of petrol subsidy.

Fashedemi described CNG as a viable and cheaper fuel alternative, noting that Nigeria had abundant natural gas resources that could be better harnessed for domestic consumption rather than wasted through gas flaring.

He explained that the State House partnered Pi-CNG & EV office and Rolling Energy to reactivate an abandoned fuel facility and convert it into a CNG refuelling and vehicle conversion centre.

According to him, the State House provided the facility, while the private sector partner handled its renovation and operational development without any financial contribution from the government.

“The State House hasn’t spent any naira in this space, but we made this place available for this purpose,” he said.

Fashedemi said the facility would not only dispense CNG but also provide conversion services for eligible vehicles, allowing motorists to switch to CNG-powered systems.

He disclosed that about 10 recently acquired State House vehicles were already hybrid vehicles capable of running on CNG, while some shuttle buses operating within the Presidential Villa also used the technology.

He added that State House workers would begin presenting eligible personal vehicles for conversion in the coming weeks.

The permanent secretary urged private investors and entrepreneurs to take advantage of the opportunities in the CNG market, stressing that the government was not expected to own or operate all refuelling stations.

He said the facility had already provided free CNG refuelling services to motorists in the surrounding communities during its testing phase for more than a week.

Fashedemi expressed optimism that its commercial operation would ease pressure on existing refuelling stations and improve access to alternative fuel for motorists in the area.

He urged more private sector operators to invest in CNG infrastructure to support the government’s drive to reduce transportation costs and expand the country’s energy options.

Also speaking, the Chief Executive Officer of Rolling Energy Limited, Mubarak Danbatta, described the project as an example of the benefits of collaboration between government and private investors, commending the State House for providing the abandoned facility for redevelopment.

Danbatta said the partnership demonstrated how the government could support private sector investment by making existing infrastructure available for commercial development.

“What you are seeing here is the power of partnership. When private entities and government come together, this is the result,” he said.

He disclosed that the facility, known as an integrated refuelling unit, combined the dispenser and compressor in a single system, with double-nozzle dispensers that allow vehicles to refuel from both sides.

According to him, the station has the capacity to serve about 150 vehicles daily, depending on cylinder size and pressure, while its vehicle conversion centre is projected to convert 12 vehicles daily.

World.title: Meghan Markle’s Father Arrested in Florida Over Alleged Child Sexual Abuse Material
World.content:
Sunday Ehigiator with agency report

Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, was arrested in Florida, yesterday, over allegations he possessed child sexual abuse material, including sexually explicit photographs of himself with minors, the Justice Department announced.

He is charged with one count of possession of child pornography, according to a criminal complaint, the NBC reported.

The FBI seized around 78 items from two storage units rented by Markle that contain “suspected child pornography,” according to court documents. Items seized include film negatives featuring an adult man with naked “pre-pubescent” girls, and a witness “positively identified the adult man as Markle,” according to the documents.

Markle, 82, was expected to make his initial appearance yesterday, in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida in Tampa, the Justice Department said.

“These allegations are extremely serious, and we will prosecute Mr. Markle to the fullest extent of federal law,” First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement.

“Working with our Justice Department partners, our agents moved quickly, identified and located the explicit material, and arrested Mr. Markle in Florida,” FBI Director Kash Patel said.

His arrest comes weeks after authorities in the Philippines said they were investigating allegations that he kept child sexual abuse images at his home while living there. Authorities in the country later said they had recovered thousands of photos featuring “underage male and females.”

Markle, a retired television lighting and photography director, denied the allegations last month, calling them “sick lies.”

A spokesperson for Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, declined to comment on the arrest.

Meghan said in a statement last month that she was “deeply distressed” by the allegations against her father. Their relationship has been limited and fraught in recent years, with her father not attending her wedding to Harry in 2018 amid widespread media scrutiny.

Her statement said that she was previously informed of “disturbing allegations” against him, with British police subsequently confirming she was passed a letter in January 2019 “containing a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom.”

London’s Metropolitan Police force said it had not informed other law enforcement agencies about the allegations in the letter at the time, referring itself to Britain’s policing watchdog over the handling of the allegations.

World.title: ELECTIONS 2026 | EFF blocks coin toss after DA tie
World.content:
EFF supporters on the campaign trail ahead of the 2026 local government elections. The party has demanded a recount after tying with the DA in Buffalo City's Ward 15. Image: Facebook/EFF

The Electoral Commission (IEC) has suspended a planned coin toss in Buffalo City after the Democratic Alliance (DA) and Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) received exactly the same number of votes in the 2026 local government elections.

Both parties secured 1 714 votes in Ward 15, leaving election officials with a deadlock.

However, the EFF objected to the coin toss on Friday, 6 November, and demanded a recount.



EFF demands recount

According to a report, EFF representative Mziyanda Hlekiso urged the IEC to recount the ballots, including spoilt votes, before deciding the ward through a coin toss.

“Can you please stop this toss thing? And go and recount the ballots because this one is not going to help us,” Hlekiso said.

He argued that officials should only consider a coin toss after exhausting other options.

“The toss is the last thing,” he added.

The IEC subsequently suspended the process while it considered the recount request.

According to the election results, the DA and EFF each received 26.5% of the ward vote.



The ANC finished just 22 votes behind with 1 692 votes, while the UDM secured 868.

Ward 15 includes Nompumelelo and Abbotsford.

The Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) in the Buffalo City Metro in the Eastern Cape has objected to a coin toss by the IEC concerning Ward 15. The party is demanding a recount of the votes in the ward. https://t.co/RtZWfVsN2j pic.twitter.com/yqVklfCyv5 — SABC News (@SABCNews) November 6, 2026

ANC loses outright majority in Buffalo City

Meanwhile, the ANC has lost its outright majority in Buffalo City after securing approximately 42% of the vote.

Although the party remains the largest in the Eastern Cape metro, it will need support from other parties to govern.

ANC Eastern Cape chairperson Oscar Mabuyane acknowledged the party’s losses and indicated that it was willing to work with other political parties.

The IEC has not confirmed a final outcome for the disputed ward.

A recount could still determine whether the DA or EFF secures the seat without resorting to a coin toss.

World.title: WATCH | KZN residents ‘bury’ ANC in hilarious funeral stunt
World.content:
KZN residents staged a mock funeral for the ANC, complete with a coffin, funeral hymns and a makeshift burial procession following the 2026 local government elections. Images: TikTok/NewsNexusOfficial

The ANC may still be alive, but some KwaZulu-Natal residents have already held its funeral!

A group of residents staged a mock funeral for the party on Thursday, 5 November, complete with a coffin, funeral hymns and mourners.

The video has since gone viral, drawing laughter and mixed reactions from South Africans.



WATCH: ANC gets a dramatic send-off

The footage, shared by NewsNexusOfficial on TikTok, shows residents carrying a cardboard coffin draped in an ANC flag and decorated with yellow flowers.

A man dressed in pastoral robes leads the procession as the group sings burial hymns.

And the mourners certainly played their part.

After placing the makeshift coffin on the ground, participants drop to their knees, wailing as they pretend to grieve the party’s demise.



ANC takes a knock in KZN

The unusual send-off followed Wednesday’s local government elections, which saw the ANC suffer major losses in KwaZulu-Natal.

Former president Jacob Zuma’s MK Party has made major gains in the province, followed by Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP), thus challenging the ANC in several of its former strongholds.

While the IEC has yet to declare the final national results, some KZN residents clearly aren’t waiting to say their goodbyes.

World.title: Preview of December 2026 SASSA Child Support Grants
World.content:
Beneficiaries of December 2026 SASSA Child Support Grants have a slightly longer wait than usual before their next payout. Due to the unforeseen clash with local government elections in November, pay days were moved around, leading to a longer gap this month …

Therefore, because December 2026 SASSA Child Support Grants next run on Friday 4 December 2026, that represents a 32-day gap between payouts. Whereas last month’s was just 28 days …

DECEMBER 2026 SASSA CHILD SUPPORT GRANTS

Sadly, there’s also no news from the South African Social Security Agency on grant increases. Then again, that’s not so bad, because no other grant got an October top-up either (usually non-childcare grants do). So, the amounts for Child Support and the two other childcare stipends are:



Child Support pays R580 , up by R20 from R560 back in April 2026.

, up by from R560 back in April 2026. SASSA Foster Child pays R1 300 , up by R50 from R1 250 back in April 2026.

, up by from R1 250 back in April 2026. SASSA Care Dependency pays R2 400 up by R80 from R2 320 back in April 2026.

Don’t forget that before you’re eligible for December 2026 SASSA Child Support Grants, you must first register your child with the Department of Home Affairs (DHA). Also note that you cannot use the digital bank system for first-time registering. You have to go to an DHA branch in person.

ELIGIBILITY FOR DECEMBER 2026 SASSA CHILD SUPPORT GRANTS

R18 rand per day. That’s what the R580 Child Support gets recipients heading into December 2026. Image: File

Nevertheless, once you’ve done this, the benefit is there for you. Calculated roughly, to a child’s 18th birthday, a Child Support beneficiary would earn approximately R185 000 (accounting for inflation over the next 18 years). Likewise, applicants shouldn’t forget the income eligibility requirements they must prove:

A single caregiver on Child Support can only earn R5 800 per month.

per month. Married couples looking after a minor, can earn no more than R11 600 per month.

per month. Annually, that is R69 600 (single person) and R139 200 (couple).

Note that there is no asset portion to the means test, like you get with any SASSA Old-Age Grants, for example.

WHAT NEW APPLICANTS REALLY NEED

Here’s what first-time applicants for December 2026 SASSA Child Support Grants need to bring on the day:

Valid identity documents (IDs) and/or birth certificates of you, your child and spouse (if married).

Proof of marital status (marriage, birth or death certificate of your spouse).

Proof of income (you and your spouse).

Certified three-month bank statement, not older than three months.

bank statement, not older than three months. Proof of address (a utility statement with your name on it that’s not more the three-months old).

If you don’t produce all the correct documents and copies, you may be sent away and asked to return. Grant approval used to take three months. However, the agency claims Child Support may be approved on the same day. And if you are denied a SASSA grant, you have three months to lodge an appeal with the DSD HERE.

You can contact SASSA through the following channels for more information:



SASSA Toll-Free Call: 0800 60 10 11

SASSA Head Office: 012 400 2322

Email SASSA: grantenquiries@sassa.gov.za

Visit the SASSA Service portal HERE

But what do you think? Do you think 32 days to wait for December 2026 SASSA Child Support Grants is acceptable? Let us know in the comments section below …

World.title: Ex-Pirates star warns Kaizer Chiefs against signing Tito Maswanganyi
World.content:
Orlando Pirates legend Lebohang Mokoena has explained why Kaizer Chiefs should think twice before considering a move for Patrick ‘Tito’ Maswanganyi.

The 28-year-old currently plays for Bahrain-based Al-Khaldiya SC. Last month, reports emerged suggesting that the midfielder could be on his way out of the club after reportedly falling out of favour with the team.

Maswanganyi has apparently dropped down the pecking order and struggled to secure regular starts. On Wednesday, however, he came on as a second-half substitute as Al-Khaldiya defeated Al-Wahda 2-1.



Chiefs told not to sign Tito

Speaking on SoccerBeat, former Pirates midfielder Mokoena, popularly known as Cheeseboy, explained why he would not recommend Maswanganyi to Chiefs.

“Yes, he’s got the experience, but he’s not the Tito that played under coach Jose Riveiro. For me, if Chiefs want to get a Tito, all I can say is good luck, because our opinions are different. But for me, I wouldn’t go for a player like Tito at Kaizer Chiefs, especially in the current situation and the type of player that he is.

“I think we had some issues at Orlando Pirates where we saw the other side of Tito. Even coach Mandla elaborated and said he’s a different type of human being. You need to sit down with him and try to understand him,” he said.

Mokoena also appeared to question whether Maswanganyi possesses the leadership qualities needed to guide the younger players at Naturena.

With Chiefs looking to strengthen their squad and build a competitive team, Mokoena believes Tito Maswanganyi might not be the right profile of player for the Soweto giants at this stage.

World.title: ZIMRA K9 dog intercepts seven pistols on bus from South Africa
World.content:
Seven pistols and 170 rounds of ammunition have been seized at the Beitbridge Border Post after Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA) officers intercepted a suspicious consignment concealed on a bus travelling from South Africa.

The interception took place in the early hours of Friday, 6 November 2026, during a routine canine inspection at the northbound bus terminal.

According to ZIMRA, the Bulawayo-bound bus was searched at approximately 03:00 when a detector dog named Poncho alerted officers to a suspicious area beneath the first row of passenger seats, directly behind the driver’s seat.



A subsequent physical inspection uncovered two parcels wrapped in black plastic and brown adhesive tape.

The parcels contained seven black pistols and 170 rounds of 9mm blank ammunition.

Driver arrested after Beitbridge discovery

ZIMRA said the bus driver acknowledged receiving the parcels in South Africa for delivery in Bulawayo.



However, he claimed he did not know what the packages contained.

The driver was subsequently taken into police custody as investigations continue.

The seized firearms and ammunition were valued at R21 400, approximately US$1 250.



The consignment was confiscated under Notice of Seizure 047464L, dated 6 November 2026.

ZIMRA warns against smuggling

The revenue authority credited its K9 unit for helping officers detect the concealed consignment, highlighting the importance of detector dogs in combating cross-border smuggling.

“The interception demonstrates the important role of our K9 dogs in combatting smuggling of dangerous goods and other forms of illicit cross-border movement,” ZIMRA said.



The authority also urged travellers and members of the public to comply with customs regulations when transporting goods across Zimbabwe’s borders.

“Members of the public are urged to desist from smuggling and to use designated and authorised ports of entry when importing or exporting goods,” it added.

ZIMRA warned that failing to declare goods constitutes smuggling under Section 182 of the Customs and Excise Act.



Offenders risk prosecution, while goods involved in smuggling activities may be seized.

The authority said it remained committed to protecting national revenue, securing Zimbabwe’s borders against illicit trade and ensuring that imported goods comply with applicable customs laws and regulations.

World.title: Carte Blanche coming up: Psych Ward Horror
World.content:
The Sunday, 08 November episode of Carte Blanche investigates disturbing allegations of abuse and suspicious deaths at a hospital entrusted with caring for some of society’s most vulnerable people.

The programme examines claims that patients who were supposed to be safe were failed, with grieving families alleging mistreatment, neglect and unanswered questions surrounding the deaths of their loved ones.

The investigation seeks to uncover what happened behind the hospital’s doors and whether those responsible for protecting vulnerable patients failed in their duty of care.



Credibility among South African viewers

Carte Blanche is a South African investigative journalism television series that airs on M-Net every Sunday at 19:00.

World.title: MK Party disputes eThekwini election results
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The MK Party is disputing the election results in eThekwini, lodging a formal objection with the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) over the counting and capturing of votes.

The party alleges there were system failures at the eThekwini Results Operations Centre.

It also claims some figures captured electronically do not correspond with results slips signed by party agents at voting stations.

The MK Party is calling on the IEC to audit the disputed results and allow an independent forensic investigation.

It wants the affected results to be placed on hold until all discrepancies have been resolved.

The party is also urging the IEC to delay the final announcement of results until the matter has been addressed.

World.title: 14-day countdown looms for coalition negotiations
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Voters have delivered their verdict at the polls, leaving political parties with the task of finding common ground and working together.

The clock will start ticking once the IEC declares the final election results, setting in motion the process of establishing new municipal administrations.

Coalition researcher Thembelani Mazibuko is urging political parties to use the time available effectively and find ways to fast-track negotiations.

“So from the day of declaring the election, parties have 14 days to elect a speaker. So within those 14 days, political parties need to then talk and engage in terms of forming coalitions within respective metros, as well as obviously districts and municipal councils," Mazibuko said.

"We have seen some reports from the ANC that coalition negotiations will be nationalised, will be centralised at the national level. That is yet to be confirmed, but that may be the most efficient way, given the number of councils that will likely be emanating from these election results.

"And of course, other political parties will talk, especially the big parties, with regard to how to get 50% plus one in their respective councils.”

World.title: Service delivery must be central to coalition agreements, says ATM
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Coalition negotiations are expected to shape the administration of many municipalities following the 2026 Local Government Elections.

Political parties are now weighing up potential partners and the conditions under which they would be willing to work together.

The African Transformation Movement (ATM) says any coalition agreement must include a shared commitment to strengthening municipal capacity and ensuring effective service delivery.

“If we agree on what’s to be done, we can work together. But if there’s no agreement in terms of the work that must be done by the municipality, it won’t work," said ATM leader Vuyo Zungula.

"For instance, we’re very clear on the question of building the capacity of the municipality to deliver services to the people, because on Wednesday, when people were voting, they were voting for exactly that: municipalities that deliver.

"So we can never work with a party that says the delivery of services, that function, must be given to the private sector that is profit-driven. For us, there’s a huge contradiction," he said.

World.title: Elections 2026 | Rise Mzansi sets out coalition conditions
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Coalition negotiations are expected to dominate the political landscape over the coming weeks.

And some parties are already making their conditions clear.

Rise Mzansi is among those setting out what it wants from any potential coalition agreement.

“Coalition agreement must be on service delivery targets, not positions, be made public and in writing," said party leader Songezo Zibi.

"Third is that part of what will make us agree, by the way, it doesn’t have to be an executive role. It must be based on some of the issues we campaign on and aim to deliver for you.”

World.title: Antonelli on top ahead of Norris in second Sao Paulo GP practice
World.content:
SAO PAULO - New world champion Kimi Antonelli topped the times for Mercedes ahead of McLaren's 2025 champion Lando Norris in Friday's second free practice for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old Italian, who clinched the drivers' title by finishing third in Mexico last Sunday, found his rhythm immediately at the Interlagos circuit as he clocked one minute and 10.763 seconds to outpace the 26-year-old Briton by 0.253 seconds.

Four-time champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull was third ahead of Mercedes' George Russell, who faces a five-place grid penalty after taking a new engine, with Oscar Piastri fifth in the second upgraded McLaren.

Seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton was sixth ahead of Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc with Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto eighth ahead of Isack Hadjar in the second Red Bull and Oliver Bearman of Haas.

Antonelli began the session with an early quickest lap in changeable conditions with a gentle drizzle drifting into Interlagos as Hamilton complained that he could not increase his tyre temperatures.

The new champion was clearly revelling in his chance to shine in Brazil, where he has spent time with the family of revered three-time champion Ayrton Senna and was the first driver to go under 1:11 after 30 minutes.

He clocked 1:10.763 to outpace nearest rival Norris, who was fastest in FP1, by two-tenths with Verstappen third ahead of Russell, as the teams completed their low fuel-load runs on soft tyres -- and did not improve again.

The two Ferraris of Hamilton and Leclerc were sixth and seventh, both having been reminded of their duty to put the team first by team chief Fred Vasseur following their first lap clash in Mexico last Sunday.

"They need to respect each other," said Vasseur. "They are two competitors with a fighting spirit, for sure, but they have to respect one another and mainly, and firstly, they must respect the brand, the team, the people working at home and working on the track."

There was no immediate response from either of the drivers before Friday's action with Leclerc returning to his car after missing FP1, having returned to Monaco for the birth of his first child.

World.title: Dutch activists invade site of Microsoft's planned data centre
World.content:
AMSTERDAM - Several hundred activists opposed to the construction of a Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam occupied the site on Friday, responding to a call for a two-day protest across Europe.

The collective Geef Tegengas, which campaigns for climate and justice, and the environmental group Fossielvrij entered the construction site in the Sloterdijk district, halting work for the day.

"It's so many things, so many struggles that come together in this data centre," Geef Tegengas spokesman, Nathan Timmer, told AFP.

"This thing will use as much energy as all of the households in Amsterdam combined... this thing will use a ridiculous amount of water."

Timmer, 30, also argued that the centre would be used "to facilitate AI warfare" and what he called the "genocide" in Gaza.

The activists made it on to the site by scaling barrier fences despite a police presence.

Once inside they shouted political slogans and sprayed anti-Microsoft messages on walls under construction.
