World.title: Israel faces new era of sinking US support after election
World.content:
Jerusalem – Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s brash campaign posters are still up on Israeli public buses — images of him, US President Donald Trump and soaring warjets that laud the two leaders attacking Iran together.

Neither is now advertising the state of the two countries’ alliance.

A week after an inconclusive election for Netanyahu, Americans overwhelmingly rejected Trump and chose a Congress led by Democrats who want a tougher approach to Israel, whether on Iran, Gaza or settler violence in the occupied West Bank.

The back-to-back elections look to many observers like a turning point, with Israel no longer able to take for granted the cover of the world’s most powerful country.

“This is a new era. The confluence of the Gaza war and the war with Iran have really changed how mainstream Americans — not people particularly concerned with the Israeli-Palestinian conflict — see Israel,” said Yael Sternhell, an expert on the United States at Tel Aviv University.

Vice President JD Vance, assessing why his Republicans fared poorly, listed four ways to bring voters back, including ending the Iran war and changing “our relationship with Israel”.

Trump did not disagree. Just as voting was underway Tuesday, Trump said he had agreed with Netanyahu to end the $3.8 billion in annual US military aid to Israel by the end of this year, explicitly tying the decision to the US political mood.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who has served on and off for nearly two decades, had eagerly sought Trump’s endorsement but also acknowledged his country’s growing isolation.

In the final days of the campaign, he suggested Israel turn to cryptocurrencies to circumvent international sanctions he expected would intensify.

Netanyahu has not commented on the US election or Trump’s aid remarks.

Amit Segal, a journalist known for his proximity to Netanyahu, posted that the political situation in the United States marked a “catastrophe” for Israel.

– Can Eisenkot restore the alliance? –

Opposition contender Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to cobble together a coalition to oust Netanyahu, has cast himself as capable of repairing relations.

In an English-language statement, the former military chief said he believed in “liberal values” and also wanted to work “closely and constructively” with Trump.

Yair Golan, the main left-wing leader inside Eisenkot’s bloc, called for Israel to restore a bipartisan approach destroyed by Netanyahu who he said promoted a “destructive Israeli narrative of eternal war and authoritarian rule”.

Netanyahu boasted in his campaign about standing up to Democratic presidents including Barack Obama, who remains a hero for many Democrats. Netanyahu openly aligned with Republicans a decade ago to attack Obama’s diplomacy on Iran.

“Netanyahu certainly rubs Democrats the wrong way and has made every effort to alienate them,” Sternhell said.

“But Eisenkot can’t just be a nicer man to receive a softer approach from this new Congress,” she added. “He’s going to need new policies.”

She said Eisenkot would likely enjoy Israeli public support for cracking down on extremist settlers, who have attacked Palestinians in the West Bank with virtual impunity.

But Israel has shifted to the right, with wide initial support for the Gaza war.

– Broadening criticism of Israel –

The new Congress will include progressive Democrats such as Abdul El-Sayed, the first Muslim elected to the Senate, who describe the devastation in Gaza as genocide, an assertion rejected by Israel.

Netanyahu “made a bet not only on the Republicans but almost personally on Trump”, said Eli Kowaz, senior policy director of the Economic Cooperation Foundation, an Israeli think tank that backs a two-state solution with the Palestinians.

“These results show that bet had an expiry date,” Kowaz said. “Also, for the first time, really, I think there’s a realisation that it isn’t only about the Democrats. It’s a problem with the relationship with America.”

Without US assistance, Israel still has its own major arms industry and retains a clear edge fighting non-state actors such as Hamas and Hezbollah, said Ehud Eilam, a former researcher for the Israeli defence ministry.

But he said Israel would need to rely more on cheaper artillery or non-sophisticated bombs, further increasing risks of civilian casualties that have enraged international opinion.

“Israel can adjust to a new strategic reality of losing much and even all US military aid, but it will be tough for Israel. It will require Israel to consider hard choices such as taking huge loans or raising taxes,” Eilam said.

Kowaz said that Eisenkot, aware of politics in Washington, was trying to show he is interested in regional stability and strategic agreements and not just “an indefinite state of war”.

“He is definitely laying out a different vision for Israel’s relationship with the United States.”

World.title: 'Democratic rights were curtailed but constitutionally': Sonia Gandhi reflects on Emergency
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) Chairperson Sonia Gandhi has accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government of causing significant damage to India's democratic institutions over the past 12 years, expressing confidence that the country's electorate would eventually bring about a return to proper governance.

In an interview with The Hindu, Sonia said the damage extended to the country's democratic fabric and institutions, adding that people were increasingly recognising the consequences of the government's actions.

"Over the last twelve years, great damage has been done to the fabric of our country, our democracy and our institutions," she said.

She expressed optimism about the country's political future, while acknowledging that restoring democratic institutions and governance would require considerable time and effort, even after the present government leaves office.



"Even after this government goes, it will take time to restore our systems to health, and great effort from political parties. People are now beginning to be restless and recognising the damage. But I am optimistic, and I know that the people of India will welcome a return to proper governance," she said.

Sonia Gandhi on the 1975 Emergency

Reflecting on the 1975 Emergency imposed by former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi acknowledged that democratic rights had been curtailed during the 21-month period but said the decision was taken constitutionally.





"It was only after the Emergency that I came to know the true gravity of what had been happening. Yes, democratic rights had been curtailed, and there was a suspension of habeas corpus, but it was done constitutionally," she said.

She also offered her perspective on the circumstances leading to the imposition of the Emergency, referring to violent protests, attacks on government offices and public transport, widespread unrest and calls for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders.

Also read:

"Yet, when I take myself back to that period and try and see it from Mrs Gandhi's (Indira Gandhi) point of view, I see her struggling to cope with the rapidly deteriorating prevailing circumstances: violent protests, government offices and public transport set on fire, widespread organised unrest and even a call for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders," she said.

Sonia further noted that Indira Gandhi eventually recognised the situation, called for general elections in March 1977 and later publicly acknowledged and apologised for the excesses committed during the Emergency.

"Hindsight allows us to put things better in perspective. Let's not forget that it was Mrs Gandhi herself who came to recognise what was happening and called for the March 1977 election. And you know very well that she herself later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency," she said.

Meanwhile, the BJP hit back at Sonia Gandhi over her criticism of the central government, with Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal invoking the 1975 Emergency and questioning her remarks on democracy.

Speaking to reporters in Bikaner, Rajasthan, Meghwal said Gandhi should also recall the period when democratic rights were curtailed, opposition leaders were jailed and journalists were silenced.

"The article makes certain observations regarding democracy. I would like to ask Sonia ji: does she not recall the period of 1975, when democracy was strangled? Thousands of senior leaders from various political parties were thrown into jail, and the voices of journalists were silenced.

She ought to remember that era as well. In contrast, over the last 12 years, PM Modi has nurtured, flourished, and strengthened democracy, proclaiming to the entire world that India is the 'mother of democracy.

' It is Prime Minister Narendra Modi who has emphatically declared that 'India is the mother of democracy,'" he said.

Responding to the opposition's demand for a special parliamentary session, Meghwal said the government was ready for a debate and urged opposition parties to submit a proposal.

He also referred to the Home Minister's remarks at a rally in Haryana, saying Parliament was the appropriate forum for such discussions.

"Our Home Minister provided a fitting response (to Rahul Gandhi) at a rally in Haryana, pointing out that the Constitution-makers designated Parliament as the proper venue for such debates. If the opposition wishes to engage in a discussion, let them put forward a proposal; we can certainly convene a special sessionâthere is no issue with that.

The Prime Minister has also expressed a similar sentiment. As for the suggestion that someone should act as a 'judge'âour democratic system already has a mechanism for this; the Speaker serves as the arbiter.

What is new about this proposal? Why not simply debate? Who is stopping them? They have written requesting a special session; the government is prepared to call one. We are ready for a debate," he said.

Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love'

The Congress leader also spoke about her upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, describing it as an account of how she grew to love her husband and former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's family and India, and how that connection eventually brought her into public life.

In the interview, she said she had long been reluctant to share her personal story but eventually decided to write about the experiences that shaped her life and her decision to enter politics.

"I had no desire to talk about it for so long. But it is not only a love story between the two of us, but it's also the story of how I grew to love Rajiv's family and the country to which they belonged, and then I too came to belong in it. And of how this love brought me into public life, when I saw the purpose of all the sacrifices they had made being threatened, and the party was weakening.

I felt I had to do something," she said.

The memoir traces Sonia's journey from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance with Rajiv Gandhi, which brought her to India, to the personal losses that shaped her life and her relationship with her adopted country. It also recounts her experiences as a member of the Nehru-Gandhi family and her journey from private life to public service.

The book, her first memoir, is scheduled to be launched on November 10.

Rahul Gandhi expresses pride over mother's memoir

Earlier, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi had expressed his excitement over the publication of his mother's memoir, saying he was proud that her personal story would reach readers.

On the 82nd birth anniversary of his father, Rajiv Gandhi, Rahul said he understood how difficult it had been for his mother, who preferred to maintain a private life, to share her experiences publicly.

"I am happy, and so proud, that your story--'Belonging: A Journey of Love'--will finally be read by the millions of people who love you. I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story. Today, on his birthday, I can see Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia," Rahul Gandhi said.

World.title: Two men charged over shooting at Kapil Sharma's restaurant in Canada
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Two men have been arrested and charged in connection with the shooting at comedian Kapil Sharma's restaurant in Surrey, Canada, last year, police said.

The incident took place on October 16, 2025, when shots were fired at the restaurant for the third time since it opened in July that year.

The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) said in a statement on Friday that the two suspects, Pardeep Singh and Saveer Khan, both aged 22, were arrested on November 1. They have also been charged in connection with a separate shooting in Surrey.

Police described both incidents as extortion-related.

Two employees were inside restaurant during shooting

"On October 16, 2025, police responded to a report of shots fired at a cafe in the 8400-block of 120 Street. Although the business was closed at the time, two employees were inside but were not injured," the RCMP said.



The second shooting took place on October 12, when police responded to reports of gunfire at a residence in Surrey. A woman was injured in the incident.

The two suspects were each charged with one count of reckless discharge of a firearm in connection with the October 12 shooting and another count relating to the October 16 incident.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The BC Extortion Task Force took over both investigations after police identified potential links between the incidents, the RCMP said.





Police cite extensive investigation

The RCMP said the charges followed an extensive investigation conducted over the past year.

"These charges are the result of extensive investigative work conducted over the past year, including multiple judicial authorisations, search warrants, and detailed analysis of evidence," Chief Superintendent Duncan Pound, Lower Mainland District Operations Officer and Assistant District Commander, was quoted as saying.

"These charges should serve as another clear message to those involved in extortion-related violence that law enforcement is working collaboratively to ensure public safety," Pound said.

World.title: 'No permanent solution': Congress slams Delhi govt as pollution levels remain severe
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress on Saturday hit out at the Delhi government over the worsening air pollution in the national capital, accusing it of failing to implement a permanent solution and offering excuses instead of taking effective measures.

Delhi Congress president Devendra Yadav alleged that the situation had deteriorated under the present administration, with several monitoring stations recording Air Quality Index (AQI) levels in the 'severe' category.

"Ever since this govt came to power two years ago, all it has done is offer excuses... Today, the situation has gone from 'very poor' to 'severe.' In many places, the AQI has crossed 500, yet this govt has no plan...



Regarding the anti-smog guns, the ones purchased last year aren't even being operated this year; instead, new orders are being placed. There is a long waiting list, and it points to the misuse of fundsâa matter we will discuss in detail.

This govt certainly needs to pay attention," Yadav said.

He also criticised the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), accusing its previous government of failing to take sustained steps to tackle pollution.





Drawing a comparison with the Congress government led by former chief minister Sheila Dikshit, Yadav said measures such as expanding green cover, introducing CNG buses and encouraging the use of LPG had been undertaken during its tenure.

"...I have maintained from the very beginning that this is nothing but making excuses. There is no doubt that the Aam Aadmi Party has failed to provide any permanent solution. During our administration, under Sheila Dikshit, we expanded the green cover, introduced CNG buses, and transitioned people to using LPG.

Throughout the 12 years that the Aam Aadmi Party has been in power, no such concerted effort has been made.

.." he added.

Meanwhile, Delhi continued to grapple with poor air quality on Saturday morning. The city's overall AQI stood at 364 at 8 am, placing it in the 'very poor' category, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data. However, several monitoring stations recorded 'severe' readings, with IIT Delhi reporting 443, Punjabi Bagh 433 and Narela 409.

The development comes a day after the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) invoked Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR as a precautionary measure to prevent further deterioration in air quality.

World.title: SC to NewsClick: Reply to ED plea against HC order quashing ECIR
World.content:
NEW DELHI: After expressing reservations, SC Friday sought news portal NewsClick's response to ED's appeal challenging a Delhi HC order quashing an ECIR under PMLA against the online media outlet purportedly based only on the contentions of the accused while disregarding the unimpeachable evidence produced by ED.

Though a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was not happy with the way the ED indirectly cast aspersions on HC, it asked the portal to file its response within four weeks.

For NewsClick, senior advocate Siddharth Agarwal wondered what exactly the portal would respond to when HC had already quashed the FIR registered by CBI for the predicate offence, based on which the ECIR was lodged by ED.

World.title: ED tracking $1m transfer to 'meddle in domestic affairs'
World.content:
Agency mounts investigation against two foreign entities

NEW DELHI: The

(ED) has initiated an investigation against two foreign entities for their alleged involvement in India's domestic affairs and in connection with a suspicious transfer of $1 million to a UK-based firm having links to India.

ED has identified TCC Digital Markets Ltd, a firm registered in the tax haven of Saint Kitts and Nevis, as the source of funds that reached entities and individuals in India through layered transactions, moving across different jurisdictions, including Germany, Dubai, Lithuania, Canada, St Kitts and the UK.

Dr Matthias Karl Vogt Trust of Germany has been identified as the actual source of the $1 million fund, which was transferred to a UK-based entity through layered transactions before being moved to India.



The German trust had first transferred the funds to XBase Digital UAB (Lithuania) to get around German law, according to a senior official aware of the probe.

Initial probe led the agency to an undated letter from Dr Matthias Vogt, which stated that the payment was made in digital currency.

Intelligence gathered by the agency revealed that digital assets were suspected to have come from 'hawala' (illegal money transfers) to Dubai and to the Lithuanian entity, before they were moved to the UK.





The UK-based firm, recipient of Vogt's money, received $1 million between Feb and March 2026 in its Airwallex (UK) Ltd account. The money passed through multiple layers of different channels and entities, including one registered in Lithuania.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Also read:

It finally took the form of a "grant" from the Saint Kitts and Nevis islands-registered firm, which transferred the funds in two tranches of GB,67,006 and GB,71,746 to the UK firm, before they reached end users in India, sources familiar with the investigation said.

The Caribbean islands are known as a tax haven convenient for laundering proceeds of crime by global economic offenders.

The enforcement agency has come across another transaction by a Canadian-registered entity, ZBase Digital Inc, which had transferred $500,000 in Feb to the same UK firm's Airwallex account. Indian agencies are in the process of verifying these details with the Airwallex. The combined value of the two alleged transactions comes to $1.5 million.

World.title: Creamy layer verdict only for those who challenged government decision, says SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday said its March 2026 verdict quashing Centre's 2004 decision to factor in salary income of PSU and private sector employees for deciding creamy layer status for OBCs would be applicable only to those who had moved the court, while those already appointed and allotted cadre would not be disturbed.

The clarification came following apprehension in many quarters that the March order would affect all subsequent appointments as those denied reservation in the last decades on that calculation would become eligible for fresh entry into the civil services.

In March, SC had held that income of parents could not be the sole criterion to determine whether a candidate fell in the creamy layer for exclusion from OBC reservation and the status and category of parents' job had to be considered along with 'income/wealth test' as an additional criterion of exclusion.



Order won't be ground to reopen appointments already made: SC

The ruling has huge implications for wards of PSU and private sector employees as in their case, parents' income was taken as the sole factor to determine creamy layer status, unlike in the case of govt job employees whose category of job was the deciding factor. As it created uncertainty over the validity of the recruitment process for OBC candidates over the years, Centre sought clarification from Supreme Court, saying its order should not be enforced retrospectively.





The bench said, "The judgement determines the rights of the parties before this court. It holds that the respondent candidates fall within the non-creamy layer of the OBC category and are entitled to the benefit of reservation together with consequential placement and allotment of posts in the selection processes in which they participated. The grant of such benefit shall not, by itself, operate to the detriment of the seniority of any other person or entail the reopening of selections or appointments already concluded.

"

Advocates Shashank Ratnoo and Varun Thakur, who represented the candidates who have been fighting a legal battle for years, said govt has to create supernumerary posts to accommodate their clients who fulfil the requisite eligibility conditions.

The Supreme Court said its judgement shall not, by itself, furnish a ground for reopening selections or appointments already concluded prior to the order and the claims of those asserting that they are similarly placed and whose cases are pending before any court, tribunal or other competent forum or authority, may be considered on their own merits.

"This court expresses no opinion on the merits of such claims, save to reiterate that the interpretation of the 1993 OM and the 2004 letter laid down in the judgement may be taken into consideration while adjudicating such claims in accordance with law," the bench said.

The office memorandum (OM) issued by Centre in 1993 had said the same principle would be applied to employees of PSUs, banks, insurance organisations, universities and similar bodies holding equivalent or comparable posts.

But the "equivalence of posts" as contemplated in the OM was not done and a clarificatory letter was issued by govt in 2004 making 'income/wealth test' the sole criterion for PSUs and private sector employees.

The court, however, had said overemphasis on the 2004 letter to the extent of making income alone determinative without regard to parental status or category of service would defeat the structural framework of exclusion envisaged under the 1993 office memorandum and there could not be different criteria for children of govt employees and the rest.

World.title: SC settles 60-yr Bhakra & Beas dispute between Punjab, Haryana and HP
World.content:
.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: SC Friday approved a cashless settlement chaperoned by attorney general R Venkataramani of a 60-year-old dispute between three states over sharing of electricity generated by Bhakra-Nangal and Beas power projects, and directed Punjab and Haryana to supply 598 million units every year, during Oct-March, to Himachal Pradesh for the next 20 years.Giving effect to a 2011 SC decree in favour of Himachal, the court expressed concern the state had still not received the benefits of a case it filed in 1996, even after 15 years.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "As a matter of abundant concern, we must express in no uncertain terms to all stakeholders concerned that the directions issued by this court are binding and are required to be acted upon without reservation."The expectation of decree, having remained pending for several decades, cannot be rendered fruitless by reason of the unwillingness or recalcitrance of a judgement debtor (Punjab and Haryana)," the bench said, adding that the total energy arrears of approximately 11,973 million units are to be supplied to Himachal over the next 20 years.The court also directed that Himachal's liability towards the project cost be adjusted against its pending power share dues.After the adjustment, its entitlement was fixed at 11,973 million units over 20 years, compared with around 13,000 million units before the deduction.On Sept 27, 2011, SC had decreed the suit in favour of Himachal by ruling, "It is hereby declared that the plaintiff-state is entitled to 7.19% of the power of the composite State of Punjab from the Bhakra-Nangal project with effect from Nov 1, 1966, and from Beas project with effect from the dates of production in Unit I and Unit II." The decree had remained on paper till date.

World.title: Take us to UP in shackles, bulletproof jackets, plead undertrials; court agrees
World.content:
Haryanvi singer and Youtuber Ankit Balyan

NEW DELHI: In an unusual request, two accused in the murder of Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan requested to be handcuffed and shackled during their production before a court in Shamli, expressing apprehension that they could be subjected to a fake encounter by UP Police. The court accepted their plea.In an order dated Nov 3, additional sessions judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler noted that the two undertrial prisoners, Deepak alias Teetar and Yogesh alias Tunda, had themselves requested that the constraints be placed on them during their production before the CJM, Shamli.Allowing their application, the court directed Tihar Jail authorities to ensure the accused are transported to Shamli court and back in handcuffs and leg shackles, while wearing bulletproof jackets. It also directed the jail authorities and DCP, North Avenue (NAV), to provide them "full protection" during the journey and their production before the court, and ensure that "no undue event happens".

World.title: Bus overturns as driver falls asleep, seven injured in Tirupati
World.content:
At least seven passengers were injured after a private bus met with an accident on the National Highway (NH-140) near Ithepalle village in Chandragiri mandal of Tirupati district on the early hours of Saturday (November 7, 2026).

According to the police, the bus belonging to Sri Naveen Travels was proceeding from Bengaluru in neighbouring Karnataka to Bhubaneshwar in Odisha, when it overturned opposite a Bharat Petroleum bunk around 4.30 am.

As per the preliminary information, the driver has reportedly dozed off and applied sudden brake while the bus slipped towards an adjacent canal, which was not clear due to stagnant rainwater on the road.

The injured passengers, including the driver, were admitted into Sri Venkateswara Institute of Medical Sciences (SVIMS) Hospital in Tirupati. The remaining 34 passengers were sent to their destinations in another bus.

World.title: Tamil Nadu govt sanctions ₹198 crore as honorarium for officials involved in 2026 Assembly election
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Government has accorded sanction for the release of ₹198 crore towards payment of honorarium to officials and staff members who worked for the conduct of the 2026 Assembly election across all 234 Assembly constituencies in the State.

A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Public (Elections) Department. Accordingly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to District Election Officers (DEOs), Returning Officers and Assistant Returning Officers of Assembly constituencies, District Revenue Officers (Elections), Personal Assistants (Elections) to Collectors, Special Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations, District Revenue Officers (DROs), Deputy Tahsildars (Elections), Zonal Officers and Liaison Officers for Observers.

Similarly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹30,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officers and staff working in the election wings of the offices of DEOs, DROs, Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations and Municipalities. The same arrangement will apply to members of Flying Squads, Video Surveillance Teams, Video Viewing Teams, Accounting Teams, Model Code of Conduct Teams, Assistant Expenditure Observers, Static Surveillance Teams and Zonal Assistants.

Other categories of staff have also been sanctioned honorarium under various slabs. This honorarium would be paid to the officers and staff members through DEOs concerned, the order said.

World.title: CM Vijay orders ₹2,000-crore allocation to implement Vetri Laptop Scheme for college students
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Saturday (November 7, 2026) ordered the sanctioning of ₹2,000 crore to implement the Vetri Laptop Scheme with the objective to enhance the technological skills of college students.

Also Read | Free laptop scheme: Delhi, Tamil Nadu, UP models and their impact on students

According to an official release, the administrative sanction has been accorded by the State government to implement the scheme, which was announced in the Budget 2026-27, at a cost of ₹ 2,000 crore.

A High-Level Steering Committee, headed by the Chief Minister, will be constituted to monitor the implementation of the scheme. The Electronics Corporation of Tamil Nadu (ELCOT) has been granted administrative sanction to procure laptops and ensure quality control.

Under the scheme, students pursuing first- and second-year undergraduate and diploma courses in government and government-aided colleges during the 2026-2027 academic year will be eligible for laptops. The beneficiaries include students pursuing arts and science, engineering, polytechnic, ITI, medicine, veterinary sciences, fisheries, agriculture and law courses.

In addition, third- and fourth-year students pursuing professional courses in government and government-aided colleges who did not benefit from the laptop scheme during the 2025-26 academic year will also be covered. Considering the technological requirements of engineering students, they will be provided with laptops equipped with Intel Core i5 processors or equivalent specifications, the release added.

World.title: Ex-Keralam Excise Commissioner flags corruption, bribery in report to govt; CPI(M) alleges Minister’s involvement
World.content:
Former Keralam Excise Commissioner Seeram Sambasiva Rao, shortly before being relieved from the post, had submitted a report to the State government alleging corruption and collection of bribes by two senior officials of the Excise Department, officials said on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Mr. Rao, who was serving as Excise Commissioner and Special Secretary in the Electronics and Information Technology Department, was transferred and posted as Special Secretary in the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Development Department.

In the report submitted to the government on Friday, Mr. Rao also mentioned that Excise Minister M. Liju was acquainted with one of the bar owners allegedly involved in the transactions.

According to the report, S. Vinod, who served as Joint Excise Commissioner (JEC), allegedly maintained close links with the owner of a bar in Muvattupuzha and acted as a liaison for the establishment in matters related to its licence.

An informant had alleged that Mr. Vinod demanded a monthly payment of ₹30,000 from the bar owner and had also received ₹50,000 for securing approvals related to bar timings and licence extensions, the report claimed.

The report also flagged allegations against Alappuzha Deputy Commissioner Ajay.

According to the information received by Mr. Rao, the owner of a bar at Kattachira in Kayamkulam was allegedly asked to pay ₹30,000 during the deputy commissioner’s inspection visits, it said.

The report identified the bar owner as Ratheesh and stated that he was known to the Excise Minister.

It also mentioned an alleged payment of ₹20,000 after Onam this year in connection with the renewal of the bar’s licence in April.

Mr. Rao recommended that Mr. Vinod and Mr. Ajay be immediately removed from field postings and transferred to offices such as the Excise Crime Records Bureau or Toddy Board.

Vigilance probe recommended

He also recommended a Vigilance inquiry into the allegations of bribe collection, monthly payments and disproportionate assets against the two officials under relevant provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

The report further called for stricter controls on posting officials facing allegations of financial irregularities to sensitive locations and establishments, and recommended that future transfers and appointments at the JEC, Additional Excise Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner levels be considered based on reports from the Excise Commissioner.

Meanwhile, CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan alleged that the disclosures in the former commissioner’s report pointed to the involvement of the Excise Minister in the alleged corruption in the department.

Speaking to reporters, Mr. Govindan said the circumstances surrounding Mr. Rao’s removal and his subsequent departure from office, reportedly leaving his official vehicle and taking an autorickshaw, indicated his protest against the decision.

Mr. Govindan said Mr. Rao had reported that senior officials in the department were involved in large-scale corruption, including benami transactions and monthly bribe collections, but was unable to transfer them due to pressure.

The former commissioner had named officials allegedly collecting money from bar owners and had also referred to a bar owner known to the minister, Mr. Govindan said.

He alleged that the disclosures raised questions about the Minister’s links with both the officials accused of corruption and the bar owners involved in the alleged payments.

“The Minister must give a clear answer to these allegations,” Mr. Govindan said.

There was no immediate response from Minister Liju and bar owners.

World.title: Qutab Road, Chirag Delhi, IIT Flyover among Delhi’s 10 worst congestion hotspots; 7 p.m. is peak traffic hour
World.content:
Qutab Road, Chirag Delhi and Baratooti Chowk are among the 10 locations contributing to Delhi’s persistent congestion, with commercial activity, roadside parking, freight movement, construction and poorly designed junctions emerging as some of the major reasons behind traffic bottlenecks, according to an analysis by ASTraM (Actionable Intelligence for Sustainable Traffic Management) shared with The Hindu.

Also read | Delhi air ‘very poor’ with AQI reading of 364

Qutab Road recorded the highest congestion among the 10 identified locations, at 59.10 km a day, followed by Chirag Delhi at 42.57 km and Baratooti Chowk at 38.90 km. Lothiyan Marg–Church Road, with 34.44 km, and Kalindi Kunj, with 30.76 km, completed the top five.

The findings point to a problem that extends beyond the sheer volume of vehicles on Delhi’s roads, which is a common concern flagged by traffic officials on ground. At several locations, commercial establishments, wholesale markets, roadside parking, loading and unloading, and encroachments reduce the usable road space. At others, poorly channelled traffic, constrained approaches and conflicting movements at junctions contribute to queues.

Markets, parking and junction design among major culprits

Qutab Road emerged as a persistent congestion hotspot, ranking among the most congested locations in most months. The problem is attributed to high commercial activity, parking, loading and unloading, encroachments and heavy traffic demand. The suggested interventions include designated loading bays, parking and encroachment management, and a review of signal timings.

Chirag Delhi, meanwhile, has witnessed a sharp deterioration. Its daily congestion length increased from around 23.6 km in September 2025 to more than 42 km in September 2026, a rise of nearly 79%. Peak-hour traffic, construction-related disruption and constrained approaches have been identified as the major factors. Signal optimisation, better channelisation and improvements to the junction’s geometry have been recommended.

At Baratooti Chowk, wholesale-market activity, freight movement, roadside parking and encroachments contribute to congestion. Although the location recorded an improvement of around 21% over the previous year, it continues to figure among the worst-affected stretches. Timed freight operations and better parking management have been identified as possible solutions.

Lothiyan Marg–Church Road recorded 34.44 km of daily congestion, with roadside parking and the movement of buses and heavy commercial vehicles contributing to the problem. At Kalindi Kunj, where congestion stood at 30.76 km a day, the convergence of traffic from multiple directions, bottleneck geometry and peak-hour demand were identified as the main concerns.

The remaining locations in the list include IIT Flyover (26.79 km a day), Ajmeri Gate (26.56 km), Bhavbhuti Marg near New Delhi Railway Station (25.57 km), Chatta Rail Junction (24.78 km) and Saraswati Marg–DB Gupta Road (22.53 km).

At IIT Flyover, the bottleneck is linked to the flyover’s approach, institutional traffic and peak-hour demand. Ajmeri Gate and Bhavbhuti Marg face a different set of challenges, with pedestrian movement, railway-station access, auto-rickshaws and e-rickshaws, and passenger pick-up and drop-off activity competing for road space.

Chatta Rail Junction has been flagged for conflicting traffic movements and inadequate junction design, while commercial activity, mixed traffic, parking and encroachments contribute to congestion along Saraswati Marg–DB Gupta Road.

Congestion rises 12.6% over a year, peaks at 3,341 km a day in February

Delhi’s average daily congestion length increased by 12.6% between September 2025 and September 2026, rising from 2,405 km to 2,708 km, according to the monthly assessment.

The AI-driven platform, that monitors more than 250 congestion points, including 62 priority hotspots, found that congestion peaked at 3,341 km a day in February 2026, nearly 39% higher than the September 2025 level, before declining over the following months. The platform was earlier implemented by the Bengaluru traffic police for traffic management and congestion mapping.

Congestion fell to 2,144 km in March and 2,126 km in April, before reaching a low of 1,562 km a day in June. However, the respite was short-lived, with congestion rising again from July onwards to 2,411 km, followed by 2,736 km in August and 2,708 km in September.

The October 2026 assessment subsequently recorded an improvement, with average daily congestion declining by about 8.6% to 2,474.49 km. It recorded a cumulative congestion length of 76,709 km and 161,876 congestion alerts, averaging 5,222 alerts a day, lower than the 5,983 daily alerts recorded in September.

7 p.m. is Delhi’s peak congestion time

Congestion remains relatively low in the early morning, begins rising after 8 a.m. and builds through the day, reaching its peak at around 7 p.m. The hourly congestion length rises to approximately 325 km at the evening peak before falling sharply thereafter.

The pattern suggests that Delhi’s traffic pressure is not confined to the morning office commute. Evening commuter movement coincides with commercial activity, deliveries, freight movement, market traffic and other journeys, placing additional pressure on already constrained roads and junctions.

Daily congestion levels also fluctuate significantly. In October, the recorded daily congestion length ranged from around 621 km on October 2 to 4,489.75 km on October 31, underlining the extent to which traffic conditions can vary from one day to another.

More than half of monitored junctions show improvement

A separate year-on-year comparison of 283 junctions in September 2025 and September 2026 found that 151 had improved. Average weekend congestion per junction declined by nearly 8%, from 1,596 km a day to 1,469 km a day.

However, the overall average congestion per junction increased by 2.33%, from around 1,800 km a day to 1,842 km a day, indicating that improvements at individual locations have not necessarily translated into a reduction across the entire network.

This comes even as Delhi’s vehicle population increased by 7.93% to 87.61 lakh, according to the Economic Survey of Delhi 2025–26.

The analysis points to the need to distinguish between infrastructure and design deficiencies, operational shortcomings and enforcement gaps. The absence of designated loading areas, parking facilities, pedestrian crossings and passenger pick-up and drop-off spaces cannot be addressed through enforcement alone. Similarly, poorly timed signals, inadequate diversions and weak junction management require operational changes.

It recommends a combination of optimised and adaptive traffic signals, coordinated junction management, designated loading and unloading spaces, improved pedestrian facilities, organised auto-rickshaw and e-rickshaw stopping areas, parking regulation and targeted restrictions on freight and heavy vehicles.

The report also stresses the need for coordination among multiple agencies, including the Public Works Department, Municipal Corporation of Delhi, New Delhi Municipal Council, Delhi Metro Rail Corporation and National Highways Authority of India, as several congestion-related issues involve road design, construction, parking and public transport infrastructure.

World.title: OMCs refute Karnataka’s E20 report, seeks additional details about procedure
World.content:
Refuting observations about ethanol blend in petrol being as high as 31% in Karnataka, the three state-owned oil-marketing companies (OMCs) stated the tests were not conducted in accordance with prescribed statutory and technical procedure.

Citing discrepancies with findings from their own quality monitoring, they urged the State government to share the complete counterpart sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports, and details about the adopted testing methodology, and samples for retesting.

“The OMCs remain committed to cooperating with the state government and other competent authorities in conducting joint sampling and testing in accordance with the Control Order and the Marketing Discipline Guidelines, 2024,” it stated, adding, “Any deviation established through the prescribed procedure will be dealt with in accordance with applicable guidelines.”

‘Density reported warrant further examination’

The OMCs raised concerns about the Karnataka Dept of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology’s use of the gas chromatography for evaluating ethanol concentration.

The process broadly entails separating compounds via vaporisation.

According to the OMCs, the certificates cited for the State government’s observations do not specify the applicable standard test method, the procedure for diluting the compounds or the reference material used for correction after vaporisation.

“In the absence of these essential details, the reported ethanol figures of 26-31% cannot be independently validated against the methodology prescribed under IS 17021,” the statement read.

Further, pointing to the Karnataka government’s reported observations, it observed, “Given that ethanol has a higher density than petrol, a higher ethanol proportion would ordinarily be expected to increase the density of the blend. This discrepancy [in Karnataka’s reported samples] further underscores the need for testing through the prescribed methodology and verification against appropriate reference samples.”

Self-monitoring reported average 19.3% ethanol content

The three OMCs put forth that 56 samples from across the State tested by them conformed to the prescribed specifications, reporting ethanol content between at an average 19.3%.

Thus, arguing that the “substantially higher ethanol levels” reported by the State Dept. warrant a “transparent, technically sound and jointly verifiable testing exercise.”

On similar lines, putting forth concerns about the Karnataka State Dept’s observations on 10% mileage loss and the ensuing ₹62,000 crore loss to consumers, it called for a transparent assessment of actual vehicle performance data, material compatibility studies and documented repair costs.

World.title: Andhra Pradesh MPTC, ZPTC election results LIVE: Counting under way across 365 centres amidst high security
World.content:
Counting of votes in 577 Zilla and 7,707 Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies began at 8 a.m. on Saturday (November 7, 2026) amidst tight security. Arrangements for the counting were made at 365 centres.

About 19,885 police officers of various capacities were deployed to ensure security keeping in view the likelihood of violence between cadres of the major political parties and the clashes jeopardising the counting process.

In East Godavari district, Damanthunigidem Panchayat of Devarapalli Mandal, 28-year-old Jana Sena Party MPTC contestant, Garapati Divya, died of cardiac arrest a few hours ahead of counting of votes.

World.title: Delhi air ‘very poor’ with AQI reading of 364
World.content:
The national capital woke up to yet another day of very poor air on Saturday (November 7, 2026) morning, a day before Diwali, which forecasts suggest is likely to impact the air quality further.

Also Read: How is Delhi implementing restrictions to reduce air pollution?

The air quality index (AQI) at 9 a.m. on Saturday (November 7) stood at 364 (very poor), as compared to the 24-hour average AQI of 382 at 4 p.m. on Friday (November 6), according to data from the Central Board of Pollution Control (CPCB).

As per CPCB standards, an AQI of 0-50 is considered 'good', 51-100 'satisfactory', 101-200 'moderate', 201-300 'poor', 301-400 'very poor', and 401-500 'severe'.

Out of the 59 air quality monitoring stations in the city, 18 recorded AQI in the severe category on Saturday (November 7) morning.

According to forecasts by the Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi, the AQI is expected to reach the severe category on Saturday (November 7). Several weather stations saw a slight dip in the minimum temperature.

Safdarjung, representative of the city's weather, recorded a minimum of 16.2 degrees Celsius, 1.9°C below the normal and one degree less than Friday (November 6). According to IMD forecast, mostly clear skies are expected for the next few days.

Up to class 5 in Delhi schools directed to operate in hybrid mode amid worsening pollution

The Delhi Directorate of Education has directed all government and private schools to conduct classes up to class 5 in hybrid mode in view of worsening air quality in the national capital.

The directive, issued Friday (November 7), applies to all government, government-aided and unaided recognised private schools under the Directorate of Education, as well as those run by the NDMC, MCD and Delhi Cantonment Board.

All the government and private schools in Delhi will conduct classes up to class 5 in hybrid mode, allowing students to attend either in person or online, it stated.

According to the circular, the decision was taken in compliance with the Commission for Air Quality Management’s (CAQM) order invoking all actions under Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) with immediate effect across Delhi-NCR.

The CAQM on Friday imposed stage three measures in Delhi-NCR under the GRAP. The city’s AQI is in the “very poor” category on Saturday with a reading of 364, as per CBCP’s Sameer App.

The directorate has also asked school heads to immediately inform parents and guardians about the arrangement.

Deputy Directors of Education (DDEs) across districts and zones have been asked to visit schools under their jurisdiction to ensure that the directions are implemented smoothly.

World.title: Petrol price down by Rs6.59 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs4.25 in fifth straight reduction
World.content:
The government on Friday once again decreased the price of petrol by Rs6.59 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.25, in the fifth consecutive cut in fuel prices.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs346 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs378.

The prices are applicable from Nov 7 (Saturday) to Nov 10 (Tuesday) due to a public holiday on Nov 9, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war
World.content:
Iran said Saturday its military has grown “stronger” since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran’s nuclear programme.

Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the Middle East conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February.

Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the US.

He also said Iran’s forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday.

“Today, the Islamic Republic’s armed forces… having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war,” he said.

“They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence.”

“Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations,” he added.

Reward offered

The US military said it was offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear programme.

The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

In a statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.”

It did not specify what type of information would warrant a $20 million reward.

US President Donald Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran’s nuclear programme.

“If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida.

“If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East.”

Dialogue

The president also said Iran — which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war — is eager to end the conflict.

“We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said.

Trump called Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani on Friday to discuss efforts to end the war.

Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said this week his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.

Early on Saturday, Iran’s Tasnim news agency reported that two missiles had struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, adding there was no official information about any damage.

Iranian state television reported two explosions on the island.

The Iranian army said early Saturday that its air defences had “struck and destroyed” a US drone that was flying over the island, according to state media. It did not say whether the island was attacked.

World.title: Pakistan warns UN against weakening peacekeeping amid budget cuts
World.content:
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan has urged the United Nations not to allow financial constraints and cost-cutting measures to weaken its peacekeeping operations, warning that reductions in resources could undermine the organisation’s ability to maintain international peace and security.

The warning comes as UN peacekeeping faces mounting financial and political pressures. The General Assembly has approved a $5.1 billion budget for peacekeeping operations for 2026-27, about 10 per cent lower than the previous year’s allocation. A funding crisis last year had already forced the organisation to reduce mission expenditure and repatriate a quarter of its uniformed personnel from peacekeeping operations.

Against this backdrop, Pakistan’s Permanent Representative, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, called for reforms that improve the effectiveness of peacekeeping without sacrificing the capabilities needed to carry out its mandates.

“What is needed is the political will in the Security Council to use this important instrument when circumstances require,” he told the Fourth Committee of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly on Friday.

Pakistan is one of the largest and longest-serving contributors to UN peacekeeping. More than 170,000 Pakistani military and police personnel have served in UN missions over the past six decades, with 183 losing their lives. Pakistan also hosts the United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP).

Ambassador Shah’s intervention comes at a time when peacekeeping operations are confronting not only financial difficulties but also increasingly complicated political and security environments. Growing reliance on regional arrangements and ad hoc operations, he argued, demonstrated that the need for a credible UN presence on the ground remained undiminished.

Welcoming the secretary-general’s review of peacekeeping operations, Pakistan outlined six priorities for reform: giving primacy to political solutions; ensuring focused and adequately resourced mandates; preserving the institutional strengths of peacekeeping; preparing for future military and police requirements; improving the safety and security of peacekeepers; and maintaining peacekeeping as a collective UN responsibility.

The central concern was the widening gap between the responsibilities assigned to peacekeeping missions and the resources made available to them.

Pakistan cautioned against allowing financial ceilings to determine operational requirements. Political objectives, Ambassador Shah argued, should first establish what a mission is expected to accomplish. Its mandate should then determine the personnel, equipment and financial resources required.

Peacekeeping missions can help stabilise conflict situations, protect civilians, sustain ceasefires and preserve space for negotiations. But these functions depend on political processes and adequate operational capabilities working together.

Pakistan also urged member states to preserve the distinctive advantages of UN peacekeeping, including its universal legitimacy, predictable financing, established command and logistics systems, and ability to draw personnel and specialised capabilities from across the UN membership.

“Efficiency and cost reduction must therefore strengthen peacekeeping, not hollow out the capabilities that give UN peacekeeping its unique value,” the ambassador said.

The protection of peacekeepers and accountability for crimes committed against them formed another major part of Pakistan’s intervention.

Pakistan, alongside Denmark, played a leading role in advancing UN Security Council Resolution 2823, which was unanimously adopted with a record 153 co-sponsors. The resolution seeks to strengthen accountability for crimes against UN peacekeepers, an issue Pakistan has repeatedly raised at the UN.

Welcoming the secretary-general’s first report on accountability for crimes against peacekeepers, Ambassador Shah also noted the appointment of Assistant Secretary-General Elizabeth Spehar as Senior Focal Point on the matter.

He called for the resolution’s effective implementation through stronger investigations and prosecutions, better tracking of cases and greater support for national capacities to ensure that those responsible for attacks on peacekeepers were brought to justice.

Pakistan also stressed the importance of the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations, known as C-34, describing it as the universal intergovernmental forum for collectively shaping peacekeeping policy.

The consensus achieved within the committee, together with the broad support for Resolution 2823, demonstrated that member states continued to regard peacekeeping as an important instrument of international cooperation.

Pakistan’s position was that reform should make peacekeeping more effective and adaptable to changing circumstances, rather than weaken the institution at a time when international conflicts and political divisions make its role increasingly important.

“Peacekeeping remains a vital, effective and cost-efficient means for ensuring peace and security. We will need this instrument again. We should ensure that it is ready when we do,” Ambassador Shah concluded.

World.title: Australia's Khawaja claims entire team knew about 'Sandpapergate'
World.content:
Usman Khawaja claimed on Saturday that the entire Australian team knew about the 2018 “Sandpapergate” scandal in Cape Town and said they also employed the tactic during the previous Test at Port Elizabeth.

Captain Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were sent home in disgrace and found by a Cricket Australia investigation to be the only three players with prior knowledge of the ball-tampering plot.

Smith was banned for a year and sacked as skipper, Warner was suspended for 12 months and stripped of all leadership roles, while Bancroft was slapped with a nine-month ban.

But former opener Khawaja, who retired this year after 88 Tests, told the Sydney Morning Herald that everyone knew.

“It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us,” he said ahead of the release of his autobiography next week where a chapter is dedicated to the issue.

Bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly in 2021 that they knew about it.

Khawaja said he spoke in the dressing room after the Cape Town Test urging the team to take collective responsibility, rather than scapegoating Warner, Smith and Bancroft.

“In an ideal world, I don’t want to do this,” Khawaja said.

“I don’t want to be the one who comes out and talks about the truth. The issue is that I genuinely thought after eight years the truth would have been out by now.

“Maybe I thought Davey (Warner) would have exposed it, or someone else would have talked about it more. I just didn’t think it was going to come down to this.” Darren Lehmann, who was head coach at the time, denied there was widespread knowledge of the plot, while claiming ball-tampering was once ever-present in international cricket.

“I don’t think everybody would have known,” he told national broadcaster ABC.

“I can’t speak for them (the players) at all. I only know what I know, and I know that ball-tampering was a big part of the game of cricket.

“Now it’s obsolete, but that doesn’t make it right either and we paid a heavy price for that.”

Comfortable

Lehmann, who quit after the series, said Khawaja’s claims dredged up “bad memories” for him, the players and their families.

“For the families and the people involved, I feel for them right now because it’s taking them back to a really bad place,” he said.

“It’s been eight years. You get to a place where you move on, and I’ve moved on with my life.” In the book, according to the newspaper, Khawaja recounts that discussions about ways to rough up the ball were first held in the dressing room during the second Test at Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqeberha.

It culminated in the discovery that sandpaper was effective, and at this point Smith allegedly walked away, saying he did not want to know about it.

Bancroft then allegedly volunteered to use sandpaper in South Africa’s first innings in Gqeberha, where the ball swung significantly.

Cricket Australia said in a statement it was “comfortable” with the findings of its original investigation, but remained open to new evidence.

“There has been a great deal of speculation in the eight years since the 2018 Cape Town Test, including extensive media coverage throughout last month’s series in South Africa,” it said.

“During this time there has been the ongoing opportunity to present any relevant information, and this remains the case.

“All relevant information presented to CA to date has been properly considered and we remain comfortable with the findings of our integrity process. “

World.title: SC calls for scrutiny of illegal power connections
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Friday underlined the need for a microscopic examination of the role of individuals involved in the theft, unauthorised sale and private siphoning of electricity, rather than supplying it through authorised channels.

The observation came from a two-judge SC bench, comprising Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar and Justice Irfan Saadat Khan, which was hearing a bail-cancellation petition in a case where a person suffered an electric shock after a power wire snapped.

In a six-page order, Justice Mazhar emphasised the need for a thorough examination of current practices by Wapda and the concerned utility companies, observing that it was inconceivable that electricity could be supplied without the knowledge of Wapda, or the concerned utility company and its officials.

Petitioner Ali Asghar Khokhar, a resident of Khuhawar Street, Larkana, had filed a criminal petition before the SC seeking cancellation of bail granted to respondent Anwar Ali Kori by the Sindh High Court’s Larkana circuit bench on Oct 20, 2025.

Wonders how ‘unauthorised’ supply rackets run under Wapda officials’ noses

The case stemmed from an incident in March 2024, when Noor Hussain, the petitioner’s brother, suffered an electric shock after a PVC wire broke and came into contact with a high-tension line. Subsequently, an FIR was registered at Rehmatpur police station in Larkana against Anwar Ali Kori and other Wapda officials.

The allegation was that the co-accused, including Wapda officials and the respondent, were supplying electricity to people in their shops by laying a special line from the disposal phase line and running an electric wire over the complainant’s shops.

The complainant, who appeared in person before the SC, argued that the high court had granted bail without examining the facts and the incriminating material collected by the investigating officer (IO).

However, the SC noted that the high court had granted bail to the respondent predominantly on the grounds of a nine-month delay in lodging the FIR, besides the fact that the role attributed to the respondent was one of negligence.

Furthermore, the high court’s order also reflected the IO’s statement that the respondent had no contact with Wapda officials.

Therefore, after considering the relevant factors, the high court had reached the tentative assessment that the allegations levelled in the FIR required further inquiry and accordingly confirmed the bail order, the SC observed. It added that the matter at hand also required further inquiry and that, unless a full-dress trial was conducted, the role and guilt of the accused persons implicated in the case could not be established.

The SC recalled that, when the complainant was asked how he was powering his shop, he said the respondent was working as a contractor in collusion with Wapda officials and supplying electricity to his shop against monetary consideration. He added that he had never been issued a bill by Wapda or any other utility company.

However, after arguing at some length, the complainant himself stated that since the trial was pending, he did not wish to press for cancellation of the respondent’s bail.

The SC observed that the high court’s order granting bail did not require any interference and directed the court office to transmit a copy of the order to the Wapda chairman for information.

Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

World.title: JUI-F decries ‘coordinated campaign’ against Fazl
World.content:
• Slams alleged drone filming of leaders’ homes, character assassination on social media

• Maulana calls for transparency in foreign investment deals

QUETTA / LARKANA: The JUI-F staged protests in different parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Friday, decrying what it called a “coordinated character assassination campaign” against its leader, Maulana Fazlur Rehman.

In Balochistan, protests were held in district headquarters across the province, including Quetta, Khuz­dar, Awaran, Musakhel, Harnai, Lasbela, Qila Saifullah, Ziarat, Nasirabad, Jaffarabad, Chaman, Pishin, Kalat, Mastung and Kohlu.

Party office-bearers, workers, religious scholars, political and social figures participated in the demonstrations, expressing their solidarity with the Maulana.

Addressing the gatherings, speakers praised the Maulana’s role in safeguarding the Constitution, democracy, parliamentary supremacy, religious values and public rights.

They said the alleged aerial surveillance of his private residence through a drone and the subsequent circulation of the footage on social media were unacceptable in any civilised society.

They emphasised that the protection of privacy and the sanctity of one’s home were fundamental rights of every citizen, adding that unjustified interference in anyone’s private life violated moral, legal and constitutional principles.

The speakers said it was deeply regrettable that political differences were being turned into personal vendettas, character assassination, unethical campaigns and violations of personal privacy.

Such actions, they argued, could intensify political tensions and create unrest and resentment in society. In democratic societies, differences of opinion should be addres­sed through dialogue, arguments and constitutional struggle rather than targeting individuals’ private lives or launching negative propaganda campaigns on social media.

They demanded an immediate, transparent and impartial investigation into the alleged drone filming of Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s residence. They called for those responsible, including the individuals allegedly involved behind the scenes, to be identified and dealt with in accordance with the law.

They also condemned the use of social media for character assassination, false allegations and organized negative campaigns instead of promoting political debate and public awareness. They stressed that those involved in such activities must be brought to justice.

Meanwhile, a meeting of JUI-F Sindh leaders expressed concern over the drone filming of the residence of its general secretary Maulana Rashid Mehmood Soomro, the issuance of NAB and FIA notices to Mufti Asad Mahmood, Kamran Murtaza and other leaders, and the sealing of shops in various cities.

Terming them acts of government panic and political vendetta, the gathering insisted that the Maulana and his party were being subjected to vindictive action for raising their voice against the “Form 47 government”, for the unity of the provinces, the NFC Award and the possible 18th Constitutional Amend­ment, and against what they termed conspiracies to seize the provinces’ mineral resources.

They stressed, however, that the party would not be intimidated and would continue its constitutional, legal and democratic struggle. The meeting announced that, on the directive of the party chief and in line with a policy of non-violence, protests would be held on highways and major roads.

Transparency in investments

Meanwhile, addressing a gathering of the Jamiat Talaba Islam in Islamabad, the Maulana called for transparency in agreements with foreign investors, particularly those involving Pakistan’s mineral resources, stressing that the country’s natural wealth should not be exploited through secret arrangements at the expense of its people.

He said his party was not oppo­sed to investment from China, the US or multinational companies, but all agreements must be made public, with clearly defined shares of profits for Pakistan, foreign investors and local communities.

“We are not against anyone’s inv­estment, but there must be transparency in the process and agreements. The nation should be informed about the conditions under which contracts are signed,” he said.

The Maulana also alleged that the government was using security measures in tribal districts to facilitate illegal trade routes.

Referring to recurring curfews in parts of the tribal belt, he questioned why restrictions were im­­posed for two days a week while the remaining five days were apparently considered free of terrorism.
